title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄序
隆慶之四年庚午天下復當
大比士巡按山西監察御史
饒〔仁侃〕兢兢焉懼無以仰稱
上德意謀悉採晉材以佐用事者
乃馳禮幣聘敎諭馬〔躍龍〕謝
〔良壬〕爲考試官曾〔嘉祿〕丁〔用〕
===
〔中〕陳〔時敎〕張〔傳〕譚〔文光〕李〔儒〕
〔賓〕爲同考試官提調則左布
政使李〔逢時〕右叅政羅〔良〕監
試則按察使王〔世貞〕副使李
〔淑〕御史〔仁侃〕寔總其大凡簾
內外百執事靡不加飭乃合
提學副使袁〔階〕所選士二千
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄序

隆慶之四年庚午，天下復當大比士。巡按山西監察御史饒〔仁侃〕兢兢焉，懼無以仰稱上德意，謀悉採晉材以佐用事者。乃馳禮幣，聘敎諭馬〔躍龍〕、謝〔良壬〕爲考試官，曾〔嘉祿〕、丁〔用〕〔中〕、陳〔時敎〕、張〔傳〕、譚〔文光〕、李〔儒〕〔賓〕爲同考試官。提調則左布政使李〔逢時〕、右叅政羅〔良〕；監試則按察使王〔世貞〕、副使李〔淑〕。御史〔仁侃〕寔總其大凡，簾內外百執事靡不加飭。乃合提學副使袁〔階〕所選士二千
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the fourth year of Longqing, gengwu (1570), it was once again time throughout the realm for the triennial examination of scholars. Rao Renkan, Investigating Censor on an inspection tour of Shanxi, conscientiously feared that he might fail to fulfill His Majesty’s benevolent intentions. He planned to seek out all the talent of Jin (Shanxi) to assist those conducting government affairs.

He therefore dispatched ceremonial gifts to invite the school instructors Ma Yuelong and Xie Liangren to serve as Examiners, and Zeng Jialu, Ding Yongzhong, Chen Shijiao, Zhang Chuan, Tan Wenguang, and Li Rubin to serve as Associate Examiners. The Proctors were Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Li Fengshi and Right Provincial Administration Vice Commissioner Luo Liang. Supervision of the examination was entrusted to Surveillance Commissioner Wang Shizhen and Surveillance Vice Commissioner Li Shu. Censor Renkan himself directed the overall arrangements, and every functionary, both inside and outside the examination compound’s screening curtain, received additional admonitions to attend diligently to his duties.

They then assembled the scholars selected by Yuan Jie, Surveillance Vice Commissioner for Education, numbering two thousand …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
有一百人三試之拔其尤得
六十有五人而梓其文之粹
者若干篇以
獻〔躍龍〕獲藉諸大夫以免於蔽
賢之罪又獲以執事序首簡
蓋甞聞人才之生與山河相
爲雄長黄河自北而來混潰
===
洶湧至晉地則下龍門經底
柱轉而東其勢瀠洄翕環若
相翼焉而太行東峙綿亙千
里恒霍中條盤紆崒嵂交錯
糾紛至於崇岡疊阜洪流巨
匯足以標靈而紀地者尤未
可殫述〔躍龍〕之應聘而來也
punctuated:
有一百人，三試之，拔其尤，得六十有五人，而梓其文之粹者若干篇以獻。〔躍龍〕獲藉諸大夫以免於蔽賢之罪，又獲以執事序首簡。
蓋甞聞人才之生，與山河相爲雄長。黄河自北而來，混潰洶湧，至晉地則下龍門，經底柱，轉而東，其勢瀠洄翕環，若相翼焉。而太行東峙，綿亙千里，恒、霍、中條盤紆崒嵂，交錯糾紛。至於崇岡疊阜、洪流巨匯，足以標靈而紀地者，尤未可殫述。〔躍龍〕之應聘而來也，
translation_en:
…and one hundred candidates were examined in three sessions. The most outstanding were selected, yielding sixty-five men, and several of the finest examination essays were printed from woodblocks for presentation. I, Yuelong, have been able, through the assistance of these gentlemen, to escape the blame of overlooking worthy men; and, by virtue of my role in conducting the examination, I have also been permitted to write the preface for its opening leaves.
I have heard that the emergence of talented men and the grandeur of mountains and rivers enhance one another. The Yellow River comes from the north, its turbid waters surging tumultuously. Upon reaching Jin, it descends through Longmen, passes Dizhu, and turns eastward. Its waters eddy and curve around, as though lending their protection. To the east rises the Taihang range, extending for a thousand li. The Heng, Huo, and Zhongtiao mountains wind and tower aloft, their interlocking ridges intricately entwined. As for the lofty ridges and tiered hills, mighty streams and vast confluences that manifest the land’s numinous power and mark its terrain, these are still less possible to recount exhaustively. When I, Yuelong, came in response to the invitation…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
即所經之地頓步徘徊瞻顧
固自以爲平生之大觀歷覽
之極致也昔人所謂表裏山
河天地之奥區者非耶以故
靈粹所鍾篤生聖哲堯舜禹
三聖人肴𢦤都於玆維其時
臯陶稷契益夷夔龍雲從景
===
附百僚師師勵翼亮采至於
德業格天勳澤垂世何其盛
哉春秋秦漢而下雖未可與
唐虞儷然其人率能奮忠亮
節闡猷經用𢦤競武功而雄
視列國𢦤敷正道而羽翼六
經即一才一藝之士亦𢦤極
punctuated: 即所經之地，頓步徘徊瞻顧，固自以爲平生之大觀、歷覽之極致也。昔人所謂表裏山河、天地之奥區者，非耶？以故靈粹所鍾，篤生聖哲，堯舜禹三聖人肴𢦤都於玆。維其時，臯陶稷契益夷夔龍，雲從景附，百僚師師，勵翼亮采，至於德業格天，勳澤垂世，何其盛哉！春秋秦漢而下，雖未可與唐虞儷，然其人率能奮忠亮節，闡猷經用，𢦤競武功而雄視列國，𢦤敷正道而羽翼六經，即一才一藝之士，亦𢦤極
translation_en:
…Along the route I traveled, I paused, lingered, and gazed about me, truly considering this the grandest spectacle of my life and the culmination of all my travels. Was this not what the ancients called a land with mountains and rivers forming its outer and inner defenses, a secluded domain of Heaven and Earth? Thus, where spiritual potency and pure essence gathered, sages and worthies were born in abundance. The three sages, Yao, Shun, and Yu, established their capitals here [?]. In their time, Gao Yao, Ji, Xie, Yi (益), Yi (夷), Kui, and Long followed like clouds and cleaved like shadows. The hundred officials took one another as models, diligently assisted their rulers, and faithfully discharged their duties. Their virtue and achievements reached Heaven, and their meritorious deeds and beneficence endured through the ages. How flourishing it was!
From the Spring and Autumn period through the Qin and Han dynasties and thereafter, although the age could not rival those of Tang and Yu, its people generally exerted themselves in loyalty and displayed lofty integrity, expounding plans and ordering practical affairs. Some distinguished themselves in martial achievements and looked proudly upon the other states; others spread the correct Way and upheld the Six Classics. Even men possessing but a single talent or skill sometimes attained the utmost…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
其所至而擅永世之名焉
皇明龍興巨儒名臣後先相望謂
非山川精醇之所醞不可也
今
聖天子媲德堯舜經文緯武聲教
四訖薄海內外罔不喁喁向
風而三晉之地最近
===
神京光被獨先夫景雲浮則應
龍翔
洽道明則儁乂臻諸士生神明
之墟當
昌隆之會興起之勢固宜與諸
藩不同而〔郡龍〕等得盡觀諸
士之文則見其飫掞醇奧噴
punctuated:
其所至，而擅永世之名焉。
皇明龍興，巨儒名臣後先相望，謂非山川精醇之所醞，不可也。今聖天子媲德堯舜，經文緯武，聲教四訖，薄海內外罔不喁喁向風。而三晉之地最近神京，光被獨先。夫景雲浮，則應龍翔；洽道明，則儁乂臻。諸士生神明之墟，當昌隆之會，興起之勢固宜與諸藩不同。而〔郡龍〕等得盡觀諸士之文，則見其飫掞醇奧，噴
translation_en:
…attained the utmost within their capacities and won enduring renown.
When our illustrious Ming arose like a dragon, great Confucian scholars and eminent ministers appeared in succession. One cannot deny that they were nurtured by the pure essence of these mountains and rivers. Now our sage Son of Heaven matches Yao and Shun in virtue, weaving together civil and military accomplishments. His renown and transforming instruction reach all four quarters; throughout the realm and beyond the seas, all eagerly turn toward his influence. The lands of the Three Jin lie closest to the sacred capital and receive its radiance before all others. When auspicious clouds float above, the responding dragon soars; when the Way of harmonious governance [?] shines clearly, men of outstanding talent arrive. Born in a land of divine spirits and living in an age of flourishing prosperity, these scholars should naturally rise with a momentum unlike that of the other provinces. We, 〔Junlong〕 and his colleagues, have had the opportunity to examine all their writings and have seen how fully they absorb and expound pure and profound learning [?], pouring forth…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
摛英華誦說先王數陳典謨
究然有唐虞氏之遺風焉亦
自辛其所講之不偶也夫河
水九折注海而流不絕者有
崑崙之輸也太行來自三危
積石而後峻極于晉則固咸
有所本矣諸士思所以靖獻
===
以成其信其亦必有所本乎
在定其志審乎義利之辨而
已昔子路曰君子之仕也行
其義也而宋儒則謂無欲之
臣然後可與言王佐此固立
身之標的而臣道之要樞也
夫委質服勞皆臣子職分之
punctuated: 摛英華，誦說先王，數陳典謨，究然有唐虞氏之遺風焉，亦自辛其所講之不偶也。夫河水九折注海而流不絕者，有崑崙之輸也；太行來自三危、積石，而後峻極于晉，則固咸有所本矣。諸士思所以靖獻，以成其信，其亦必有所本乎？在定其志，審乎義利之辨而已。昔子路曰：「君子之仕也，行其義也。」而宋儒則謂無欲之臣，然後可與言王佐。此固立身之標的，而臣道之要樞也。夫委質服勞，皆臣子職分之
translation_en:
…display literary brilliance, recite and expound the teachings of the former kings, and repeatedly set forth their canons and counsels. In them there is indeed [?] something of the surviving spirit of Tang and Yu. We also count ourselves fortunate [?] that what we have discussed is no mere chance encounter [?]. The Yellow River bends nine times before pouring into the sea, yet its flow never ceases because Kunlun supplies it. The Taihang Mountains extend from Sanwei and Jishi before attaining their towering height in Jin: all assuredly have a source. As you gentlemen consider how to offer yourselves devotedly in service and thereby fulfill your good faith, must you not likewise have a foundation? It lies simply in fixing your resolve and carefully discerning the distinction between righteousness and profit.

Zilu once said: “When a gentleman takes office, he practices righteousness.” The Confucian scholars of the Song held that only with a minister free from selfish desires could one discuss assisting a true king. This is indeed the standard for establishing oneself and the essential pivot of the way of a minister. Pledging allegiance and undertaking arduous service are both among the duties of a subject …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
常義之不可逃者遑恤其他
一有計利之心則私矣百爲
從此蹊矣故古之人功業不
可及者皆無所爲而爲者也
諸士進身之始眞樸未漓趨
向未岐要在辨乎此而已志
在乎義則必能因位立忠策
宣猷爲夷險不渝窮達可一
===
疏附禦侮惟
天子使譬之脯腊膎腆以供滋膳
參朮芝桂以防疾疢雖品質
不同要皆可以適諸用是謂
涵泳
大化而有得焉則諸士之令聞嘉
punctuated: 常義之不可逃者，遑恤其他？一有計利之心，則私矣，百爲從此蹊矣。故古之人功業不可及者，皆無所爲而爲者也。諸士進身之始，眞樸未漓，趨向未岐，要在辨乎此而已。志在乎義，則必能因位立忠策，宣猷爲，夷險不渝，窮達可一。疏附禦侮，惟天子使。譬之脯腊膎腆，以供滋膳；參朮芝桂，以防疾疢。雖品質不同，要皆可以適諸用。是謂涵泳大化而有得焉，則諸士之令聞嘉
translation_en: …constant duties that righteousness does not permit one to evade; how could one spare a thought for anything else? Once the thought of calculating personal advantage arises, selfishness enters, and all one's actions follow this path. Thus those men of antiquity whose accomplishments cannot be matched all acted without ulterior motives. You gentlemen, at the beginning of your advancement into office, have not yet lost your native sincerity and simplicity, nor have your aspirations diverged. The essential thing is simply to discern this distinction. If your resolve rests upon righteousness, you will surely be able, each according to his position, to devise loyal policies and carry out worthy undertakings [?], remaining steadfast in ease and danger alike, consistent whether frustrated or successful. Whether winning allegiance or resisting aggression, you will act at the Son of Heaven's command. Consider dried meats and rich viands [?], which supply nourishing meals, or ginseng, atractylodes, numinous fungus, and cinnamon, which ward off illness. Though their qualities differ, all can be put to fitting use. This is what it means to immerse oneself in the great transforming influence and gain something from it. Then your fine reputations and admirable…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
績且將與山河流峙無極無
愧於聖賢之鄉人而主司者
有進賢之慶矣是役也總督
右都御史兼兵部右侍郎王
〔崇古〕巡撫右僉都御史石〔茂華〕巡撫大同右僉都御史方
〔逢時〕咸秉七德以毗翼五敎
===
巡按宣大御史〔燕可〕巡鹽
御史郜〔永春〕行邊御史武〔尚賢〕
貞肅憲度爲祉衍禔模楷督
儲郎中楊〔應茂〕主事姜〔密〕觀
風樂成右布政使周〔世遠〕左
參政張〔崇〕右參政孫〔枝〕楊〔錦〕
鄭〔洛〕右參議黃〔九成〕何〔棐〕崔
punctuated: 績，且將與山河流峙無極，無愧於聖賢之鄉人，而主司者有進賢之慶矣。是役也，總督右都御史兼兵部右侍郎王〔崇古〕、巡撫右僉都御史石〔茂華〕、巡撫大同右僉都御史方〔逢時〕，咸秉七德以毗翼五敎。巡按宣大御史〔燕可〕、巡鹽御史郜〔永春〕、行邊御史武〔尚賢〕，貞肅憲度，爲祉衍禔模楷。督儲郎中楊〔應茂〕、主事姜〔密〕，觀風樂成。右布政使周〔世遠〕、左參政張〔崇〕、右參政孫〔枝〕、楊〔錦〕、鄭〔洛〕、右參議黃〔九成〕、何〔棐〕、崔
translation_en:
…accomplishments will endure without end, like the flowing rivers and standing mountains. These scholars will be worthy of being fellow countrymen of the sages and worthies, and those presiding over the examination will have the joy of having advanced worthy men.

For this examination, Wang Chonggu, Supreme Commander, Right Censor-in-Chief, and concurrently Right Vice Minister of War; Shi Maohua, Grand Coordinator and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief; and Fang Fengshi, Grand Coordinator of Datong and Right Assistant Censor-in-Chief, all upheld the seven martial virtues to support the five moral teachings. Yan Ke, Regional Inspector for Xuanfu and Datong; Gao Yongchun, Salt Inspector; and Wu Shangxian, Censor inspecting the frontier, maintained the integrity and rigor of disciplinary standards, serving as models for bringing blessings and extending well-being [?]. Yang Yingmao, Director supervising grain reserves, and Jiang Mi, Secretary, observed local customs and rejoiced in the accomplishment.

Zhou Shiyuan was Right Provincial Administration Commissioner. Zhang Chong was Left Administration Vice Commissioner. Sun Zhi, Yang Jin, and Zheng Luo were Right Administration Vice Commissioners. Huang Jiucheng, He Fei, and Cui … were Right Administration Assistant Commissioners …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
〔鏞〕按察副使董〔堯封〕廖〔逢節〕
劉〔應箕〕紀〔誠〕紀〔公巡〕朱〔裳〕僉
事孫〔坤〕張〔希稷〕劉〔時秋〕韓〔宰〕
劉〔宗岱〕總兵署都督僉事郭
〔琥〕參將劉〔鳳翔〕署都指揮僉
事王〔元〕洪〔國忠〕胡〔希賢〕飭內
翊外於法咸得書云
直隸廣平府清河縣儒學教
諭馬〔躍龍〕謹序
punctuated:
〔鏞〕、按察副使董〔堯封〕、廖〔逢節〕、劉〔應箕〕、紀〔誠〕、紀〔公巡〕、朱〔裳〕，僉事孫〔坤〕、張〔希稷〕、劉〔時秋〕、韓〔宰〕、劉〔宗岱〕，總兵署都督僉事郭〔琥〕，參將劉〔鳳翔〕，署都指揮僉事王〔元〕、洪〔國忠〕、胡〔希賢〕，飭內翊外，於法咸得書云。
直隸廣平府清河縣儒學教諭馬〔躍龍〕謹序。
translation_en:
…[Cui] Yong; Surveillance Vice Commissioners Dong Yaofeng, Liao Fengjie, Liu Yingji, Ji Cheng, Ji Gongxun, and Zhu Shang; Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Sun Kun, Zhang Xiji, Liu Shiqiu, Han Zai, and Liu Zongdai; Regional Commander Guo Hu, serving as acting Assistant Commissioner-in-chief; Brigade Commander Liu Fengxiang; and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Wang Yuan, Hong Guozhong, and Hu Xixian—all maintained order within and provided support without, and all merit recording according to established standards.
This preface is respectfully composed by Ma Yuelong, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qinghe County, Guangping Prefecture, in the Metropolitan Region.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
隆慶四年山西鄉試
監臨官
巡按山西監察御史饒仁侃〔近剛湖廣崇陽縣人　壬戌進士〕
提調官
山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使李逢時〔化甫直隸德州衛籍江西贛縣人甲辰進士〕
山西等處承宣布政使司右參政羅　良〔處臣江西萬安縣人　癸丑進士〕
監試官
山西等處提刑按察司按察使王世貞〔元美直隸太倉州人　丁未進士〕
山西等處提刑按察司副使李　淑〔師孟湖廣京山縣人　庚戌進士〕
===
考試官
直隸廣平府清河縣儒學教諭馬躍龍〔子進四川璧山縣人　戊午貢士〕
河南彰德府湯陰縣儒學教諭謝良任〔元重廣東番禺縣人　己酉貢士〕
同考試官
河南汝寧府光州商城縣儒學教諭曾嘉祿〔以學湖廣麻城縣人　辛酉貢士〕
直隸徽州府祁門縣儒學教諭丁用中〔師舜廣西灌陽縣人　辛酉貢士〕
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教諭陳時敎〔敬敷四川酌連縣人　辛酉貢士〕
河南懷慶府濟源縣儒學教諭張　惇〔崇謙貴州宣慰司籍江西吉水縣人丁卯貢士〕
山東濟南府濱州蒲臺縣儒學教諭譚文光〔時觀廣西賓州人　辛酉貢士〕
punctuated:
隆慶四年山西鄉試

監臨官
巡按山西監察御史饒仁侃〔近剛，湖廣崇陽縣人，壬戌進士〕。

提調官
山西等處承宣布政使司左布政使李逢時〔化甫，直隸德州衛籍，江西贛縣人，甲辰進士〕。
山西等處承宣布政使司右參政羅　良〔處臣，江西萬安縣人，癸丑進士〕。

監試官
山西等處提刑按察司按察使王世貞〔元美，直隸太倉州人，丁未進士〕。
山西等處提刑按察司副使李　淑〔師孟，湖廣京山縣人，庚戌進士〕。

考試官
直隸廣平府清河縣儒學教諭馬躍龍〔子進，四川璧山縣人，戊午貢士〕。
河南彰德府湯陰縣儒學教諭謝良任〔元重，廣東番禺縣人，己酉貢士〕。

同考試官
河南汝寧府光州商城縣儒學教諭曾嘉祿〔以學，湖廣麻城縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
直隸徽州府祁門縣儒學教諭丁用中〔師舜，廣西灌陽縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
湖廣岳州府華容縣儒學教諭陳時敎〔敬敷，四川酌連縣人，辛酉貢士〕。
河南懷慶府濟源縣儒學教諭張　惇〔崇謙，貴州宣慰司籍，江西吉水縣人，丁卯貢士〕。
山東濟南府濱州蒲臺縣儒學教諭譚文光〔時觀，廣西賓州人，辛酉貢士〕。
translation_en:
Shanxi Provincial Examination, Fourth Year of Longqing (1570)

Supervising Official
Rao Renkan, Regional Inspector of Shanxi and Investigating Censor, had the courtesy name Jingang and was a native of Chongyang County, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the renxu year.

Proctors
Li Fengshi, Left Provincial Administration Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Huafu. He was registered in Dezhou Guard, Zhili, and was a native of Gan County, Jiangxi; he became a metropolitan graduate in the jiachen year.
Luo Liang, Right Administration Vice Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Chuchen and was a native of Wan'an County, Jiangxi. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Examination Overseers
Wang Shizhen, Provincial Surveillance Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Yuanmei and was a native of Taicang Subprefecture, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the dingwei year.
Li Shu, Surveillance Vice Commissioner of Shanxi, had the courtesy name Shimeng and was a native of Jingshan County, Huguang. He became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Examiners
Ma Yuelong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qinghe County, Guangping Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Zijin and was a native of Bishan County, Sichuan. He became a tribute student (gongshi) in the wuwu year.
Xie Liangren, Instructor at the Confucian School of Tangyin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yuanzhong and was a native of Panyu County, Guangdong. He became a tribute student in the jiyou year.

Associate Examiners
Zeng Jialu, Instructor at the Confucian School of Shangcheng County, Guang Subprefecture, Runing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Yixue and was a native of Macheng County, Huguang. He became a tribute student in the xinyou year.
Ding Yongzhong, Instructor at the Confucian School of Qimen County, Huizhou Prefecture, Zhili, had the courtesy name Shishun and was a native of Guanyang County, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the xinyou year.
Chen Shijiao, Instructor at the Confucian School of Huarong County, Yuezhou Prefecture, Huguang, had the courtesy name Jingfu and was a native of Zhuolian County [?], Sichuan. He became a tribute student in the xinyou year.
Zhang Dun, Instructor at the Confucian School of Jiyuan County, Huaiqing Prefecture, Henan, had the courtesy name Chongqian. He was registered under the Guizhou Pacification Commission and was a native of Jishui County, Jiangxi; he became a tribute student in the dingmao year.
Tan Wenguang, Instructor at the Confucian School of Putai County, Bin Subprefecture, Jinan Prefecture, Shandong, had the courtesy name Shiguan and was a native of Bin Subprefecture, Guangxi. He became a tribute student in the xinyou year.

translation_en:
Li Jiabin, Instructor of the Confucian School of Liangxiang County, Shuntian Prefecture, had the courtesy name Kongzhao and was a native of Yang County, Shaanxi. He became a tribute student in the wuwu year.

Officials in Charge of Printing Examination Papers

Shen Jie, Assistant Judicial Officer in the Judicial Office of the Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Weifan and was a native of Deqing County, Zhejiang. He was an Imperial University student.

Wang Yan, Examiner of Records in the Records Office of the Shanxi Provincial Surveillance Commission, had the courtesy name Zijing and was a native of Dezhou, Shandong. He was an Imperial University student.

Officials in Charge of Collecting and Keeping Examination Scripts

Qiao Yingchun, Prefect of Taiyuan, had the courtesy name Renqing. He was registered with the Wuxiang Left Guard, was a native of Anyang County, Henan, and became a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) in the renxu year.

Lü Mingke, Prefect of Pingyang, had the courtesy name Shengfu. He was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a native of Lishui County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the jiwei year.

Wang Gongyong, Prefect of Lu’an, had the courtesy name Jinchen and was a native of Cheng’an County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the guichou year.

Lu Jian, Associate Salt Distribution Commissioner of the Hedong–Shaanxi Salt Distribution Commission, had the courtesy name Daohan. He was registered in Xiangfu County, Henan, was a native of Jinhua County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the gengxu year.

Officials in Charge of Receiving Examination Scripts

Yang Song, Record Keeper in the Records Office of the Shanxi Provincial Administration Commission, had the courtesy name Weiqiao. He was registered with the Henan Guard in Henan, was a native of Haining County, Zhejiang, and became a metropolitan graduate in the yichou year.

Wang Haoxue, Vice Prefect of Taiyuan, had the courtesy name Daoqing and was a native of Laoting County, Zhili. He became a tribute student in the gengzi year.

Liu Lu, Prefectural Judge of Pingyang, had the courtesy name Xizeng and was a native of Anyang County, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Lei Dazhuang, Magistrate of Xinzhou in Taiyuan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Qinfu and was a native of Shangcai County, Henan. He became a metropolitan graduate in the renxu year.

Gu Xianren, Magistrate of Zezhou, had the courtesy name Yuanbo and was a native of Wujin County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Yuan Kui, Magistrate of Yangqu County, Taiyuan Prefecture, had the courtesy name Ziji and was a native of Cheng’an County, Zhili. He became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Chen Wanyan, Magistrate of Linfen County, Pingyang Prefecture, had the courtesy name Rujia. He was registered with the Embroidered-uniform Guard, was a native of Wanping County, Shuntian Prefecture, and became a metropolitan graduate in the wuchen year.

Zhou Shi, Magistrate of Qinshui County, Zezhou, had the courtesy name Yizheng and was a native of Gushi County, Henan. He became a tribute student in the wuwu year.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
好仁者無以尚之
時使薄斂所以勸百姓也
子路人告之以有過則喜禹聞善言則拜
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取
於人以為善
易
龍德而正中者也
===
象曰告公從以益志也
祐者助也天之所助者順也人之所助者
信也
復德之本也
書
明四目達四聰
后從諫則聖后克聖臣不命其承疇敢不
祇若王之休命
王省惟歲卿士惟月師尹惟日歲月日時
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

好仁者，無以尚之。

時使薄斂，所以勸百姓也。

子路，人告之以有過則喜；禹聞善言則拜。大舜有大焉：善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以為善。

易

龍德而正中者也。

象曰：「告公從，以益志也。」

祐者，助也。天之所助者，順也；人之所助者，信也。

復，德之本也。

書

明四目，達四聰。

后從諫則聖。

后克聖，臣不命其承，疇敢不祇若王之休命？

王省惟歲，卿士惟月，師尹惟日。歲月日時
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Nothing can surpass one who loves benevolence.

Employing the people at the proper seasons and taxing them lightly are the means of encouraging the common people.

When someone told Zilu that he had a fault, he rejoiced; when Yu heard good words, he bowed. The great Shun had something greater still: he shared with others in doing good, set aside his own views to follow others, and delighted in drawing upon others to do good.

Book of Changes

He possesses the virtue of the dragon and is correctly placed in the center.

The Commentary on the Images says: “Announcing it to the duke and being followed serves to advance one's purpose.”

To bless means to assist. Those whom Heaven assists are compliant; those whom people assist are trustworthy.

Return is the root of virtue.

Book of Documents

Make clear the sight of the four quarters; open channels for hearing from the four quarters.

A ruler who follows remonstrance becomes a sage.

If the ruler can become a sage, his ministers will carry out his will without being commanded. Who would dare not reverently obey the king's excellent command?

The king examines the year; the ministers, the month; the heads of offices, the day. The years, months, days, and seasons …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
無易百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用
平康
厥惟艱哉思其艱以圖其易民乃寧
詩
素絲祝之良馬六之
春日遲遲卉木萋萋倉庚喈喈采蘩祁祁
執訊獲醜薄言還歸
赫赫業業有嚴天子
受小球大球爲下國綴旒何天之休不競
不絿不剛不柔敷政優優百祿是遒受
小共大共爲下國駿厖何天之龍敷奏
其勇不震不動不戁不竦百祿是總
===
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊公十三年〕
夏公追戎于濟西〔莊公十八年〕齊人侵我
西鄙公追齊師至酅弗及〔僖公二十六年〕
punctuated:
無易，百穀用成，乂用明，俊民用章，家用平康。
厥惟艱哉！思其艱，以圖其易，民乃寧。

詩
素絲祝之，良馬六之。
春日遲遲，卉木萋萋，倉庚喈喈，采蘩祁祁。
執訊獲醜，薄言還歸。
赫赫業業，有嚴天子。
受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。不競不絿，不剛不柔，敷政優優，百祿是遒。受小共大共，爲下國駿厖，何天之龍。敷奏其勇，不震不動，不戁不竦，百祿是總。

春秋
春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。〔莊公十三年〕
夏，公追戎于濟西。〔莊公十八年〕齊人侵我西鄙，公追齊師至酅，弗及。〔僖公二十六年〕
translation_en:
…are not disrupted, the hundred grains thereby ripen, government is thereby enlightened, men of outstanding ability thereby become manifest, and households thereby enjoy peace and well-being.
How difficult it is! Consider its difficulties in order to devise ways of making it easy; then the people will be at peace.

Book of Odes
Bind them with plain silk; provide six fine horses.
The spring days lengthen; plants and trees grow luxuriantly. Orioles sing harmoniously; those gathering white southernwood come in throngs.
Taking prisoners for interrogation and capturing the enemy host, we return home.
Illustrious and awe-inspiring, majestic is the Son of Heaven.
He receives the small and great jade balls and serves as the binding cord of the states below, bearing Heaven’s blessings. Neither contentious nor impetuous, neither harsh nor yielding, he administers government with generous ease, and all blessings converge upon him. He receives the small and great jades of tribute and serves as the mighty support of the states below, bearing Heaven’s favor. He displays and brings into action his courage, neither shaken nor swayed, neither fearful nor alarmed; all blessings gather upon him.

Spring and Autumn Annals
In spring, the Marquis of Qi and men of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing. 〔Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕
In summer, the duke pursued the Rong west of the Ji River. 〔Eighteenth year of Duke Zhuang.〕 Men of Qi invaded our western borderlands. The duke pursued the army of Qi as far as Xi but did not catch up with it. 〔Twenty-sixth year of Duke Xi.〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
晉人執季孫意如以歸〔昭公十三年春意〕
〔如至自晉昭公十四年〕
入月己酉入邾以邾子益來〔哀公七年夏〕
〔齊人取讙及闡歸邾子益于邾〕齊人
〔歸讙及闡俱哀公八年〕
禮記
以三十年之通制國用量入以爲出
君子如欲化民成俗其必由學乎
樂極和禮極順內和而外順則民瞻其顔
色而弗與爭也望其容貌而民不生易
慢焉故德煇動於內而民莫不承聽理
發諸外而民莫不承順
君子不盡利以遺民
===
第貳場
論
人臣尊君之大
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔〔文帝二年〕
punctuated:
晉人執季孫意如以歸。〔昭公十三年。春，意〕〔如至自晉。昭公十四年。〕
入月己酉，入邾，以邾子益來。〔哀公七年。夏，〕〔齊人取讙及闡。歸邾子益于邾。〕齊人〔歸讙及闡。俱哀公八年。〕
禮記
以三十年之通制國用，量入以爲出。
君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎！
樂極和，禮極順。內和而外順，則民瞻其顔色而弗與爭也；望其容貌，而民不生易慢焉。故德煇動於內，而民莫不承聽；理發諸外，而民莫不承順。
君子不盡利以遺民。
第貳場
論
人臣尊君之大。
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢賜天下今年田租之半詔。〔文帝二年〕
translation_en:
The men of Jin seized Jisun Yiru and took him back with them. 〔Duke Zhao, year 13. “In spring, Yiru returned from Jin,” Duke Zhao, year 14.〕

In the [eighth?] month, on the jiyou day, our forces entered Zhu and brought back Yi, Viscount of Zhu. 〔Duke Ai, year 7. “In summer, the men of Qi took Huan and Chan.” “Yi, Viscount of Zhu, was returned to Zhu.”〕 The men of Qi 〔returned Huan and Chan. These entries are all from Duke Ai, year 8.〕

Book of Rites

Regulate state expenditure on the basis of a thirty-year accounting, determining expenditure according to revenue.

If the gentleman wishes to transform the people and establish good customs, must he not proceed through education?

Music brings harmony to its utmost; ritual brings conformity to its utmost. When one is harmonious within and compliant without, the people look upon one's countenance and do not contend with one; they observe one's bearing and develop no disrespect or arrogance. Thus, when the radiance of virtue stirs within, none among the people fails to heed it; when order manifests itself outwardly, none fails to comply.

The gentleman does not take all the profit, but leaves some for the people.

Second Session

Discourse

The great importance of a minister's honoring his ruler.

Edicts, Patents, and Memorials 〔One question from among these categories [?].〕

Compose an edict in the manner of the Han dynasty granting the realm remission of half this year's land tax. 〔Emperor Wen, year 2.〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕
擬宋開天章閣召輔臣條對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
判語〔五條〕
官吏給由
功臣田土
上書陳言
盤詰姦細
辯明冤枉
===
第叁場
策〔五道〕
問太子天下本學士大夫類能言之而莫
詳於賈誼其說果盡出於誼否也三代
而下不能蚤豫教故其治不古若亦可
聞其略否夫論予道者則有溫嶠之侍
臣王褒之太子二箴亦君道者則有唐
文皇之帝範十二至我
punctuated:
擬唐加左僕射房玄齡太子少師誥〔貞觀十三年〕。
擬宋開天章閣召輔臣條對謝表〔慶曆三年〕。
判語〔五條〕：官吏給由；功臣田土；上書陳言；盤詰姦細；辯明冤枉。
===
第叁場。
策〔五道〕。
問：太子，天下本，學士大夫類能言之，而莫詳於賈誼。其說果盡出於誼否也？三代而下，不能蚤豫教，故其治不古若，亦可聞其略否？夫論予道者，則有溫嶠之《侍臣》、王褒之《太子》二箴；亦君道者，則有唐文皇之《帝範》十二。至我
translation_en:
Draft an investiture proclamation in the manner of the Tang dynasty conferring on Fang Xuanling, Vice Director of the Left, the additional title of Junior Preceptor of the Heir Apparent. 〔Thirteenth year of Zhenguan.〕
Draft a memorial of thanks in the manner of the Song dynasty for opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning the chief ministers to submit responses item by item. 〔Third year of Qingli.〕
Legal judgments 〔five topics〕: issuing service certificates to officials and clerks; lands of meritorious officials; submitting written statements to the throne; interrogating suspicious persons and spies; investigating and clearing wrongful accusations.

Third Session
Policy questions 〔five questions〕
Question: The heir apparent is the foundation of the realm. Scholars and officials can generally discuss this, but none has treated it more fully than Jia Yi. Did these teachings indeed all originate with Jia Yi? Since the Three Dynasties, rulers have failed to provide instruction early and in advance, and consequently their governance has fallen short of antiquity. May we also hear an outline of this matter? On the way of the son [?], there are the two admonitions: Wen Jiao’s Admonition to Attendant Officials and Wang Bao’s Admonition to the Heir Apparent. On the ruler’s way [?], there are the twelve chapters of the Tang Emperor Wen’s Model for Emperors (Difan). Coming to our …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
太祖高皇帝及
成祖
宣
憲諸廟皆勑成一書以示
皇太子其旨與帝範同與異否
今上之元年即
詔立元良以定
國本天下欣然謂吾
君有子矣夫出閣之期已示而所以輔導匡翼
===
之具未悉諸生其爲我詳言之庶幾備
承華寶鑑之一二云
問孔子刪述六經垂訓萬世葢昭昭如日
焉自楊雄王通氏始竊法言中說以擬
論語而雄復著太玄以準易通續六經
君子非之以爲僭然宋之諸儒亦有太
極圖通書定性皇極西銘等篇彼盡黜
漢儒而自精醇其語寧無意於續也然
易繫有非夫子所撰者乾坤多餘章而
punctuated:
太祖高皇帝及成祖、宣、憲諸廟，皆勑成一書以示皇太子，其旨與《帝範》同與異否？今上之元年，即詔立元良，以定國本。天下欣然謂：「吾君有子矣！」夫出閣之期已示，而所以輔導匡翼之具未悉。諸生其爲我詳言之，庶幾備《承華寶鑑》之一二云。
問：孔子刪述六經，垂訓萬世，葢昭昭如日焉。自楊雄、王通氏始，竊《法言》《中說》以擬《論語》，而雄復著《太玄》以準《易》，通續六經，君子非之，以爲僭。然宋之諸儒亦有《太極圖》《通書》《定性》《皇極》《西銘》等篇。彼盡黜漢儒而自精醇其語，寧無意於續也？然《易繫》有非夫子所撰者，乾坤多餘章，而
translation_en:
… Emperor Taizu Gao, Chengzu, and the emperors known by the temple names Xuanzong and Xianzong each commanded the compilation of a book to instruct the heir apparent. Were their purposes the same as, or different from, those of the Model for Emperors (Di fan)? In the first year of the present emperor’s reign, he issued an edict establishing the heir apparent, thereby securing the foundation of the state. All under Heaven rejoiced, saying, “Our sovereign has a son!” The date when the heir apparent is to leave the inner palace to begin his formal education has already been announced, but the arrangements for assisting, guiding, correcting, and supporting him are not yet fully known. You candidates should explain these matters to me in detail, so that your answers may supply something toward a Precious Mirror for the Heir Apparent (Chenghua baojian).
Question: Confucius edited and transmitted the Six Classics, leaving instruction for ten thousand generations, as luminous as the sun. Beginning with Yang Xiong and Wang Tong, men presumptuously used such works as Model Sayings (Fa yan) and Discussions of the Mean (Zhong shuo) to imitate the Analects. Yang Xiong also wrote the Supreme Mystery (Tai xuan) to match the Changes, while Wang Tong continued the Six Classics. Gentlemen condemned them for overstepping their proper bounds. Yet the Confucian scholars of the Song likewise produced such works as the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taiji tu), the Comprehensive Writings (Tong shu), Stabilizing the Nature (Ding xing), the Supreme Pole (Huang ji), and the Western Inscription (Xi ming). They rejected the Han scholars wholesale and regarded their own words as refined and pure; could they have had no intention of continuing the Classics? Yet the Appended Statements to the Changes contain passages not written by the Master, and the sections on Qian and Kun contain many superfluous passages, while …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
毛詩雜淫風周禮缺冬官而大學缺格
致禮記雜出漢儒之手春秋如公穀各
泥其師說訖未有定不知雄通輩何以
不敢討定而敢於續也今論者往往有
異議如謂冬官格致本不缺大學周易
有古本之類其說可盡舉而折衷之否
問
太廟之時饗也與文廟之釋奠也蓋皆有從祀
焉豈亦出於報功崇道之意歟其禮始
何代而損益何主大較可得聞否
===
國家於典禮至明備也
先帝蓋惓惓致意焉今
太廟從祀之臣自
成祖而後寥寥矣不聞有議增入者文廟之兩
廡自元季而後寥寥矣間有議增入訖
於今未定者抑果難其人耶或慎重其
典不輕舉耶
國家熙明累洽之運以崇德右文稱而使
punctuated:
毛詩雜淫風，周禮缺冬官，而大學缺格致，禮記雜出漢儒之手，春秋如公穀各泥其師說，訖未有定。不知雄通輩何以不敢討定而敢於續也？今論者往往有異議，如謂冬官、格致本不缺，大學、周易有古本之類，其說可盡舉而折衷之否？
問：太廟之時饗也，與文廟之釋奠也，蓋皆有從祀焉，豈亦出於報功崇道之意歟？其禮始何代，而損益何主？大較可得聞否？國家於典禮至明備也，先帝蓋惓惓致意焉。今太廟從祀之臣，自成祖而後寥寥矣，不聞有議增入者；文廟之兩廡，自元季而後寥寥矣，間有議增入，訖於今未定者。抑果難其人耶？或慎重其典，不輕舉耶？國家熙明累洽之運，以崇德右文稱，而使
translation_en:
…the Mao recension of the Book of Odes contains licentious Airs; the Rites of Zhou lacks the Offices of Winter; the Great Learning lacks the section on investigating things and extending knowledge; the Record of Rites derives variously from the hands of Han scholars; and, among commentaries on the Spring and Autumn Annals, those of Gongyang and Guliang each cling to their own teachers’ interpretations, with no definitive settlement ever reached. Why did men such as Yang Xiong and Wang Tong dare to compose continuations but not to examine and establish these texts? Scholars today often advance divergent views—for instance, that the Offices of Winter and the section on investigating things and extending knowledge were never missing, or that ancient versions of the Great Learning and the Changes of Zhou exist. Can you enumerate these views fully and adjudicate among them?
Question: At the seasonal sacrifices in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and the presentation of offerings in the Confucian Temple, others are also enshrined to receive accompanying sacrifices. Does this, too, arise from the intention to reward merit and honor the Way? In which dynasty did this rite begin, and under which rulers was it modified? May we hear its broad outlines? Our dynasty’s ceremonial institutions are exceedingly clear and complete; the late emperor devoted unremitting attention to them. Yet few ministers from the reign of Chengzu onward receive accompanying sacrifices in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and we hear of no proposals to add any. In the two side cloisters of the Confucian Temple, few figures from the end of the Yuan onward are enshrined. Proposals to add some have occasionally been made, but remain unsettled to this day. Is it truly difficult to find suitable men? Or is this institution treated with such circumspection that action is not taken lightly? In an era when our dynasty has enjoyed successive reigns of flourishing, enlightened government and pervasive harmony, renowned for honoring virtue and esteeming letters, yet allows…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
列聖無臣孔門無賢誰怳不取也諸士子熟琬
琰之編且習俎豆久矣其毋曰鄒人之
子不知而不以告也
問太史公有云天下熙熙皆爲利來固聖
門罕言之然大學稱理財冢宰制國用
豈非以當世所急也耶卽不敢與諸儒
生爲雜言夫齊越蕞爾國耳管夷吾計
然爲之謀而卒以富役天下桑弘羊一
賈人子然當漢疲耗之極而營之使大
===
農有奇羨劉晏幹吏也以區區十五道
之賦而供度支不乏果何筴也今天下
雖號全盛然中外恒枵然若果然之腹
不能以月計大司農時時告不支矣豈
其源尚有可闢而其流或有可塞歟願
與諸生商之以觀有用之學且上主計
者采焉
問夷狄之爲中國患也久矣邇者葢益訌
焉以戰則多餒以守則多瑕孳孳然聚
punctuated:
列聖無臣，孔門無賢，誰怳不取也？諸士子熟琬琰之編，且習俎豆久矣，其毋曰鄒人之子不知，而不以告也。

問：太史公有云：「天下熙熙，皆爲利來。」固聖門罕言之，然大學稱理財，冢宰制國用，豈非以當世所急也耶？卽不敢與諸儒生爲雜言。夫齊越蕞爾國耳，管夷吾、計然爲之謀，而卒以富役天下。桑弘羊，一賈人子，然當漢疲耗之極，而營之，使大農有奇羨。劉晏，幹吏也，以區區十五道之賦，而供度支不乏，果何筴也？今天下雖號全盛，然中外恒枵然，若果然之腹，不能以月計，大司農時時告不支矣。豈其源尚有可闢，而其流或有可塞歟？願與諸生商之，以觀有用之學，且上主計者采焉。

問：夷狄之爲中國患也久矣，邇者葢益訌焉。以戰則多餒，以守則多瑕，孳孳然聚
translation_en:
…the successive sage emperors appear to have no worthy ministers, and the school of Confucius no worthy followers—who would not find this unacceptable [?]? You candidates are familiar with the volumes recording illustrious deeds and have long been versed in sacrificial rites. Do not say that the son of the man of Zou does not know, and therefore fail to inform him.

Question: The Grand Historian said, “All the world bustles joyfully, all coming for profit.” Admittedly, this was seldom discussed in the school of the Sage. Yet the Great Learning speaks of managing wealth, and the Minister of State regulated state expenditure. Was this not because these were urgent concerns of their times? I would nevertheless not venture to offer you Confucian students indiscriminate remarks on the subject. Qi and Yue were merely tiny states; yet Guan Yiwu and Ji Ran devised plans for them, and ultimately their wealth enabled them to command all under Heaven. Sang Hongyang was a merchant’s son, yet, at a time when the Han was utterly exhausted and depleted, his management left the Minister of Agriculture with a surplus. Liu Yan was an able official: with the revenues of a mere fifteen circuits, he met state expenditures without shortfall. What methods did they actually employ? Today, although the realm is said to enjoy complete prosperity, the central and regional treasuries are constantly hollow, like the belly of a guoran monkey; they cannot make provision even a month ahead, and the Minister of Revenue repeatedly reports that funds are insufficient. Might there still be sources of revenue that could be opened, and outflows that could be stopped? I wish to discuss this with you students, to assess your practically useful learning and also to submit your proposals for those responsible for fiscal affairs to draw upon.

Question: The peoples beyond our borders have long been a source of trouble for China, and recently the disturbances have apparently grown worse. In battle we are often disheartened; in defense we have many weaknesses. Diligently gathering…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
天下之策而日講求之而卒不得其要
領夫我之所以不敵者其故何也虜雖
強其視匈奴突厥女直蒙古孰類今縉
紳之士或議戰而介胄之士或更議守
要必有折衷者
明威德薄海內外今縱不能犁其庭禽若上而
勒石於燕然之巔門郊多壘師何策以
洗其恥乎諸士子之鄉中虜數矣其必
有習者明以語我
punctuated:
天下之策，而日講求之，而卒不得其要領。夫我之所以不敵者，其故何也？虜雖強，其視匈奴、突厥、女直、蒙古孰類？今縉紳之士或議戰，而介胄之士或更議守，要必有折衷者。
明威德薄海內外，今縱不能犁其庭、禽若上，而勒石於燕然之巔，門郊多壘，師何策以洗其恥乎？諸士子之鄉中虜數矣，其必有習者，明以語我。
translation_en:
…the strategies of all under Heaven, discussing and investigating them daily, yet ultimately failing to grasp their essentials. What accounts for our inability to match the enemy? Though these raiders are strong, how do they compare with the Xiongnu, the Tujue, the Jurchens, and the Mongols? Some among the scholar-officials now advocate battle, while some among the men in armor instead advocate defense. Surely there must be a sound judgment between these positions.
The Ming’s awe-inspiring power and virtue extend throughout the realm and beyond the seas. Even if we cannot now plow up their encampments, capture their ruler [?], and engrave a stone commemorating victory atop Mount Yanran, enemy ramparts crowd our very outskirts: by what strategy can our armies wipe away this humiliation? Your native districts, gentlemen, have repeatedly suffered incursions by these raiders. Surely some of you know these matters well; explain them clearly to me.

translation_en:
Sixty-five successful provincial graduates (juren).

Second place: Lang Jin, a student at the Lan County school. His examination classic was the Book of Changes.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
好仁者無以尚之
馮懋仁
同考試官教諭丁　批〔其得無以尚之之旨且精醇併〕
雅錄之
考試官教諭謝　批〔精確明透是究心理學者〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔體認親切措詞平實〕
聖人揭言好仁者之心一於仁而已矣夫好而
===
猶有可尚非好之一也一則心純乎仁矣其斯
爲好仁者乎此成德之事夫子所以歎其未見
也若曰仁者天下之公理好仁者天下之公心
宜好仁者之多見也而吾以爲未見者何哉亦
以好仁者之未可易言耳蓋其眞知仁爲天命
之降衷而好爵之靡根於由衷而不可奪眞知
仁爲人心之秉彝而懿德之好出於天眞而不
可易物之感人無窮非一無可好也以仁視之
皆無益於吾心者也吾惟知好吾心之仁而已
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

好仁者，無以尚之。

馮懋仁

同考試官教諭丁批：〔其得「無以尚之」之旨，且精醇併〕雅，錄之。
考試官教諭謝批：〔精確明透，是究心理學者。〕
考試官教諭馬批：〔體認親切，措詞平實。〕

聖人揭言好仁者之心，一於仁而已矣。夫好而猶有可尚，非好之一也；一則心純乎仁矣，其斯爲好仁者乎！此成德之事，夫子所以歎其未見也。若曰：「仁者，天下之公理；好仁者，天下之公心。宜好仁者之多見也，而吾以爲未見者何哉？亦以好仁者之未可易言耳。蓋其眞知仁爲天命之降衷，而好爵之靡根於由衷而不可奪；眞知仁爲人心之秉彝，而懿德之好出於天眞而不可易。物之感人無窮，非一無可好也；以仁視之，皆無益於吾心者也。吾惟知好吾心之仁而已
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“Those who love benevolence place nothing above it.”

Feng Maoren

Comment by Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor: “This captures the meaning of ‘place nothing above it’ and is also refined, pure, and elegant. Include it.”
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: “Precise, clear, and penetrating: this is someone who has devoted himself to investigating the Learning of Principle.”
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: “His understanding is intimate and assured; his wording is plain and substantial.”

The Sage explicitly states that the heart of one who loves benevolence is devoted solely to benevolence. If one loves it yet still has something one places above it, that love is not single-minded. With single-mindedness, the heart becomes pure in benevolence. Surely this is what it means to love benevolence! This is a matter of perfected virtue, which is why the Master lamented that he had never seen such a person. It is as though he said: “Benevolence is the principle common to all under Heaven; the love of benevolence is the disposition common to all human hearts. Those who love benevolence ought therefore to be frequently encountered. Why, then, do I say that I have never seen one? It is simply because one cannot lightly speak of someone as loving benevolence. Such a person truly knows benevolence to be the inner nature bestowed by Heaven’s mandate, and his attachment to the good rank [?] is rooted in his innermost heart and cannot be wrested away. He truly knows benevolence to be the constant norm inherent in the human heart, and his love of admirable virtue arises from his natural authenticity and cannot be changed. The things that move people are inexhaustible; it is not that none is lovable. Yet, viewed in relation to benevolence, they are all of no benefit to my heart. I know only to love the benevolence within my own heart …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而庸知其他乎人之感物而動非一無可欲也
以仁視之皆無與於吾性者也吾惟知好吾性
之仁而已而他尚何羨乎天之所以與我者惟
有此仁吾之所以爲情者惟有此好雖舉天下
之可愛可求者咸不足以尚之矣自吾仁之外
一物不得而容自好仁之外一念不得而雜雖
極天下之至富至貴者舉不足以加之矣是非
有所勉而然也惟其知之也眞故其好之也篤
若曰所好在仁而猶有可好者得而尚之則是
===
仁之未好也豈我之所謂好仁者哉亦非有所
爲而爲也惟其見之也定故其慕之也專若曰
仁爲所好而又有可好者出於其上則是好之
未至也豈吾之所謂未見者哉是則惟好仁者
而後無以尚而必無以尚而後爲好仁此之謂中
心安仁天下一人而已矣夫子之歎其未見者
非斯人歟抑論好德非難知德爲難夫子他日
謂吾未見好德如好色者而語由又謂知德者
鮮夫亦以知與好非二理天下未有知而不好
punctuated: 而庸知其他乎？人之感物而動，非一無可欲也；以仁視之，皆無與於吾性者也。吾惟知好吾性之仁而已，而他尚何羨乎？天之所以與我者，惟有此仁；吾之所以爲情者，惟有此好。雖舉天下之可愛可求者，咸不足以尚之矣。自吾仁之外，一物不得而容；自好仁之外，一念不得而雜。雖極天下之至富至貴者，舉不足以加之矣。是非有所勉而然也，惟其知之也眞，故其好之也篤。若曰所好在仁，而猶有可好者得而尚之，則是仁之未好也，豈我之所謂好仁者哉？亦非有所爲而爲也，惟其見之也定，故其慕之也專。若曰仁爲所好，而又有可好者出於其上，則是好之未至也，豈吾之所謂未見者哉？是則惟好仁者而後無以尚，而必無以尚而後爲好仁。此之謂中心安仁，天下一人而已矣。夫子之歎其未見者，非斯人歟？抑論好德非難，知德爲難。夫子他日謂「吾未見好德如好色者」，而語由又謂「知德者鮮」。夫亦以知與好非二理，天下未有知而不好
translation_en:
…and why should I concern myself with anything else? When people are stirred by external things, there is certainly no lack of things they may desire. Yet viewed in light of benevolence, these all have no part in my nature. I know only to love the benevolence of my own nature; what else, then, should I covet? What Heaven has bestowed upon me is this benevolence alone; what constitutes my feeling is this love alone. Even all that is lovable and worth seeking under Heaven is insufficient to rank above it. Beyond my benevolence, not a single thing may be admitted; alongside my love of benevolence, not a single other thought may intrude. Even the utmost wealth and highest rank under Heaven are insufficient to surpass it. This does not come about through forced effort. Only because one’s knowledge of it is true is one’s love of it profound. If one claims to love benevolence, yet still allows some other lovable thing to rank above it, then one has not yet loved benevolence. How could such a person be what I call a lover of benevolence?

Nor does one act thus for some ulterior end. Only because one’s perception of it is settled is one’s yearning for it single-minded. If benevolence is what one loves, yet another lovable thing stands above it, then one’s love has not reached its utmost. How could such a person be the one whom I say I have never seen? Thus, only for one who loves benevolence does nothing rank above it; and only when nothing ranks above it does one truly love benevolence. This is what is meant by resting content in benevolence in one’s innermost heart: such a person is unique under Heaven. Was it not such a person that the Master lamented he had never seen?

Yet, to discuss the matter further, loving virtue is not difficult; knowing virtue is difficult. On another occasion the Master said, “I have never seen anyone who loves virtue as he loves beauty”; and, speaking to You, he also said, “Few know virtue.” This, too, is because knowing and loving are not two separate principles: there has never been anyone under Heaven who knows it yet does not love it…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
者孔門三月不違僅見顏子其餘日月至焉民
由知之至與不至耳嗚呼有明睿之智斯有服
膺之仁學顏子之所學者何如亦曰進學則在
致知
時使薄斂所以勸百姓也
鄒　錦
同考試官教諭陳　批〔勸百姓作者類多直逆勸此說所以勸之源隱然有催科中撫字意得之宜錄〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔理明詞達可式一受〕
===
考試官教諭馬　批〔意語亮□〕
君有恤民之政斯能得民之情矣夫欲佚欲富
民之同情也使必以時而斂從其薄所以恤之
者至矣民焉有不勸者乎夫子告哀公以九經
至此若謂人君有天下國家之責固當以子庶
民爲常道矣而其事果何如哉誠以君者所事
也則使民者固分也必於使民之中而寓吾不
忍使之意龍見而戒事焉火見而致用焉雖國
有大興不奪其三農之候蓋寧緩我之役以急
punctuated:
者。孔門三月不違，僅見顏子；其餘日月至焉，民由知之至與不至耳。嗚呼！有明睿之智，斯有服膺之仁。學顏子之所學者何如？亦曰：進學則在致知。
時使薄斂所以勸百姓也。
鄒　錦
同考試官教諭陳　批〔勸百姓，作者類多直逆勸，此說所以勸之源，隱然有催科中撫字意，得之，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔理明詞達，可式一受。〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔意語亮□。〕
君有恤民之政，斯能得民之情矣。夫欲佚欲富，民之同情也。使必以時，而斂從其薄，所以恤之者至矣，民焉有不勸者乎？夫子告哀公以九經，至此若謂人君有天下國家之責，固當以子庶民爲常道矣，而其事果何如哉？誠以君者所事也，則使民者固分也，必於使民之中而寓吾不忍使之意。龍見而戒事焉，火見而致用焉，雖國有大興，不奪其三農之候。蓋寧緩我之役，以急
translation_en:
…such a person. Among Confucius’s disciples, only Master Yan was seen to go three months without departing from benevolence; the others attained it for a day or a month. This simply depended [?] on whether their knowledge had reached its fullest extent. Alas! Only with clear and penetrating wisdom can one possess benevolence held firmly to the breast. How does one learn what Master Yan learned? It is simply this: progress in learning lies in extending knowledge.
“Employing them at the proper seasons and taxing them lightly are the means of encouraging the common people.”
Zou Jin.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔On encouraging the common people, most writers address encouragement directly [?]. This essay explains the source from which encouragement arises. Implicitly, it conveys the idea of caring for the people even while collecting taxes. It has grasped the point and merits inclusion.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔The reasoning is clear and the wording expressive; it can serve as a model [remainder doubtful: 一受].〕
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: 〔The ideas and language are lucid [one character illegible].〕
Only when a ruler has policies that care for the people can he win their hearts. The desire for ease and the desire for prosperity are feelings common to all people. If he employs their labor only at the proper seasons and keeps taxation light, his care for them is complete. How could the people fail to be encouraged? When the Master explained the nine guiding principles to Duke Ai, at this point he seemed to be saying: a ruler bears responsibility for all under Heaven, his state, and his house, and should certainly make treating the common people as his children his constant principle. But what, in practice, does this entail? Since the ruler is the one whom the people serve, employing their labor is indeed his proper prerogative. Yet in employing them, he must embody his reluctance to impose labor upon them. When the Dragon constellation appears, he gives notice of the work; when the Fire star appears, he puts their labor to use. Even when the state undertakes great works, he does not encroach upon the seasons of the three kinds of farming. For he would rather delay his own labor services in order to give priority to…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
彼之時而後可也君者所養也則役民者亦分
也必於斂民之內而致吾不忍斂之情什一而
議徹焉九一而議助焉雖國有餘用不踰其九
賦之等蓋寧縮我之入以寬彼之出而後可也
夫曰使則不能不用民之力矣曰斂則不能不
用民之財矣惡在其爲勸我殊不知用其力而
不盡者將欲使天下欣然樂我之力而忘其勞
於使用其財而不盡者將欲使天下驩然德我
之薄而忘其費於斂力役之征民罔違於其分
===
矣而所以默誘其子來之忱而莫甘後者固我
卹傷之一念爲之也布粟之征民罔吝於其分
矣而所以默動其孔邇之懷而不至過者固吾
卹保之一念爲之也蓋樽節愛養之仁與趨赴
轉輸之義流通浹洽而無間矣故曰所以勸百
姓也百姓勸而文武之政舉矣兹其爲九經之
一乎嗚呼夫子之告哀公至矣而公之不悟也
曰二吾猶不足遂至驅會之民盡入於三桓而
後已夫子深致憂焉故作春秋曰城中丘譏非
punctuated: 彼之時而後可也。君者所養也，則役民者亦分也。必於斂民之內，而致吾不忍斂之情。什一而議徹焉，九一而議助焉。雖國有餘用，不踰其九賦之等。蓋寧縮我之入，以寬彼之出，而後可也。夫曰使，則不能不用民之力矣；曰斂，則不能不用民之財矣。惡在其爲勸？我殊不知，用其力而不盡者，將欲使天下欣然樂我之力，而忘其勞於使；用其財而不盡者，將欲使天下驩然德我之薄，而忘其費於斂。力役之征，民罔違於其分矣，而所以默誘其子來之忱，而莫甘後者，固我卹傷之一念爲之也。布粟之征，民罔吝於其分矣，而所以默動其孔邇之懷，而不至過者，固吾卹保之一念爲之也。蓋樽節愛養之仁，與趨赴轉輸之義，流通浹洽而無間矣。故曰：「所以勸百姓也。」百姓勸，而文武之政舉矣。兹其爲九經之一乎！嗚呼！夫子之告哀公至矣，而公之不悟也，曰：「二，吾猶不足。」遂至驅會之民盡入於三桓而後已。夫子深致憂焉，故作《春秋》，曰：「城中丘」，譏非
translation_en:
…their seasonal needs; only then will it be acceptable. The ruler is the one whom the people support, so requiring their service is also within his proper role. Yet in levying upon the people, I must fully express my reluctance to exact anything from them. At one part in ten, consider the che system of taxation; at one part in nine, consider the zhu system of communal cultivation. Even when the state has expenditures beyond its means, do not exceed the prescribed rates of the nine categories of levies. Better to reduce my receipts so as to ease their payments; only then will it be acceptable.

To speak of employing the people necessarily means using their labor; to speak of levying upon them necessarily means using their wealth. How does this amount to encouraging them? I had not realized that using their labor without exhausting it is intended to make all under Heaven gladly welcome my exertions [?], forgetting the toil of their service; and that using their wealth without exhausting it is intended to make all under Heaven joyfully appreciate the lightness of my levies, forgetting the expense of taxation. With labor-service levies, the people do not shirk their allotted duties. Yet what silently inspires their sincerity in coming like children to a parent, with none willing to lag behind, is precisely my concern for their suffering. With levies of cloth and grain, the people do not begrudge their allotted contributions. Yet what silently moves them to feel very close to me, without going to excess [?], is precisely my concern to cherish and protect them.

Thus the benevolence of restraint, care, and nurture, and the dutifulness of hastening to service and transporting supplies, circulate in complete harmony, without interruption. Hence it is said: “This is how to encourage the common people.” When the common people are encouraged, the government of Kings Wen and Wu is put into practice. Is this not one of the nine guiding principles?

Alas! The Master’s instruction to Duke Ai was most complete, yet the duke failed to understand, saying: “Even with two parts in ten, I still do not have enough.” In the end he drove the people of Hui [?] entirely into the hands of the three Huan lineages. The Master was deeply troubled by this. Thus he composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, writing, “They built walls at Zhongqiu,” to criticize its not being…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
時也曰用田賦譏厚斂也意者不能得之於哀
公而庶幾得之於後世也噫以此爲訓猶有虐
用其民以逞者
子路人告之以有過則喜禹聞善言則拜
大舜有大焉善與人同舍己從人樂取
於人以爲善
陳功
同考試官教諭張　批〔認題明白措詞沖澹錄之以式〕
多士
===
考試官教諭謝　批〔峻潔明爽是作手語〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔順暢純雅〕
大賢敘古人之好善而推極於公善者焉夫善
以公天下爲極也此大舜之公善非禹與子路
之所可及與孟子之意謂夫善之在天下本通
物我而無間聖賢之樂善貴合天下以爲公自
今言之夫人每吝於改過子路則勇於自治者
也故人告之以有過則喜其忠告之益得以爲
進善之圖推其心蓋汲汲焉恐有過之不聞矣
punctuated:
時也；曰「用田賦」，譏厚斂也。意者不能得之於哀公，而庶幾得之於後世也。噫！以此爲訓，猶有虐用其民以逞者！

「子路，人告之以有過則喜；禹聞善言則拜；大舜有大焉，善與人同，舍己從人，樂取於人以爲善。」
陳功
同考試官教諭張，批〔認題明白，措詞沖澹，錄之以式〕多士。
考試官教諭謝，批〔峻潔明爽，是作手語。〕
考試官教諭馬，批〔順暢純雅。〕

大賢敘古人之好善，而推極於公善者焉。夫善以公天下爲極也，此大舜之公善，非禹與子路之所可及與？孟子之意謂：夫善之在天下，本通物我而無間；聖賢之樂善，貴合天下以爲公。自今言之，夫人每吝於改過，子路則勇於自治者也。故人告之以有過則喜，其忠告之益，得以爲進善之圖。推其心，蓋汲汲焉，恐有過之不聞矣。
translation_en:
…because it was untimely. When he wrote, “The levy on fields was imposed,” he criticized excessive exactions. Perhaps, unable to secure this from Duke Ai, he hoped to secure it from later generations. Alas! Even with this teaching, there are still those who cruelly exploit their people to gratify themselves!

“When someone told Zilu that he had a fault, he rejoiced. When Yu heard good counsel, he bowed. The great Shun surpassed them: he shared goodness with others, set aside his own views to follow others, and gladly drew upon others to practice goodness.”
Chen Gong
Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor, comments: “The topic is clearly understood, and the wording is restrained and plain. Selected to serve as a model for the many scholars.”
Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: “Elevated and polished, lucid and clear: these are the words of an accomplished writer.”
Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: “Flowing smoothly, pure and elegant.”

The great worthy recounts the ancients’ love of goodness and carries his account to its culmination in one who shared goodness with all. For goodness reaches its highest point when it is shared with all under Heaven. Was not the great Shun’s sharing of goodness beyond what Yu and Zilu could attain? Mencius means that goodness in the world is fundamentally common to others and oneself, without separation. In their delight in goodness, sages and worthies prize bringing all under Heaven together to share it. To speak of this now: people are often reluctant to correct their faults, but Zilu was courageous in disciplining himself. Thus, when someone told him that he had a fault, he rejoiced, for the benefit of such loyal admonition could serve his purpose of advancing in goodness. If we consider his heart, he was surely anxious lest he have a fault of which he had not heard.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
由其可賢者乎夫人莫難於受善禹則虛以受
人者也故人告之以善則本以祇台之德而承
以撝謙之度推其心蓋孳孳焉恐善言之不再
矣禹其無間者乎夫聞過而喜猶知有己也聞
善而拜猶知有人也若大舜則又有大於是者
焉善爲天下所同具而在己在人渾然其無迹
善非有我所得私而忘己忘人廓然其太公已
未善也則無所繫吝而舍以從人自岳牧以至
芻蕘皆其所能從者也人有善也則不待勉强
===
而取之於己自邇言以至疇咨皆其所樂取者
也是內不見己在己莫非人也外不見人在人
莫非己也何所庸其喜而亦何所庸其拜乎舜
之所以爲大者如此後有作者其弗可及也已
易曰山下有澤咸君子以虛受人故舜禹子路
同一樂善之心納百川而注之海其所委不同
其虛受一也無所壅則易入无妄然後可畜故
有子路喜聞過之心則主善惟師禹可至也用
人則稽舜可幾也彼諱疾忌醫則善言莫有至
punctuated: 由其可賢者乎？夫人莫難於受善，禹則虛以受人者也。故人告之以善，則本以祇台之德，而承以撝謙之度。推其心，蓋孳孳焉恐善言之不再矣。禹其無間者乎？夫聞過而喜，猶知有己也；聞善而拜，猶知有人也。若大舜，則又有大於是者焉。善爲天下所同具，而在己在人，渾然其無迹；善非有我所得私，而忘己忘人，廓然其太公。已未善也，則無所繫吝，而舍以從人，自岳牧以至芻蕘，皆其所能從者也；人有善也，則不待勉强，而取之於己，自邇言以至疇咨，皆其所樂取者也。是內不見己，在己莫非人也；外不見人，在人莫非己也。何所庸其喜，而亦何所庸其拜乎？舜之所以爲大者如此，後有作者，其弗可及也已。《易》曰：「山下有澤，咸；君子以虛受人。」故舜、禹、子路，同一樂善之心。納百川而注之海，其所委不同，其虛受一也。無所壅則易入，无妄然後可畜。故有子路喜聞過之心，則主善惟師，禹可至也；用人則稽，舜可幾也。彼諱疾忌醫，則善言莫有至
translation_en:
…Was You (Zilu) not worthy of admiration? Nothing is harder for people than accepting goodness from others, yet Yu emptied himself to receive it. Thus, when someone offered him good counsel, he responded from a foundation of reverence—regarding such counsel as reverence toward himself—and received it with a disposition of manifest humility. Examining his heart, we find him diligently concerned lest good counsel not come again. Was Yu not beyond reproach? Yet to rejoice on hearing of one’s faults is still to be conscious of oneself; to bow on hearing good counsel is still to be conscious of others. The great Shun possessed something greater still. Goodness is shared by all under Heaven: whether in oneself or in others, it forms an undivided whole, leaving no trace of distinction. Goodness is not something one can possess privately; forgetting both self and others, he was expansively and utterly impartial. When he himself was not yet good [?], he clung to nothing and begrudged nothing, but abandoned his own ways to follow others. From the chiefs of the regions and provincial governors down to grass cutters and wood gatherers, all were people he could follow. When others possessed goodness, he took it into himself without needing to force himself. From everyday remarks to deliberations in council, all were things he gladly drew upon. Thus, looking inward, he saw no separate self: whatever was in him came from others. Looking outward, he saw no separate others: whatever was in them was also his own. What need, then, had he to rejoice, or to bow? Such was what made Shun great. Those who arose after him could not equal him.

The Book of Changes says: “Below the mountain is a lake: Influence. The noble man accordingly empties himself to receive others.” Thus Shun, Yu, and Zilu shared the same heart that delighted in goodness. Receiving the hundred streams and pouring them into the sea, they differed in where their waters gathered, but were alike in their open receptivity. Where there is no obstruction, entry is easy; only after Freedom from Falsehood can there be Accumulation. Thus, with Zilu’s heart that rejoiced to hear of his faults, one can take goodness as one’s master and attain Yu’s level; by consulting others when drawing upon their abilities, one can approach Shun’s. But for those who conceal their illness and shun the physician, no good counsel will ever reach…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
將而聽音顏色拒人千里之外亦終違復而已
矣故曰吾人當學子路
易
象曰告公從以益志也
葉士敦
同考試官教諭陳　批〔筆力簡勁且能發君臣益下志〕
尚書錄之
考試官教諭謝　批〔醇雅有味〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔說益上意甚精切〕
===
聖人於六四得益之象而原其有愛民之心也
夫君以民爲心者也人臣精白此心以告君而
君其有不從者乎夫子係益之六四以此意謂
甚矣其臣納忠之難也臣能進其言而不能使
其言之必從與徒往有之令六四而曰告公從
則凡其陳嘉謨嘉猷而爲謀嘉猷之入告者一怡
然而無所拂援事圖策而法語巽語之與聞者
即沛然而莫能禦是知無不言罔四之所以自
盡其職而言無不聽又四之所以自慶其遇也
punctuated:
將而聽音，顏色拒人千里之外，亦終違復而已矣。故曰：吾人當學子路。
易
象曰：「告公從，以益志也。」
葉士敦
同考試官教諭陳，批〔筆力簡勁，且能發君臣益下志〕。尚書錄之。
考試官教諭謝，批〔醇雅有味〕。
考試官教諭馬，批〔說益上意甚精切〕。
聖人於六四得益之象，而原其有愛民之心也。夫君以民爲心者也，人臣精白此心以告君，而君其有不從者乎？夫子係益之六四以此意，謂甚矣其臣納忠之難也！臣能進其言，而不能使其言之必從，與徒往有之。令六四而曰「告公從」，則凡其陳嘉謨嘉猷而爲謀嘉猷之入告者，一怡然而無所拂；援事圖策而法語巽語之與聞者，即沛然而莫能禦。是知無不言，罔四之所以自盡其職；而言無不聽，又四之所以自慶其遇也。
translation_en:
…[?] and, in listening to their words, repels people a thousand li away by his expression; he will ultimately only turn away from returning to goodness. Thus I say: we should learn from Zilu.

Book of Changes

The Commentary on the Images says: “He informs the duke, who follows his advice, because his intention is to bring benefit.”

Ye Shidun

Associate Examiner Chen, an Instructor, comments: 〔The writing is concise and vigorous, and brings out the intention of ruler and minister to benefit those below.〕 The Minister recorded it [?].

Examiner Xie, an Instructor, comments: 〔Pure and elegant, with a lingering savor.〕

Examiner Ma, an Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of the intention to benefit those above is exceptionally precise and apt.〕

In the image of obtaining benefit at the fourth, yin line, the sage traces this benefit to a heart that loves the people. The ruler takes the people as his concern. If a minister makes this concern pure and sincere and presents it to his ruler, how could the ruler fail to follow him? The Master attached this meaning to the fourth, yin line of the hexagram Increase, implying how very difficult it is for a minister to offer loyal counsel! A minister can advance his words, but cannot ensure that they will be followed; there are occasions when his efforts are in vain [?]. Yet of the fourth, yin line it is said, “He informs the duke, who follows his advice.” Thus, whenever he sets forth excellent plans and policies and presents his counsel, all is received with pleasure and without resistance; whenever he cites precedents and devises measures, and offers direct admonition or tactful persuasion for the ruler’s hearing, acceptance flows forth abundantly and cannot be checked. Thus, withholding nothing that he knows is how the fourth line fully discharges its duty [?]; having every word he speaks heeded is also why the fourth line congratulates itself on its fortunate reception.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
然豈無道以致之哉亦由其以益下爲心耳蓋
九五以剛德而主乎上則益下者固公之志也
導公之益而布之下者尤公之所望於四者也
今四也眞知民之天爲君之天而朝夕之所講
求者皇皇焉惟民務之爲急而一念不暇爲身
圖眞以君之心爲我之心而思慮之所經營者
汲汲焉惟民瘼之是軫而一毫不敢爲私計苟
有益於吾民雖屢言之而不爲瀆蓋於未告之
先而吾益下之志潛孚於君心而無間矣苟有
===
損於吾民雖極言之而不爲諱蓋於將告之際
而公知人之哲洞悉乎吾志而無疑矣然則四
之所以告者唯此志也而公之所以從者亦唯
此志也上下交而其志同世豈有不治者哉雖
然所以能通四之志者五也人主之念苟不在
民則以蕭相國之重且賢一爲民請苑而不免
於就繫況其下者乎陸忠州之不能勝延齡司
馬涑水之不能勝安石固其所也故讀九五之
辭曰有孚惠心有孚惠我德然後知六四之道
punctuated:
然豈無道以致之哉？亦由其以益下爲心耳。蓋九五以剛德而主乎上，則益下者固公之志也；導公之益而布之下者，尤公之所望於四者也。今四也，眞知民之天爲君之天，而朝夕之所講求者，皇皇焉惟民務之爲急，而一念不暇爲身圖；眞以君之心爲我之心，而思慮之所經營者，汲汲焉惟民瘼之是軫，而一毫不敢爲私計。苟有益於吾民，雖屢言之而不爲瀆，蓋於未告之先，而吾益下之志潛孚於君心而無間矣。苟有損於吾民，雖極言之而不爲諱，蓋於將告之際，而公知人之哲洞悉乎吾志而無疑矣。然則四之所以告者，唯此志也；而公之所以從者，亦唯此志也。上下交而其志同，世豈有不治者哉？
雖然，所以能通四之志者，五也。人主之念苟不在民，則以蕭相國之重且賢，一爲民請苑而不免於就繫，況其下者乎？陸忠州之不能勝延齡，司馬涑水之不能勝安石，固其所也。故讀九五之辭曰：「有孚惠心，有孚惠我德。」然後知六四之道
translation_en:
Yet is there no way to bring this about? It comes simply from setting one’s heart on benefiting those below. The Nine in the Fifth Place presides above with firm virtue: benefiting those below is indeed the duke’s intention. To convey the duke’s beneficence and distribute it below is, above all, what the duke expects of the fourth line.
Now the fourth line truly understands that what the people regard as Heaven is what the ruler regards as Heaven. In everything he studies and seeks out morning and evening, he anxiously treats the people’s affairs alone as urgent, without a moment’s thought to spare for his own advantage. He truly takes the ruler’s heart as his own. In all that occupies his thoughts and deliberations, he earnestly concerns himself only with the people’s sufferings, not daring in the slightest to calculate his private benefit. If something benefits our people, even repeated representations are not importunate. For before I make my report, my resolve to benefit those below has already, without words, won the ruler’s trust, leaving no estrangement between us. If something harms our people, even speaking with the utmost frankness encounters no taboo. For when I am about to report, the duke’s discernment in understanding men penetrates my intentions completely, leaving no doubt.
Thus it is solely this resolve that moves the fourth line to report, and solely this same resolve that moves the duke to heed him. When those above and below communicate and share one purpose, how could the realm fail to be well governed?
Nevertheless, it is the fifth line that enables the fourth line’s purpose to find expression. If the ruler’s thoughts are not with the people, then even someone as eminent and worthy as Chancellor Xiao could not escape imprisonment after a single request that an imperial park be made available to the people. How much less could those beneath him! That Lu of Zhongzhou could not prevail over Yanling, and Sima of Sushui could not prevail over Anshi, was only to be expected. Thus, after reading the words of the Nine in the Fifth Place, “There is sincerity in a benevolent heart; there is sincerity in cherishing my virtue,” one then understands the way of the Six in the Fourth Place…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
所以行而夫子之意明矣
祐者助也天之所助者順也人之所助者
信也
鄧鏓
同考試官教諭陳　批〔講信順得天人處不費力〕〔何明〕
奏可謝
考試官教諭謝　批〔詞氣暢裕覺之斐然〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔順理成章足執於易者〕
大傳釋祐之義而因推天人所祐惟一理焉蓋
===
理不外於信順也天人交與之道謂不在是乎
大傳釋大有上九爻義若曰道莫難於處有德
莫大於動天大有上九其辭曰自天祐之吉無
不利者何哉所謂祐者非他也一動止焉而繁
祉之休自默牖於何言之表一出入焉而單厚
之益若顯相於無朕之中是祐祐者助之謂耳然
助有得之天者天非漫焉而助我也亦曰順耳
蓋順者天之理而亦我之所得以立命者也故
人惟順焉吾見奉天理以周旋則天心必為之
punctuated:
所以行，而夫子之意明矣。
「祐者，助也。天之所助者，順也；人之所助者，信也。」
鄧鏓
同考試官教諭陳，批〔講信順得天人處不費力〕〔何明〕。奏可謝。
考試官教諭謝，批〔詞氣暢裕覺之斐然〕。
考試官教諭馬，批〔順理成章足執於易者〕。
大傳釋祐之義，而因推天人所祐惟一理焉。蓋理不外於信順也，天人交與之道，謂不在是乎？
大傳釋大有上九爻義，若曰：道莫難於處有，德莫大於動天。大有上九，其辭曰：「自天祐之，吉無不利」者，何哉？所謂祐者，非他也。一動止焉，而繁祉之休自默牖於何言之表；一出入焉，而單厚之益若顯相於無朕之中。是祐，祐者，助之謂耳。然助有得之天者，天非漫焉而助我也，亦曰順耳。蓋順者，天之理，而亦我之所得以立命者也。故人惟順焉，吾見奉天理以周旋，則天心必為之
translation_en:
…the means by which it is put into practice, and the Master's meaning becomes clear.

“Blessing means assistance. Those whom Heaven assists are the compliant; those whom people assist are the trustworthy.”

Deng Cong 鄧鏓

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation of how trustworthiness and compliance win the support of Heaven and people is effortless.〕〔How clear! [?]〕 “Submitted and approved; Xie” [?].

Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and tenor are fluent and ample; one finds it richly accomplished.〕

Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔Following the principle, it forms a coherent composition, sufficient to serve as a guide for those studying the Changes [?].〕

The Great Commentary explains the meaning of “blessing” and thereby deduces that a single principle governs whom Heaven and people bless. This principle extends no further than trustworthiness and compliance. Could the way to obtain the combined support of Heaven and people lie anywhere else?

The Great Commentary explains the meaning of the top yang line of the hexagram Great Possession, as though saying: No way is harder than managing abundance; no virtue is greater than moving Heaven. Why does the statement for the top yang line of Great Possession say, “Heaven itself blesses him: good fortune, with nothing unfavorable”? What is called blessing is nothing other than this: in every movement or rest, the favor of manifold blessings silently opens a way beyond the realm of speech; in every departure or return, abundant benefits seem visibly to assist amid what leaves no trace. This is blessing; blessing simply means assistance. Yet some assistance is obtained from Heaven. Heaven does not assist me indiscriminately: it is simply a matter of compliance. Compliance is Heaven's principle, and it is also what I receive through which to establish my allotted destiny. Thus, if a person is compliant, I see that, when he conducts himself in accordance with Heaven's principle, Heaven's heart will surely, for his sake …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
中養循帝則以默識則帝命必爲之胙祥順而
思焉若或啓之也順而行焉若或翼之也蓋未
有順而不獲助於天亦未有天之助而不及於
順者否則從逆者日速戾於天矣而欲厚望其
助哉助有得之人者人非漫焉而助我也亦曰
信耳蓋信者人之理而亦我之所具以立心者
也故人惟信焉吾見中孚方起信之本而衆志
自妙於感通至誠涵動物之原而羣情自速於
丕應信諸言而民莫不承聽也信諸行而民莫
===
不歸順也蓋未有信而不獲助於人亦未有人
之助而不在於信者否則作僞者將取尤於人
矣而欲强覬其助哉由是觀之順非有求於天
也而天之助恒在焉惟天祐於一德也信非有
求於人也而人之助恒在焉惟民歸於一德也
有之上九所以獲福於天而吉無不利也謂不
有本哉抑夫子序卦嘗曰有大者不可以盈又
曰有大而能謙必豫蓋諄諄然示人以處有之
道非信順不足以居之也然信順之理在我者
punctuated: 中養，循帝則以默識，則帝命必爲之胙祥。順而思焉，若或啓之也；順而行焉，若或翼之也。蓋未有順而不獲助於天，亦未有天之助而不及於順者。否則從逆者日速戾於天矣，而欲厚望其助哉？助有得之人者，人非漫焉而助我也，亦曰信耳。蓋信者，人之理，而亦我之所具以立心者也。故人惟信焉，吾見中孚方起信之本，而衆志自妙於感通；至誠涵動物之原，而羣情自速於丕應。信諸言而民莫不承聽也，信諸行而民莫不歸順也。蓋未有信而不獲助於人，亦未有人之助而不在於信者。否則作僞者將取尤於人矣，而欲强覬其助哉？由是觀之，順非有求於天也，而天之助恒在焉，惟天祐於一德也；信非有求於人也，而人之助恒在焉，惟民歸於一德也。有之上九所以獲福於天而吉無不利也，謂不有本哉？抑夫子《序卦》嘗曰：「有大者不可以盈。」又曰：「有大而能謙必豫。」蓋諄諄然示人以處有之道，非信順不足以居之也。然信順之理，在我者……
translation_en:
…be nurtured within. If one follows the Supreme Lord’s standards and silently apprehends them, the Supreme Lord will surely bestow auspicious blessings. When one thinks in accord with Heaven, it is as though someone enlightens one; when one acts in accord with Heaven, it is as though someone lends one wings. There has never been anyone who accorded with Heaven yet failed to receive its aid, nor has Heaven’s aid ever failed to reach those who accord with it. Otherwise, those who follow a contrary course daily incur Heaven’s wrath: how could they entertain high hopes of its aid?

As for aid received from other people, they do not help me without reason either: it is simply a matter of trustworthiness. Trustworthiness is the principle governing human relations, and it is also what I possess within myself as the foundation of my heart. Thus, when a person is trustworthy, I see that inward sincerity has only just established the root of trust, yet the intentions of the multitude already enter into a wondrous sympathetic communion; perfect sincerity contains the source of the power to move others, and their feelings spontaneously hasten to respond abundantly. If one is trustworthy in speech, none among the people will fail to heed one; if trustworthy in conduct, none will fail to give allegiance. There has never been anyone who was trustworthy yet failed to receive others’ aid, nor has others’ aid ever been independent of trustworthiness. Otherwise, those who practice deceit will incur others’ blame: how could they obstinately hope for their aid?

Viewed in this light, according with Heaven does not mean seeking something from Heaven, yet Heaven’s aid is always present: Heaven aids those of undivided virtue. Trustworthiness does not mean seeking something from other people, yet their aid is always present: the people give allegiance to those of undivided virtue. This is why the top nine of Possession [the hexagram Great Possession, Dayou] receives blessings from Heaven and is auspicious, with nothing unfavorable. Could one say that this has no foundation?

Moreover, the Master once said in the Sequence of the Hexagrams: “One who possesses greatness must not become full.” He also said: “One who possesses greatness and can remain humble will surely find joy.” These earnest and repeated instructions show people the way to conduct themselves amid abundance: without trustworthiness and accordance with Heaven, one cannot dwell in that condition. Yet, as for the principles of trustworthiness and accordance with Heaven, what lies within oneself…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
所當爲天人之助在天者不可必是以古之君
子惟以修悖爲吉凶而不以災祥爲作輟善學
者亦惟求諸己而已天人感應之際曷論哉
書
明四目達四聰
孟養浩
同考試官教諭譚　批　作此題者於明達二字率多未〔　〕
〔歌獨此篇能悉其旨且詞雅格高是諳典謨而有得者〕
考試官教諭謝　批　明暢典雅得大舜命四岳之意
===
考試官教諭馬　批　語意精當
聖君謀治於大臣欲其通天下之情焉蓋安民
莫大於悉其情也廣四方之視聽則民情達於
無間矣其斯以爲圖治之先務哉大舜詢四岳
之意以爲人君之於天下上下者分也一體者
情也惟情睽而弗達此民之所以不安而吾茲
不能無望於汝矣是故人君通天下爲一身則
合天下以爲一人之耳目者固宜也然民情隱
伏於四方則不能以一人而盡天下之聞見者
punctuated:
所當爲，天人之助在天者不可必。是以古之君子惟以修悖爲吉凶，而不以災祥爲作輟。善學者亦惟求諸己而已，天人感應之際曷論哉？

書
明四目，達四聰。
孟養浩

同考試官教諭譚批：作此題者於明達二字率多未〔　〕〔歌，獨此篇能悉其旨，且詞雅格高，是諳典謨而有得者。〕
考試官教諭謝批：明暢典雅，得大舜命四岳之意。
考試官教諭馬批：語意精當。

聖君謀治於大臣，欲其通天下之情焉。蓋安民莫大於悉其情也，廣四方之視聽，則民情達於無間矣。其斯以爲圖治之先務哉！大舜詢四岳之意，以爲人君之於天下，上下者分也，一體者情也。惟情睽而弗達，此民之所以不安，而吾茲不能無望於汝矣。是故人君通天下爲一身，則合天下以爲一人之耳目者固宜也。然民情隱伏於四方，則不能以一人而盡天下之聞見者
translation_en:
…what one ought to do; assistance from Heaven and humankind, insofar as it rests with Heaven, cannot be assured. Thus the gentlemen of antiquity regarded self-cultivation or misconduct as determining good or ill fortune; they did not let calamities or auspicious signs determine whether they continued or ceased their efforts. Those who learn well likewise seek only within themselves. What need is there to discuss the workings of mutual response between Heaven and humankind?

Book of Documents
“Make clear the eyes of the four quarters; open communication to the ears of the four quarters.”
Meng Yanghao

Comment by Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor: Those writing on this topic mostly fail to … [?] in their treatment of the two words “make clear” and “open communication.” 〔This essay alone fully grasps their meaning. Its language is elegant and its style elevated: here is someone thoroughly familiar with the Canons and Counsels who has gained genuine understanding.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: Clear, fluent, classically grounded, and elegant; it captures the intent of Great Shun’s charge to the Four Chiefs.
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: The language and meaning are precise and apt.

When a sage ruler consults his great ministers about governance, he wishes them to make the circumstances of all under Heaven known to him. For nothing is more important in bringing peace to the people than fully understanding their circumstances. If sight and hearing extend throughout the four quarters, the people’s circumstances can be communicated without obstruction. Surely this is the foremost task in planning good government!

Great Shun’s intent in consulting the Four Chiefs was this: “Between the ruler and all under Heaven, distinctions of rank place some above and others below, but their shared feelings unite them as one body. It is only when these feelings become estranged and are not communicated that the people lack peace. Thus I cannot but place my hopes in you.

“Therefore, since the ruler forms one body with all under Heaven, it is certainly fitting that he should bring together all under Heaven to serve as the eyes and ears of one man. Yet the people’s circumstances lie concealed throughout the four quarters, and for one man to encompass everything heard and seen under Heaven is impossible…”

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
亦勢也所以流通於其閒者非爾四岳乎汝其
率天下之諸侯爲我明四目焉其爲太和之景
象是吾之所願見也吾得而見之其爲畎畝之
艱難是吾之所不樂於見者而亦得以見之卽
閭閻之情狀以達之於九重則不必吾之親歷
其地而小人之依皆將宛然有得於目擊矣曾
謂四目明而博觀之外猶有遺情乎汝其率四
方之諸侯爲我達四聰焉其爲黎庶之謳歌是
吾之所樂聞者吾得而聞之其爲小人之怨咨
===
是吾之所不樂於聞者而亦得以聞之卽鰥寡
之有辭以入告於爾后則不必予之親問其人
而小人之依藏皆將恍然如得於耳聞矣曾謂
四聰達而清問之外猶有遺情乎是知惟四岳
以耳目寄諸侯故能作天子之耳目惟天子以
耳目寄四岳故能盡天下之見聞通天下爲一
身而囿四海於度內此有虞之民所以安而協
和萬邦之治垂之無窮也與雖然四目明矣而
又晃旒以爲蔽四聰達矣而又黈纊以爲塞若
punctuated:
亦勢也。所以流通於其閒者，非爾四岳乎？汝其率天下之諸侯，爲我明四目焉。其爲太和之景象，是吾之所願見也，吾得而見之；其爲畎畝之艱難，是吾之所不樂於見者，而亦得以見之。卽閭閻之情狀，以達之於九重，則不必吾之親歷其地，而小人之依，皆將宛然有得於目擊矣。曾謂四目明，而博觀之外猶有遺情乎？汝其率四方之諸侯，爲我達四聰焉。其爲黎庶之謳歌，是吾之所樂聞者，吾得而聞之；其爲小人之怨咨，是吾之所不樂於聞者，而亦得以聞之。卽鰥寡之有辭，以入告於爾后，則不必予之親問其人，而小人之依藏，皆將恍然如得於耳聞矣。曾謂四聰達，而清問之外猶有遺情乎？

是知惟四岳以耳目寄諸侯，故能作天子之耳目；惟天子以耳目寄四岳，故能盡天下之見聞。通天下爲一身，而囿四海於度內，此有虞之民所以安，而協和萬邦之治垂之無窮也與！雖然，四目明矣，而又晃旒以爲蔽；四聰達矣，而又黈纊以爲塞。若
translation_en:
…is also dictated by circumstances. Are you, the Four Peaks, not the ones who ensure communication between them? Lead the feudal lords of the realm and make my sight clear in all four directions. When there are scenes of perfect harmony, which I wish to see, I shall be able to see them; when there are hardships in the fields, which I take no pleasure in seeing, I shall nevertheless be able to see them too. Convey the circumstances of the common people to the innermost palace. Then, without personally visiting those places, I shall apprehend what sustains the common people as vividly as if I had witnessed it myself. Could one suppose that, with sight clear in all four directions, any circumstances would still escape this comprehensive view? Lead the feudal lords of the four quarters and make my hearing unobstructed in all four directions. When the common people sing songs of praise, which I delight in hearing, I shall be able to hear them; when ordinary people voice grievances, which I take no pleasure in hearing, I shall nevertheless be able to hear them too. Bring the words of widowers and widows before your sovereign. Then, without personally questioning those people, I shall clearly apprehend the common people's means of support and what they keep hidden [?], as if I had heard them myself. Could one suppose that, with hearing unobstructed in all four directions, any circumstances would still escape these discerning inquiries?

Thus we know that only because the Four Peaks entrust the feudal lords with serving as their eyes and ears can they serve as the Son of Heaven's eyes and ears; only because the Son of Heaven entrusts the Four Peaks with serving as his eyes and ears can he encompass all that is seen and heard throughout the realm. He unites the realm into one body and brings all within the Four Seas within the compass of his governance. Is this not why the people of Youyu were at peace, and why his rule, which brought the myriad states into harmony, was handed down without end? Nevertheless, though his sight was clear in all four directions, he also used the pendant strands of his crown [?] to screen it; though his hearing was unobstructed in all four directions, he also used yellow floss ear pendants to block it. If so…

無易百穀用成乂用明俊民用章家用

同考試官教諭張批：詞不繁累，而意義自盡，且提掇分明，結構周密，文之可式者。

君子論君臣之異省，而因及休徵之效焉。甚矣，天人感應之理不可誣也！君臣隨分以自省，則休徵應之矣，其效不亦大哉？箕子衍庶徵以告武王，而以省驗之道望之如此。意謂上下之位雖懸，而感通之機則速。是故天人相與之際，可畏也，而亦可喜也。當何如以省之乎？彼五事在
translation_en:
…is it thus that hearing and sight are not valued for their acuity? Ah! This is the meaning of neither undertaking all duties oneself nor claiming to know everything. Thus, when the Four Chiefs are consulted, the ruler’s hearing may be stopped, yet he makes good use of it; when the Four Chiefs are consulted, his sight may be screened, yet he makes good use of it. This is the way by which an enlightened ruler brings about transformation through his own reverent comportment. Should those who desire good government not examine this as well?
“The king should examine the year, the high ministers the month, and the various officials the day. When the seasons of the year, months, and days are not disordered, the hundred grains ripen, government is enlightened, men of outstanding ability become distinguished, and households enjoy peace and well-being.”
Chen Gong
Comment by Associate Examiner Zhang, Instructor: “The wording is neither prolix nor cumbersome, yet fully conveys the meaning. Moreover, the main points are clearly brought out and the structure is meticulous. This is writing that can serve as a model.”
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: “In discussing examination and verification, he clearly grasps the substance and proceeds methodically.”
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: “Concise and clean.”
The gentleman discusses the differing examinations undertaken by ruler and ministers, and thereby proceeds to the effects of auspicious signs. How undeniable is the principle of mutual stimulus and response between Heaven and humanity! When ruler and ministers examine themselves according to their respective responsibilities, auspicious signs appear in response. Are the effects not great? Jizi expounded the various signs to instruct King Wu, placing such expectations upon him concerning the way of examination and verification. His meaning was that, although the positions of superior and subordinate are far apart, the workings of their mutual influence are swift. Thus, the interaction between Heaven and humanity is cause for both awe and joy. How, then, should one conduct this examination? Those five activities reside in…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
人非獨王者有得失於已也而卿士而師尹隨
尊卑而異修者莫非所以感乎天也五氣在天
非獨一歲有利害之係也而一月而一日隨大
小而異運者莫非所以應乎人也惟王之尊無
乎不統則所關甚大其省在已之得失惟以一
歲之利害下此而卿士之統於王也而省以月
焉非其職近卑而責自小乎師尹之統於卿士
也而省以日焉非其職益卑而任愈微乎省驗
之功於斯為密是惟患其不能盡耳誠使王與
===
卿士也上下交脩期得乎五事之理由是歲與
月日也太和洋溢不爽夫五氣之期則休徵應
而所省得矣其效當何如哉吾知百穀得時以
發育者也陰陽和而品彙成遂粒食之天遂矣
治道隨時以章顯者也氣化順而庶事惟新虎
采之績著矣相時而動者有俊民焉黎獻切觀
光之心寧有遺佚者乎乘時而興者有家道焉
比屋洽昌隆之會寧有式微者乎至是則天道
與人道相為流通而氣化與治化相為感召是
punctuated: 人，非獨王者有得失於已也，而卿士，而師尹，隨尊卑而異修者，莫非所以感乎天也。五氣在天，非獨一歲有利害之係也，而一月，而一日，隨大小而異運者，莫非所以應乎人也。惟王之尊，無乎不統，則所關甚大；其省在已之得失，惟以一歲之利害。下此而卿士之統於王也，而省以月焉，非其職近卑而責自小乎？師尹之統於卿士也，而省以日焉，非其職益卑而任愈微乎？省驗之功，於斯為密，是惟患其不能盡耳。誠使王與卿士也，上下交脩，期得乎五事之理；由是歲與月日也，太和洋溢，不爽夫五氣之期，則休徵應而所省得矣。其效當何如哉？吾知百穀得時以發育者也，陰陽和而品彙成，遂粒食之天遂矣；治道隨時以章顯者也，氣化順而庶事惟新，虎采之績著矣；相時而動者有俊民焉，黎獻切觀光之心，寧有遺佚者乎？乘時而興者有家道焉，比屋洽昌隆之會，寧有式微者乎？至是，則天道與人道相為流通，而氣化與治化相為感召，是
translation_en:
…in human affairs. It is not only the king who succeeds or fails in his own conduct: the high ministers and the various officials, whose cultivation differs according to their rank, all thereby move Heaven to respond. The five atmospheric conditions belong to Heaven. It is not only a whole year that bears upon benefit and harm: each month and each day, with their different cycles on larger and smaller scales, likewise respond to human conduct. In his exalted position, the king oversees everything, and thus his responsibilities are exceedingly great. In examining the successes and failures of his own conduct, he takes the benefits and harms of an entire year as his measure. Below him, the high ministers are subject to the king and examine themselves by the month. Is this not because their offices are somewhat lower and their responsibilities correspondingly smaller? The various officials are subject to the high ministers and examine themselves by the day. Is this not because their offices are lower still and their duties yet more limited? The work of self-examination and verification is thus meticulous; the only concern is that they may fail to carry it out fully.

If the king and high ministers truly cultivated themselves together, those above and those below, seeking to realize the principles of the five activities, then throughout the year, months, and days, supreme harmony would overflow, and the five atmospheric conditions would arrive at their proper times without fail. Auspicious signs would then respond, and their self-examination would have attained its purpose. What would the effects be? I know that the many grains would grow and ripen in their proper seasons: yin and yang would be harmonious, all kinds of things would reach maturity, and Heaven’s purpose in providing grain for sustenance would be fulfilled. The way of governance would become manifest in accordance with the seasons: atmospheric transformations would proceed smoothly, all affairs would be renewed, and achievements as brilliant as a tiger’s markings would be displayed. There would be outstanding men who acted when the time was right: with the worthy among the people eagerly wishing to behold the realm’s splendor, could any remain overlooked? There would be households that flourished as opportunity arose: with every home sharing in the occasion of prosperity, could any fall into decline? At this point, the Way of Heaven and the human Way would flow into one another, and transformations in the atmosphere and transformations through governance would mutually evoke responses. This is…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
休徵之大效也反是而咎徵應之矣君臣省驗
之功烏容已哉嘗謂天人之蘊未易達也箕子
衍庶徵而惓惓於事應之說其於春秋之止言
災異者不幾於相戾矣乎是不然箕子之意推
天而徵之人也夫子之言責人而及於天也立
言雖異而致望人君之意同矣自此義不明後
世爭爲劉向五行之論拘其迹於類應之間穿
鑿旁引以啓人主之不信而省驗之道荒矣無
怪乎治之不古也意
===
詩
素絲祝之良馬六之
渠兆昌
同考試官教諭李　批　〔題枯淡而文充腴且大夫遂良〕
〔素志溢於言外佳作也〕
考試官教諭謝　批　〔善發大夫見賢之意〕
考試官教諭馬　批　〔詞旨婉順得風人之體〕
大夫之見賢者而極其儀之盛焉夫車馬旌旗
大夫之所以爲儀也用之以見賢者而各極其
punctuated:
休徵之大效也。反是而咎徵應之矣，君臣省驗之功烏容已哉？嘗謂天人之蘊未易達也。箕子衍庶徵而惓惓於事應之說，其於《春秋》之止言災異者，不幾於相戾矣乎？是不然。箕子之意，推天而徵之人也；夫子之言，責人而及於天也。立言雖異，而致望人君之意同矣。自此義不明，後世爭爲劉向五行之論，拘其迹於類應之間，穿鑿旁引，以啓人主之不信，而省驗之道荒矣。無怪乎治之不古也。意！

詩
素絲祝之，良馬六之。
渠兆昌

同考試官教諭李批：〔題枯淡而文充腴，且大夫遂良〕〔素志溢於言外，佳作也。〕
考試官教諭謝批：〔善發大夫見賢之意。〕
考試官教諭馬批：〔詞旨婉順，得風人之體。〕

大夫之見賢者，而極其儀之盛焉。夫車馬旌旗，大夫之所以爲儀也。用之以見賢者，而各極其
translation_en:
…the great effect of auspicious signs. Conversely, ominous signs will appear in response. How could ruler and ministers ever cease their work of scrutiny and verification? I have often said that the profound workings of Heaven and humanity are not easily understood. Jizi elaborated upon the various signs, dwelling earnestly on the doctrine that they respond to human affairs. Does this not seem almost to contradict the Spring and Autumn Annals, which speaks only of calamities and anomalies? It does not. Jizi’s intention was to reason from Heaven and seek verification in human affairs; the Master’s words held humanity responsible and extended to Heaven. Although their formulations differed, their expectations of the ruler were the same. Once this principle became obscure, later generations competed in advancing theories of the Five Phases like those of Liu Xiang. They confined their inquiries to correspondences between categories, forcing interpretations and adducing far-fetched parallels, thereby inviting the ruler’s disbelief and allowing the practice of scrutiny and verification to fall into neglect. No wonder government failed to match that of antiquity. Alas! [?]

Book of Poetry
“Bind them with white silk; provide six fine horses.”
Qu Zhaochang

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔The topic is dry and plain, but the writing is rich and full; moreover, the grand officer’s〕〔long-held aspiration to advance the worthy is conveyed beyond the words themselves. An excellent composition.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔It brings out well the grand officer’s intention in visiting the worthy.〕
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: 〔The language and meaning are gentle and harmonious, capturing the manner of the poets of the Airs.〕

When the grand officer visits a worthy man, he displays the utmost magnificence of his ceremonial equipment. Carriages, horses, and banners are what constitute a grand officer’s ceremonial array. He uses them when visiting the worthy, bringing each to its utmost…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
盛謂非好德之誠乎昔詩人之意謂夫人臣切
