爲國之忠必親賢而後可以善其治敦下士之
典必隆禮而後可以洽其交大夫有事於見賢
固在浚之城也吾人何幸逢其盛乎是故大夫
有浚明之寄而先王分物采以彰之於是有旄
以建於車焉斯固有位者之表儀而人之所具
瞻者使不有以祝之則無以盡其制而祝匪素
絲亦無以備其飾矣今不徒紕之組之已也但
見屬之以絲而維繫極綜理之周尚之以素而
===
白賁昭安節之吉質而不靡焉簡而有文焉雖
大夫求賢之素志非祝絲之所能盡而以是設
於號見則一時折節之敬不溢於儀文之表矣
乎以至大夫與從政之列而先王頒車服以庸
之於是有馬以引夫車焉是固有位者之名器
而人之所快覩者使馬有不良則無以盡其材
而良馬匪六亦無以昭其盛矣今不特四之五
之已也但見調習有方莫非上襄之選驂服有
備又極蕃庶之多等威以辨焉輪轅以飭焉雖
punctuated: 盛，謂非好德之誠乎？昔詩人之意，謂夫人臣切爲國之忠，必親賢而後可以善其治；敦下士之典，必隆禮而後可以洽其交。大夫有事於見賢，固在浚之城也。吾人何幸逢其盛乎！是故大夫有浚明之寄，而先王分物采以彰之，於是有旄以建於車焉。斯固有位者之表儀，而人之所具瞻者。使不有以祝之，則無以盡其制；而祝匪素絲，亦無以備其飾矣。今不徒紕之組之已也，但見屬之以絲，而維繫極綜理之周；尚之以素，而白賁昭安節之吉。質而不靡焉，簡而有文焉。雖大夫求賢之素志，非祝絲之所能盡，而以是設於號見，則一時折節之敬，不溢於儀文之表矣乎？以至大夫與從政之列，而先王頒車服以庸之，於是有馬以引夫車焉。是固有位者之名器，而人之所快覩者。使馬有不良，則無以盡其材；而良馬匪六，亦無以昭其盛矣。今不特四之五之已也，但見調習有方，莫非上襄之選；驂服有備，又極蕃庶之多。等威以辨焉，輪轅以飭焉。雖
translation_en: …splendor—could this be anything other than sincerity in loving virtue? The poet’s meaning was that a minister earnestly devoted to his state must draw close to worthy men before he can govern it well; to uphold the practice of humbling oneself before men of worth, he must give full expression to ritual courtesy before their relations can become harmonious. The grand officer was engaged in visiting a worthy man, there at the city of Jun. How fortunate we are to witness such splendor! Thus the grand officer was entrusted with making virtue shine forth [?], and the former kings allotted distinctive insignia to make his standing manifest. Hence a yak-tail banner was erected on his carriage. This was indeed an emblem of a man holding office, upon which all eyes were fixed. Without something to bind it, its prescribed form could not be fully realized; and unless it was bound with plain silk, its ornamentation could not be complete. Now it was not merely edged and adorned with woven bands: we see it attached with silk, its fastenings arranged with the utmost thoroughness, and adorned with plain white, whose unadorned beauty manifests the good fortune of resting content within proper limits. It was substantial without extravagance, simple yet patterned. Although silk bindings cannot fully express the grand officer’s enduring resolve to seek worthy men, when displayed for his visit [?], did not the respect he showed in humbling himself overflow beyond the outward forms of ceremony? Furthermore, the grand officer belonged to the ranks of those engaged in government, and the former kings rewarded his service with carriages and robes. Hence there were horses to draw his carriage. These were indeed the insignia and equipment of a man holding office, which people delighted to behold. If the horses were not fine, their capacities could not be fully realized; and unless there were six fine horses, their splendor could not be displayed. Now there were not merely four or five: we see them trained by proper methods, every one selected for superior quality [?]; the outer and central horses were all provided, in the fullest abundance. The distinctions of rank were thereby made clear, and the wheels and shafts duly arrayed. Although…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
大夫遂良之夙心非六馬之所能悉而以是隆
於下交則一時枉駕之禮不侈其載道之光矣
乎夫大夫見賢而其儀極盛如此蓋深知以人
事君之義矣然則賢者有不樂告以善道者哉
宜衛之勃然而中興也抑考之易曰天地交而
萬物通上下交而其志同蓋言君臣相須之重
也懿公使鶴乘軒而不知尊士久矣文公徙居
楚丘固克振式微之業而又有禮賢下士如干
旄之大夫焉則所以上下交修而成治功者非
===
偶然也噫詩可以觀信夫
受小球大球爲下國綴旒何天之休不競
不絿不剛不柔敷政優優百祿是遒受
小共大共爲下國駿厖何天之龍敷奏
其勇不震不動不戁不竦百祿是總
王士毅
同考試官教諭李　批
〔氣昌而詞暢文之推者錄之以〕
式多士
考試官教諭謝　批
〔通篇發明德意盡是深於詩者〕
punctuated:
大夫遂良之夙心，非六馬之所能悉，而以是隆於下交，則一時枉駕之禮，不侈其載道之光矣乎？夫大夫見賢，而其儀極盛如此，蓋深知以人事君之義矣。然則賢者有不樂告以善道者哉？宜衛之勃然而中興也。抑考之《易》曰：「天地交而萬物通，上下交而其志同。」蓋言君臣相須之重也。懿公使鶴乘軒，而不知尊士久矣。文公徙居楚丘，固克振式微之業，而又有禮賢下士如《干旄》之大夫焉，則所以上下交修而成治功者，非偶然也。噫！《詩》可以觀，信夫！

受小球大球，爲下國綴旒，何天之休。不競不絿，不剛不柔，敷政優優，百祿是遒。受小共大共，爲下國駿厖，何天之龍。敷奏其勇，不震不動，不戁不竦，百祿是總。

王士毅

同考試官教諭李，批：〔氣昌而詞暢，文之推者，錄之以〕式多士。

考試官教諭謝，批：〔通篇發明德意，盡是深於詩者。〕
translation_en:
…the grand officer’s longstanding desire to advance worthy men could not be fully expressed by six horses. Yet by thus honoring those below him, did not the courtesy of his personal visit magnify the splendor of his bearing the Way? When this grand officer visited worthy men, his ceremonial observances were so splendid because he deeply understood the duty of serving one’s ruler by securing worthy men for him. How, then, could the worthy fail to delight in telling him of the good Way? It was fitting that Wei should flourish and revive.

Moreover, the Book of Changes says: “Heaven and earth interact, and all things communicate; those above and below interact, and their purposes accord.” This speaks of the importance of the ruler’s and his ministers’ mutual dependence. Duke Yi let cranes ride in carriages reserved for dignitaries and had long failed to honor men of worth. Duke Wen moved his seat to Chuqiu and indeed revived his declining state. With a grand officer like the one in “The Raised Pennants” (Gan mao), who honored worthy men and humbled himself before them, the achievement of good government through mutual cultivation between those above and below was no accident. Ah! That the Odes can be used to observe the state of society is true indeed!

He received small jade spheres and great jade spheres,
And became the fastening cord for the states below,
Bearing Heaven’s favor.
Neither forceful nor hasty,
Neither hard nor soft,
He administered government with ample ease,
And all blessings gathered around him.
He received small offerings and great offerings,
And became the mighty support of the states below,
Bearing Heaven’s bounty.
He displayed and exerted his courage,
Neither shaking nor wavering,
Neither fearing nor trembling,
And all blessings were gathered in him.

Wang Shiyi

Comment by Associate Examiner Li, Instructor: “〔His spirit is vigorous and his expression fluent. This is writing to be commended [?]; it is recorded to〕 serve as a model for the assembled scholars.”

Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: “〔Throughout, this piece elucidates the meaning of virtue; it is entirely the work of someone with a deep understanding of the Odes.〕”

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭馮　批〔憔暢無一浮語〕
商人表聖人之受命而推其本於敬焉夫行政
用武皆所以體天之心也而聖人一本於敬焉
則其受天下之朝貢有由然哉此商人祫祭之
詩也若曰惟我成湯聖敬日躋而帝心簡在固
命式於九圍矣然果何以見之自先王以覲禮
親邦國有小球大球焉是天之休命也今各修
夫合瑞之典而湯於是乎受之則聯屬諸侯誠
為下國之綴旒而天休之所荷者至矣果何施
===
而臻此哉蓋政所以代天而理物者惟成湯之
敷政也化裁以盡制而競絿不倚於一偏隨時
以用中而剛柔每得於相濟優優乎一敬以運
之而有以奉若乎天道矣則夫受小大之球而
百祿所由聚者殆不約而同也所以荷天之休
者孰非帝天之命哉自先王以享禮仁邦國有
小貢大貢焉是天之寵命也今各盡夫職貢之
常而湯於是乎受之則承藉四方誠為下國之
駿厖而天寵之所荷者至矣抑何脩而得此哉
punctuated:
考試官教諭馮批〔憔暢，無一浮語。〕

商人表聖人之受命，而推其本於敬焉。夫行政用武，皆所以體天之心也，而聖人一本於敬焉，則其受天下之朝貢有由然哉！此商人祫祭之詩也。若曰：惟我成湯，聖敬日躋，而帝心簡在，固命式於九圍矣。然果何以見之？自先王以覲禮親邦國，有小球大球焉，是天之休命也。今各修夫合瑞之典，而湯於是乎受之，則聯屬諸侯，誠為下國之綴旒，而天休之所荷者至矣。果何施而臻此哉？蓋政所以代天而理物者。惟成湯之敷政也，化裁以盡制，而競絿不倚於一偏；隨時以用中，而剛柔每得於相濟。優優乎，一敬以運之，而有以奉若乎天道矣。則夫受小大之球，而百祿所由聚者，殆不約而同也。所以荷天之休者，孰非帝天之命哉？自先王以享禮仁邦國，有小貢大貢焉，是天之寵命也。今各盡夫職貢之常，而湯於是乎受之，則承藉四方，誠為下國之駿厖，而天寵之所荷者至矣。抑何脩而得此哉？
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Feng, Instructor: 〔Fluid and expansive [?], without a single empty expression.〕

The people of Shang celebrated the sage’s receipt of the Mandate and traced its foundation to reverence. Conducting government and employing military force are both means of embodying Heaven’s intentions. Since the sage grounded both entirely in reverence, surely there was a reason why he received court attendance and tribute from all under Heaven! This is a poem for the Shang people’s combined ancestral sacrifice. It speaks as follows: Our Cheng Tang advanced daily in sagely reverence and was chosen in the heart of the Sovereign on High; his mandate was firmly established throughout the nine regions. Yet how can this actually be seen?

From the time of the former kings, the rites of royal audience served to bring the regional states into close relations, with their small and large jade tokens: these signified Heaven’s gracious mandate. Now each lord observes the ceremony of matching jade credentials, and Tang receives them. Thus, binding the feudal lords together, he truly serves as the cord holding together the pendant banners of the states below, and receives Heaven’s grace to the utmost. What measures brought him to this point? Government is the means of ordering affairs on Heaven’s behalf. In Cheng Tang’s administration, he adapted and regulated affairs to perfect his institutions, inclining neither toward contention nor toward haste. He applied the mean as circumstances required, so that firmness and gentleness always complemented one another. With ample ease, he directed everything through reverence alone, thereby following the Way of Heaven. Thus his receipt of the small and large jade tokens and the gathering of the hundred blessings occurred together, almost as though in concert without prior agreement. Of all that enabled him to receive Heaven’s grace, what was not the mandate of the Heavenly Sovereign?

From the time of the former kings, the rites of presentation served to extend benevolence to the regional states, with their small and large tribute offerings: these signified Heaven’s favoring mandate. Now each lord fully discharges his regular tribute obligations, and Tang receives their offerings. Thus, sustaining the four quarters, he truly serves as the great support of the states below, and receives Heaven’s favor to the utmost. Yet what did he cultivate to obtain this?

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
蓋武所以奉天而伐暴者惟成湯之奏功也忠
爲戡定之猷而震動之無遠恢爲奮揚之烈而
難疎之不形赫赫然一敬以發之而有以奉行
乎天威矣則夫受小大之共而百祿所由會者
殆不期而至也所以荷天之寵者孰非帝命之
齊哉是則敬德純於一已無忝濬哲之資朝貢
合乎萬邦自極發祥之盛信乎成湯之大造於
商也而可忘所自耶抑論敬者帝王祈天永命
之本也有商之業肇於玄王之率履不越固世
===
德之所由基而成湯之聖又有以光大之宜其
式九圍而朝貢不能外矣要之有本焉書曰天
乃錫王勇智表正萬邦又曰惟尹躬暨湯咸有
一德此固其厚於天而脩於人者也合而觀之
始得
春秋
春齊侯宋人陳人蔡人邾人會于北杏〔莊〕
公十三年
馮懋仁
punctuated:
蓋武所以奉天而伐暴者，惟成湯之奏功也。忠爲戡定之猷，而震動之無遠；恢爲奮揚之烈，而難疎之不形。赫赫然一敬以發之，而有以奉行乎天威矣。則夫受小大之共，而百祿所由會者，殆不期而至也。所以荷天之寵者，孰非帝命之齊哉？是則敬德純於一已，無忝濬哲之資；朝貢合乎萬邦，自極發祥之盛。信乎成湯之大造於商也，而可忘所自耶？抑論敬者，帝王祈天永命之本也。有商之業，肇於玄王之率履不越，固世德之所由基，而成湯之聖又有以光大之，宜其式九圍而朝貢不能外矣。要之，有本焉。《書》曰：「天乃錫王勇智，表正萬邦。」又曰：「惟尹躬暨湯咸有一德。」此固其厚於天而脩於人者也。合而觀之，始得。

春秋
春，齊侯、宋人、陳人、蔡人、邾人會于北杏。〔莊〕公十三年。
馮懋仁
translation_en:
…For martial power, used to serve Heaven and punish tyranny, found its achievement in Cheng Tang. Loyalty guided his plans for conquest and pacification, and no place was beyond the reach of his awe; magnanimity informed his vigorous deeds, and hostility and estrangement did not appear [?]. Manifest in his majesty, he brought these forth through undivided reverence and thereby carried out Heaven’s awesome authority. Thus, as he received the tribute of the small and the great, the hundred blessings gathered upon him, arriving almost unbidden. In bearing Heaven’s favor, what was there that did not accord with the Supreme Lord’s command? His reverent virtue was pure within himself, doing no discredit to his endowment of profound wisdom; the myriad states joined in presenting tribute at court, bringing the flourishing of auspicious beginnings to its height. Truly, Cheng Tang’s accomplishment for Shang was great. Yet could its source be forgotten?

To discuss reverence further: it is the foundation upon which emperors and kings seek from Heaven an enduring mandate. Shang’s enterprise began with the Dark King’s following the proper course without transgression. This laid the foundation for the virtue transmitted through successive generations, and Cheng Tang’s sageliness further enlarged and glorified it. Fittingly, he became a model for the nine regions, and none could remain outside the order of tribute and court attendance. In sum, this had a foundation. The Book of Documents says: “Heaven then bestowed courage and wisdom upon the king, that he might serve as a model and rectify the myriad states.” It also says: “Yin himself and Tang both possessed undivided virtue.” These passages indeed show his generous endowment from Heaven and his cultivation in the human sphere. Only by considering them together can one grasp the meaning.

Spring and Autumn Annals
“In spring, the Marquis of Qi and representatives of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu met at Beixing.” Thirteenth year of Duke Zhuang 〔Zhuang〕.
Feng Maoren.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教諭丁　批〔發揮聖人尊王衛世之意極爲明盡且詞氣充暢規格整齊宜錄爲式〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔氣昌義精〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔得謹嚴體〕
春秋示予奪於羣霸之會無非爲王道計也甚
矣王霸盛衰之機可慮也桓霸因以匡王焉春
秋酌經權而予奪之有以哉且北杏曷爲而會
也齊平宋難遂圖霸業故合宋陳蔡邾之君以
相會也夫四國稱人何罪乎蓋文侯命爲方伯
===
乎王錫之桓非受命之霸也周德雖衰綴旒猶
在四國何心也可急於桓之戴乎夫何命未請
于王朝策未作於內史私相依附以主天下會
盟之政是有見於從霸無見於尊王厚在於齊
則薄在於周矣噫宗周所賴以匡翼者列國也
今也惟霸是與所謂預贅周道誰復念之自是
强國更霸相繼以遑使禮樂征伐自諸侯出焉
謂非此會有以倡之與故正以人諸侯者爲王
道憂也齊侯稱爵何予乎蓋叅離降爲國風天
punctuated:
同考試官教諭丁　批〔發揮聖人尊王衛世之意，極爲明盡，且詞氣充暢，規格整齊，宜錄爲式。〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔氣昌義精。〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔得謹嚴體。〕
春秋示予奪於羣霸之會，無非爲王道計也。甚矣，王霸盛衰之機可慮也！桓霸因以匡王焉，春秋酌經權而予奪之，有以哉！且北杏曷爲而會也？齊平宋難，遂圖霸業，故合宋陳蔡邾之君以相會也。夫四國稱人，何罪乎？蓋文侯命爲方伯乎？王錫之。桓非受命之霸也。周德雖衰，綴旒猶在，四國何心也？可急於桓之戴乎？夫何命未請于王朝，策未作於內史，私相依附，以主天下會盟之政？是有見於從霸，無見於尊王，厚在於齊，則薄在於周矣。噫！宗周所賴以匡翼者，列國也。今也惟霸是與，所謂預贅周道，誰復念之？自是强國更霸，相繼以遑，使禮樂征伐自諸侯出焉，謂非此會有以倡之與？故正以人諸侯者，爲王道憂也。齊侯稱爵，何予乎？蓋叅離降爲國風，天
translation_en:
Comment by Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor: 〔The exposition of the Sage’s intention to honor the king and safeguard the age is exceptionally clear and thorough. Moreover, the language is vigorous and fluent, and the composition orderly and well proportioned. It should be recorded as a model.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔Vigorous in spirit and refined in meaning.〕
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: 〔It achieves a meticulous and disciplined style.〕
In bestowing approval and censure upon the assemblies of the various hegemons, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably has the kingly Way in view. How deeply troubling are the turning points in the rise and decline of kingship and hegemony! Duke Huan used his hegemony to uphold the king. The Annals weighs constant principles against expedient measures in granting or withholding approval: surely it has its reasons!
Why, then, was the assembly at Beixing held? Having settled the troubles in Song, Qi proceeded to seek hegemony, and therefore brought together the rulers of Song, Chen, Cai, and Zhu. What offense had these four states committed, that their rulers are designated merely as “men”? As for the appointment of the Marquis of Wen as regional lord, was it not conferred by the king? Huan, however, was a hegemon who had received no royal commission. Although Zhou’s virtue had declined, the king remained, like a pendant suspended from a banner. What were the four states thinking? Could they be so eager to uphold Huan? Why, before authorization had been sought from the royal court and a patent drawn up by the Interior Scribe, did they privately attach themselves to one another to control the affairs of assemblies and covenants throughout the realm? This showed an understanding of following a hegemon, but none of honoring the king. Their greater devotion to Qi meant diminished devotion to Zhou.
Alas! The royal house of Zhou depended upon the several states to sustain and assist it. Now they supported only the hegemon. Who any longer gave thought to what is called sustaining the Way of Zhou [?]? Thereafter, powerful states became hegemons in succession, one after another [the wording here is doubtful: ?], causing ritual, music, and punitive expeditions to issue from the feudal lords themselves. Can one say that this assembly did not help initiate that development? Thus, it is precisely out of concern for the kingly Way that the Annals calls the feudal lords merely “men.”
Why, then, does it grant approval by referring to the Marquis of Qi by his noble rank? When “Can Li” [?; apparently “Shu Li,” or “Millet Drooping”] was relegated to the Airs of the States, all under Heaven …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
下傷之桓國乘時而霸者也伯侯失職夷狄日
横斯何時耶而可少於桓之興乎幸而遠追賜
履之勳聿紹夾輔之烈合謀經營以免斯民左
衽之患卒之威令行於九合事業成於一匡是
霸圖之啓諸夏之幸也噫中國所恃以安攘者
齊桓也今而身任其責所謂四國有王桓與寄
之自是南權西抑遂主夏盟使民到於今受其
賜焉謂非此會有以致之與故權以爵齊侯者
爲世道計也吁誅諸侯見天下不可以無王予
===
齊侯見天下不可以無霸春秋尊王衞世之意
不旣深乎蓋當是時周衰夷横管仲相桓公圖
霸業宋有逆萬之亂故爲此會以平之其名正
矣四國來從桓其以義率人者與但不能加兵
於萬識者恨之或無討賊誠心故也魯衞最爲
近齊俱不至焉蓋桓公之信未孚於人也故曰
五霸假之也
八月己酉入邾以邾子益來〔哀公七年夏〕
齊人取讙及闡歸邾子益于邾〔齊人〕
punctuated:
下傷之。桓國乘時而霸者也。伯侯失職，夷狄日横，斯何時耶？而可少於桓之興乎？幸而遠追賜履之勳，聿紹夾輔之烈，合謀經營，以免斯民左衽之患。卒之威令行於九合，事業成於一匡，是霸圖之啓，諸夏之幸也。噫！中國所恃以安攘者，齊桓也。今而身任其責，所謂四國有王，桓與寄之。自是南權西抑，遂主夏盟，使民到於今受其賜焉，謂非此會有以致之與？故權以爵齊侯者，爲世道計也。吁！誅諸侯，見天下不可以無王；予齊侯，見天下不可以無霸。《春秋》尊王衞世之意，不旣深乎？蓋當是時，周衰夷横，管仲相桓公，圖霸業。宋有逆萬之亂，故爲此會以平之，其名正矣。四國來從桓，其以義率人者與？但不能加兵於萬，識者恨之，或無討賊誠心故也。魯衞最爲近齊，俱不至焉，蓋桓公之信未孚於人也。故曰：「五霸假之也。」
八月己酉，入邾，以邾子益來。〔哀公七年夏〕
齊人取讙及闡，歸邾子益于邾。〔齊人〕
translation_en:
…all under heaven grieved over it. Huan’s state [?] seized the opportunity of the times to establish hegemony. The regional lords neglected their duties, and the Yi and Di grew daily more unruly. What sort of time was this? Could the rise of Duke Huan possibly have been dispensed with? Fortunately, he emulated the distant achievements for which his ancestor had been granted territory, continuing that illustrious service in support of the royal house. Through concerted planning and action, he spared the people the calamity of wearing their robes fastened on the left, in the manner of the barbarians. Ultimately, his authority prevailed through nine assemblies of the lords, and his achievement culminated in bringing all under heaven into order. This beginning of his hegemonic undertaking was a blessing for the Xia states.
Alas! It was Duke Huan of Qi upon whom the central states relied for internal peace and resistance to outsiders. Now he personally assumed that responsibility. As for the saying, “The four quarters have their king,” its fulfillment was entrusted to Huan. Thereafter he exercised power in the south and imposed restraints in the west [?], becoming the leader of the Xia states’ covenants, so that the people have benefited from his bounty down to the present. Can one deny that this assembly helped bring that about? Thus, the expedient recognition of the lord of Qi by his noble rank was a measure taken for the sake of order in the world.
Ah! Censuring the regional lords shows that all under heaven cannot do without a king; commending the lord of Qi shows that all under heaven cannot do without a hegemon. Is not the intent of the Spring and Autumn Annals—to honor the king and safeguard the world—profound indeed? At that time, Zhou was declining and the barbarians were rampant. Guan Zhong served as chief minister to Duke Huan and planned the establishment of his hegemony. Song suffered the rebellion of the traitor Wan, and this assembly was therefore convened to settle it: its stated purpose was proper. Four states came to follow Huan; was he not leading others through righteousness? Yet he failed to take military action against Wan, something discerning men regretted. Perhaps this was because he lacked a sincere resolve to punish the traitor. Lu and Wei were the states nearest Qi, yet neither attended: Duke Huan’s good faith had evidently not yet won people’s confidence. Thus it is said: “The Five Hegemons borrowed it”—that is, the outward practice of benevolence and righteousness.
On the jiyou day of the eighth month, [the forces of Lu] entered Zhu and brought back Yi, Viscount of Zhu. 〔Summer, seventh year of Duke Ai.〕
The men of Qi took Huan and Chan and returned Yi, Viscount of Zhu, to Zhu. 〔The men of Qi …〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
歸讙及闡　似哀公八十
劉　迵
同考試官教諭丁　批〔此作發明齊人改過遷善之美〕
〔最爲詳悉而語意精純尤非諸作可及允宜高薦〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔詳重克贍〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔平實雅贍〕
春秋詳內君遠順之應見其遷善之優也夫哀
公去惡以召順是蓋其致逆之愆也此春秋於
入邾之役原始要終以彰其善歟且邾之於魯
===
也在邦域之中方將恃我以相恤者何哀也聽
康子之謀興入國之師俘其君而負瑕因焉何
義乎於是齊人觀釁謀讙闡是取周公之宇岌岌
乎分崩莫保矣吾見邾有俘君之慘我有危國
之憂二邑之處謂非自貽之戚不可也君子曰
非齊之始禍魯之啓戎有以來之也故書曰以
曰取造惡之尤夫豈待辯乎乃若邾罹殘滅之
後無復得國之是望者然哀也悔旣往之愆復
曹陝之祀返其君而東要安焉非義乎於是齊
punctuated:
歸讙及闡。似哀公八十。
劉迵
同考試官教諭丁批〔此作發明齊人改過遷善之美〕〔最爲詳悉，而語意精純，尤非諸作可及，允宜高薦。〕
考試官教諭謝批〔詳重克贍。〕
考試官教諭馬批〔平實雅贍。〕
春秋詳內君遠順之應，見其遷善之優也。夫哀公去惡以召順，是蓋其致逆之愆也。此春秋於入邾之役，原始要終，以彰其善歟？且邾之於魯也，在邦域之中，方將恃我以相恤者。何哀也聽康子之謀，興入國之師，俘其君而負瑕因焉，何義乎？於是齊人觀釁謀讙，闡是取，周公之宇岌岌乎分崩莫保矣。吾見邾有俘君之慘，我有危國之憂，二邑之處，謂非自貽之戚不可也。君子曰：「非齊之始禍，魯之啓戎有以來之也。」故書曰「以」，曰「取」，造惡之尤，夫豈待辯乎？乃若邾罹殘滅之後，無復得國之是望者，然哀也悔旣往之愆，復曹陝之祀，返其君而東要安焉，非義乎？於是齊
translation_en:
…returned Huan and Chan. [The following date notation, 似哀公八十, is garbled; apparently the eighth year of Duke Ai.]
Liu Dong 劉迵
Associate Examiner Ding, an Instructor, comments: 〔This composition elucidates the merit of the people of Qi in correcting their faults and turning toward goodness.〕〔Its treatment is exceptionally thorough, and its language and thought are refined and pure, beyond the reach of the other compositions. It certainly deserves a strong recommendation.〕
Examiner Xie, an Instructor, comments: 〔Thorough, weighty, and amply developed.〕
Examiner Ma, an Instructor, comments: 〔Unpretentious and substantial, elegant and ample.〕
The Spring and Autumn Annals details the favorable response elicited by the ruler of its own state [?], showing the excellence of his turning toward goodness. Duke Ai abandoned wrongdoing and thereby called forth compliance; this concerned the fault by which he had previously provoked hostility [?]. In its account of the invasion of Zhu, does not the Spring and Autumn Annals trace the beginning and examine the outcome in order to make his goodness manifest?
Now Zhu, in its relation to Lu, lay within its territorial bounds and was looking to us for protection and assistance. Why, then, did Duke Ai listen to Kangzi’s scheme, raise an army to invade that state, capture its ruler, and confine him at Fuxia [?]? What righteousness was there in this? Thereupon the people of Qi watched for an opening, plotted against Huan, and seized Chan. The territory of the Duke of Zhou stood perilously close to disintegration, beyond safeguarding. I see Zhu suffering the calamity of its ruler’s capture, while we face anxiety over our state’s peril. The predicament of the two towns cannot be called anything other than a sorrow we brought upon ourselves. The gentleman says: “It was not Qi that initiated the disaster. Lu’s opening of hostilities did something to bring it on.” Thus the Annals writes “brought along” and “seized.” Could the gravity of initiating wrongdoing require further argument?
After Zhu had suffered devastation and destruction, it no longer had any hope of recovering its state. Yet Duke Ai regretted his past fault, restored the ancestral sacrifices of Cao Shan [?], returned Zhu’s ruler, and secured peace in the east [?]. Was this not righteous? Thereupon Qi…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
人感悟讙闡見歸强力之邦章章乎歸于之疆
矣吾見邾有置君之幸我免失地之辱土宇之
復謂非自求之福不可也君子曰非齊之效順
魯之休復有以召之也故書曰歸而去惡之美
不從可見乎聖人脩經至此以爲逆以召逆昔
一哀也固將怙終之足虞者何意後之善反乎
然則内外交輸其情過以更而愈仰矣順以召
順今一哀也幸而息爭以見休者寧復向之爭
姦乎然則齊魯同歸於善惡以去而美彰矣歟
===
不諱入邾以邾子益來者以明歸益于邾之能
掩其前惡而美之也雖然魯之歸益怵於四鄰
之見謀果其悔心之萌乎二邑之歸季姬嬖請
之以來見善端之由衷也邾幸復國乃益底弗
類因而弗革更何望之至於樓臺之囚子華之
奉僭大權而擅廢立吳又適爲諸侯憂究而論
之無一可者聖人不得已而予歸邾之殺春秋
所以作乎
禮記
punctuated:
人感悟，讙闡見歸，强力之邦章章乎歸于之疆矣。吾見邾有置君之幸，我免失地之辱，土宇之復，謂非自求之福不可也。君子曰：「非齊之效順，魯之休復有以召之也。」故書曰「歸」，而去惡之美，不從可見乎？聖人脩經至此，以爲逆以召逆，昔一哀也，固將怙終之足虞者，何意後之善反乎？然則内外交輸其情，過以更而愈仰矣。順以召順，今一哀也，幸而息爭以見休者，寧復向之爭姦乎？然則齊魯同歸於善，惡以去而美彰矣歟！
不諱入邾、以邾子益來者，以明歸益于邾之能掩其前惡而美之也。雖然，魯之歸益，怵於四鄰之見謀，果其悔心之萌乎？二邑之歸，季姬嬖請之以來，見善端之由衷也。邾幸復國，乃益底弗類，因而弗革，更何望之？至於樓臺之囚、子華之奉，僭大權而擅廢立，吳又適爲諸侯憂。究而論之，無一可者。聖人不得已而予歸邾之殺，《春秋》所以作乎？
《禮記》
translation_en:
…the people of Qi came to their senses, and Huan and Chan were returned. That powerful state manifestly restored the territory [?]. I see that Zhu had the good fortune of having its ruler reinstated, while we escaped the disgrace of losing territory. The recovery of our lands cannot be called anything other than a blessing we secured for ourselves. The gentleman says: “It was not that Qi simply chose to act compliantly; Lu’s felicitous return to right conduct brought this about.” Thus the text says “returned”: can we not see therein the merit of abandoning evil [?]? When the Sage revised the Classic and reached this point, he considered how wrongdoing summoned wrongdoing. Duke Ai in those earlier days had indeed given cause to fear that he would persist in error to the end. Who could have expected his subsequent welcome change of course? Thus, as those within and beyond the state mutually disclosed their true intentions, his faults were corrected, and he became all the more worthy of esteem. Right conduct summons right conduct: this was still the same Duke Ai, now fortunate enough to end contention and attain a favorable outcome. Would he return to his former contentious wickedness? Thus Qi and Lu alike returned to goodness; evil was abandoned, and their merit became manifest!
The text does not conceal the invasion of Zhu and the bringing back of Yi, Viscount of Zhu. This makes clear that returning Yi to Zhu could redeem the earlier wrongdoing, and commends that act. Even so, Lu returned Yi because it feared the neighboring states’ designs against it: was this truly the budding of remorse? The return of the two towns came about through the entreaties of Ji Ji, a favored woman; this showed that the impulse toward goodness came from the heart [?]. Zhu was fortunate enough to have its state restored, yet Yi sank into misconduct and persisted without reform. What further hope could one place in him? As for the imprisonment in a tower and the installation of Zihua, Wu usurped supreme authority and arbitrarily deposed and installed rulers, thereby becoming a source of anxiety to the feudal lords. Examined to the end, none of these actions was acceptable. The Sage could only accord qualified approval to the return of the ruler to Zhu [?]. Was this why the Spring and Autumn Annals was composed?
Book of Rites

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
君子如欲化民成俗其必由學乎
郝桂芳
同考試官教諭曾　批〔當　王之治本於學此作理融詞達意惬氣暢蓋深造而有得者〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔說得化民成俗之意出〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔文有温藉宜冠多士〕
君子欲致天下之大治必本於天下之大道焉
夫明德新民道莫大焉者也君子欲化成天下
舍是其何以哉且夫天下之習尚係於民心民
===
心之淳漓風俗之所由以汙隆也民心之趨向
關於教化教化之淺深風治之所由以升降也
是故設聞者非所以感人動衆者不足以達化
以是言治隘矣君子如欲以大順為極功而鼓
舞盡神務納斯民於皇極以至治為良圖而神
化宜民期升斯世於大猷黎民欲其於變也而
時雍之風成焉遵道遵路必躋之有唐之盛而
后其心始慰矣百姓欲其昭明也而熙皞之俗
成焉會極歸極必媲之有虞之隆而后其願始
punctuated:
君子如欲化民成俗，其必由學乎？
郝桂芳
同考試官教諭曾　批〔當　王之治本於學，此作理融詞達，意惬氣暢，蓋深造而有得者。〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔說得化民成俗之意出。〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔文有温藉，宜冠多士。〕
君子欲致天下之大治，必本於天下之大道焉。夫明德新民，道莫大焉者也。君子欲化成天下，舍是其何以哉？且夫天下之習尚係於民心，民心之淳漓，風俗之所由以汙隆也。民心之趨向關於教化，教化之淺深，風治之所由以升降也。是故設聞者，非所以感人；動衆者，不足以達化。以是言治，隘矣。君子如欲以大順為極功，而鼓舞盡神，務納斯民於皇極；以至治為良圖，而神化宜民，期升斯世於大猷。黎民欲其於變也，而時雍之風成焉；遵道遵路，必躋之有唐之盛，而后其心始慰矣。百姓欲其昭明也，而熙皞之俗成焉；會極歸極，必媲之有虞之隆，而后其願始
translation_en:
“If the gentleman wishes to transform the people and establish good customs, must he not proceed through learning?”
Hao Guifang
Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: 〔The government of the king [?] is rooted in learning. This composition integrates its reasoning and expresses it lucidly; its meaning satisfies and its flow is unimpeded. It is surely the work of someone who has studied deeply and attained understanding.〕
Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔It brings out the meaning of transforming the people and establishing good customs.〕
Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔The writing possesses warmth and restraint, and deserves to rank first among the candidates.〕
If the gentleman wishes to bring about great order throughout the world, he must take the great Way of the world as his foundation. Manifesting luminous virtue and renewing the people—there is no Way greater than this. If the gentleman wishes to transform and perfect the world, how could he do so apart from this? Moreover, the habits and preferences of the world depend upon the hearts of the people. Whether those hearts are sincere or shallow determines whether customs decline or flourish. The direction taken by the people's hearts depends upon moral instruction; the shallowness or depth of that instruction determines the decline or advance of public morals and governance. Thus, setting forth things to be heard [?] is no means of moving people inwardly, and stirring the multitude is insufficient to achieve transformation. To speak of governing in these terms is narrow indeed.
If the gentleman wishes to make perfect accord his ultimate achievement, he must inspire and animate the people with consummate spiritual efficacy, striving to bring them within the sovereign's supreme standard. If he takes perfect government as his worthy design, he must transform the people with spiritual efficacy and provide suitably for them, hoping to raise this age to the great Way. He wishes the common people to be transformed, so that a spirit of harmony may prevail. Following the Way and its paths, he must bring them to the flourishing condition of Tang under Yao before his heart can find comfort. He wishes the hundred families to become luminously enlightened, so that customs of joyful simplicity may prevail. Gathering at the supreme standard and returning to it, he must bring them to match the prosperity of Yu under Shun before his aspiration can begin to …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
愜矣君子望治之心固如此其其殷也然果何
道可以致之哉亦曰由學焉耳蓋大學之道先
之明德帝王所以緼內聖之體而盡君師之責
者也推之新民帝王所以弘外王之用而大經
綸之業者也故由此而建極則道之大者其治
自神民則式和固治道之所從出也所謂格心
之化不言而喻者是已是設開不足言而豈慮
憲求賢之所能致哉由此而章軌則德之盛者
其化自光文教覃敷固風俗之所由同也所謂
===
神道之教不動而變者是已是動衆不足言而
豈就賢體遠之所可及哉吁學之所係如此君
人者誠建學以爲天下先民俗有不化成者哉
大抵帝王之世揖讓而天下治設爲庠序學校
至周始備其時人心淳厚民俗雍熙比家有道
之長由此其選也後世辟雍泮宮僅存文具倚
席不講則弁其法而廢之妄惑乎治之不若古
也噫有天下者可以鑒矣
樂極和禮極順內和而外順則民瞻其顏
punctuated:
愜矣。君子望治之心，固如此其其殷也。然果何道可以致之哉？亦曰由學焉耳。蓋大學之道，先之明德，帝王所以緼內聖之體而盡君師之責者也；推之新民，帝王所以弘外王之用而大經綸之業者也。故由此而建極，則道之大者，其治自神，民則式和，固治道之所從出也。所謂格心之化，不言而喻者，是已。是設開不足言，而豈慮憲求賢之所能致哉？由此而章軌，則德之盛者，其化自光，文教覃敷，固風俗之所由同也。所謂神道之教，不動而變者，是已。是動衆不足言，而豈就賢體遠之所可及哉？吁！學之所係如此，君人者誠建學以爲天下先，民俗有不化成者哉？大抵帝王之世，揖讓而天下治，設爲庠序學校，至周始備。其時人心淳厚，民俗雍熙，比家有道之長，由此其選也。後世辟雍泮宮，僅存文具，倚席不講，則弁其法而廢之，妄惑乎治之不若古也。噫！有天下者可以鑒矣。

樂極和，禮極順，內和而外順，則民瞻其顏
translation_en:
…is satisfied. Such indeed is the earnestness with which the gentleman hopes for good government. Yet by what way can it actually be achieved? The answer is simply through learning. The Way of the Great Learning begins with illuminating virtue: this is how emperors and kings cultivate the substance of inner sagehood and discharge their responsibilities as rulers and teachers. Extended to renewing the people, it is how emperors and kings broaden the operation of outward kingship and enlarge their work of ordering the realm. Thus, when they establish the supreme standard through learning, the greatness of their Way makes their government spontaneously wondrous, and the people become harmonious. This is indeed the source of the way of government. It is what is meant by transformation that reaches the heart and brings understanding without words. Mere institutional arrangements [?] are hardly worth mentioning; how could deliberating upon models and seeking worthy men [?] achieve this? When they make their guiding norms manifest through learning, the fullness of their virtue makes their transforming influence shine forth of itself. Civil instruction spreads everywhere: this is indeed how customs become uniform. It is what is meant by instruction through the numinous Way, bringing change without action. Merely stirring the multitude is hardly worth mentioning; how could drawing close to the worthy and showing solicitude for those far away attain this?

Ah! Such is the importance of learning. If the ruler truly establishes schools and thereby takes the lead for all under Heaven, could the people's customs fail to be transformed and perfected? In the age of the ancient emperors and kings, the realm was governed through deference and yielding. Schools of various kinds were established, but their system became complete only under the Zhou. At that time, people's hearts were sincere and generous, and popular customs harmonious and flourishing. Virtuous heads of neighborhood groups were selected through this system [?]. In later ages, the imperial and princely schools retained only empty formalities. Instruction from the teaching mat was neglected [?], their regulations were cast aside and abandoned, and people mistakenly wondered why government fell short of antiquity. Alas! Those who possess the realm may take warning from this.

Music brings harmony to its utmost; ritual brings compliance to its utmost. When there is harmony within and compliance without, the people look upon his countenance…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
色而弗與爭也望其容貌而民不生易
慢焉故德煇動於內而民莫不承聽理
發諸外而民莫不承順
王乾亨
同考試官教諭曾　批〔禮樂感人只是道理故作者往往難之子盡深於禮樂之旨者沖澹爾雅錄以爲式〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔宛然承聽承順氣象〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔瑩徹渾成佳士也〕
記者論君子於禮樂功極而化自神也夫本諸
===
身者必徵諸民也禮樂會中和之極德斯盛矣
化豈有不神者哉此記者論禮樂而極言之也
若曰君子修德固無責效之心而天下覩德自
有類應之化吾嘗有以觀其深矣何則樂動於
內以和爲至也君子以之治心則易直子諒之
生入於安久天神之妙性情融液殆無斯須之
不和矣禮動於外以順爲至也君子以之治躬
則莊敬嚴威之著黜乎鄙詐易慢之私儀則從
容殆無一毫之不順矣夫內和而外順則有以
punctuated:
色而弗與爭也，望其容貌而民不生易慢焉。故德煇動於內，而民莫不承聽；理發諸外，而民莫不承順。

王乾亨

同考試官教諭曾　批〔禮樂感人，只是道理，故作者往往難之。子盡深於禮樂之旨者，沖澹爾雅，錄以爲式。〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔宛然承聽承順氣象。〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔瑩徹渾成，佳士也。〕

記者論君子於禮樂功極，而化自神也。夫本諸身者，必徵諸民也。禮樂會中和之極，德斯盛矣，化豈有不神者哉？此記者論禮樂而極言之也。若曰：君子修德，固無責效之心，而天下覩德，自有類應之化。吾嘗有以觀其深矣。何則？樂動於內，以和爲至也。君子以之治心，則易直子諒之生，入於安久天神之妙，性情融液，殆無斯須之不和矣。禮動於外，以順爲至也。君子以之治躬，則莊敬嚴威之著，黜乎鄙詐易慢之私，儀則從容，殆無一毫之不順矣。夫內和而外順，則有以
translation_en:
…countenance and do not contend with him; they look upon his bearing, and no disrespect or arrogance arises among them. Thus, when the radiance of virtue stirs within, none among the people fails to heed him respectfully; when principle manifests itself outwardly, none fails to comply respectfully.

Wang Qianheng

Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor, comments: 〔Rites and music move people solely through moral principle, so writers often find this subject difficult. You have thoroughly penetrated the purport of rites and music [?]. Serene, restrained, and elegant: selected as a model.〕
Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔It vividly conveys the air of respectful heed and compliance.〕
Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔Luminous, lucid, and seamlessly composed—a fine scholar indeed.〕

The recorder argues that when the gentleman’s accomplishment in rites and music reaches its utmost, his transforming influence naturally becomes wondrous. What is rooted in his own person must find its verification among the people. When rites and music unite at the pinnacle of equilibrium and harmony, virtue flourishes to its fullest. How could its transforming influence fail to be wondrous? This is why the recorder, in discussing rites and music, carries his account to its furthest extent.

It is as though he were saying: The gentleman cultivates virtue without any thought of demanding results; yet when all under Heaven behold his virtue, a transformation naturally follows, as like responds to like. I have sought to discern the depth of this. Why is it so? Music stirs within, taking harmony as its highest attainment. The gentleman uses it to regulate his mind: ease, uprightness, kindness, and trustworthiness arise, entering the wondrous state of abiding tranquillity and heavenly spirituality [?]. His nature and feelings blend harmoniously, so that scarcely a moment passes without harmony. Rites operate outwardly, taking conformity as their highest attainment. The gentleman uses them to regulate his person: dignity, reverence, gravity, and majesty become manifest, banishing selfish impulses toward baseness, deceit, disrespect, and arrogance. His deportment accords effortlessly with proper standards, so that scarcely the slightest trace of nonconformity remains. With harmony within and conformity without, he thus has the means to…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
凝天地之命而備中和之紀君子之德於斯爲
盛矣其微諸民也何如哉但見生色之符一大
和之發也而民之得於瞻視者自啓夫揖遜之
風孰敢有與爭者乎容貌之動一顒若之觀也
而民之得於仰望者自肅夫欽承之念孰敢有
易慢者乎大曰不爭者非色莊而使民悅也英
華發於和順而德煇內動自有以服天下之心
焉以和召和蓋不令而民聽命矣致樂之化何
其神耶不生易慢者非作威而使民畏也周旋
===
妙於中禮而文章外見自有以懾天下之志焉
以順逵順蓋無爲而民歸極矣致禮之化何其
神耶吁禮樂之功用如此君子可以斯須去身
哉雖然此要其極耳而學者立禮和樂之功果
能一蹴至是歟觀之聖門求也遜而不居赤也
未能而願學四代禮樂惟顏子得聞之故曰不
聞性與天道而能制禮作樂者末矣彼綿蕞之
儀功德之舞逐末而忘本身心治道也何裨
第貳場
punctuated:
凝天地之命，而備中和之紀，君子之德於斯爲盛矣。其微諸民也何如哉？但見生色之符，一大和之發也，而民之得於瞻視者，自啓夫揖遜之風，孰敢有與爭者乎？容貌之動，一顒若之觀也，而民之得於仰望者，自肅夫欽承之念，孰敢有易慢者乎？大曰不爭者，非色莊而使民悅也。英華發於和順，而德煇內動，自有以服天下之心焉。以和召和，蓋不令而民聽命矣。致樂之化，何其神耶！不生易慢者，非作威而使民畏也。周旋妙於中禮，而文章外見，自有以懾天下之志焉。以順逵順，蓋無爲而民歸極矣。致禮之化，何其神耶！吁！禮樂之功用如此，君子可以斯須去身哉？雖然，此要其極耳，而學者立禮和樂之功，果能一蹴至是歟？觀之聖門，求也遜而不居，赤也未能而願學。四代禮樂，惟顏子得聞之。故曰：「不聞性與天道，而能制禮作樂者，末矣。」彼綿蕞之儀、功德之舞，逐末而忘本，身心治道也何裨？

第貳場
translation_en:
…to bring to fullness the mandate of Heaven and Earth and encompass the ordering principles of equilibrium and harmony: here the gentleman’s virtue reaches its height. How does it manifest itself among the people [?]? The vitality evident in his countenance is entirely an expression of supreme harmony. What the people gain from beholding it naturally awakens a disposition toward courtesy and deference. Who would dare contend with him? His bearing presents an entirely dignified appearance. What the people gain from looking up to him naturally makes their thoughts of reverent obedience more solemn. Who would dare show carelessness or contempt?

As for the statement that they do not contend [?], it is not through a solemn countenance that he makes the people pleased. His inner excellence blossoms in harmony and compliance, and the radiance of virtue stirs within; these naturally win the hearts of all under Heaven. Harmony calls forth harmony: without issuing commands, he has the people obey him. How wondrous is the transforming power of music brought to perfection! That no carelessness or contempt arises is not because he assumes an intimidating manner to make the people afraid. His every movement accords exquisitely with ritual, and its patterned beauty appears outwardly; these naturally awe the wills of all under Heaven. Through compliance he brings forth compliance [?]: without deliberate action, he has the people turn toward the supreme standard. How wondrous is the transforming power of ritual brought to perfection!

Ah! Since ritual and music have such efficacy, can the gentleman let them depart from his person for even a moment? Yet this merely sums up their ultimate achievement. Can students, through their efforts to establish themselves in ritual and attain harmony through music, really reach this point at a single bound? Consider the disciples of the Sage: Qiu was deferential and did not claim mastery; Chi professed himself incapable but wished to learn. Only Master Yan was privileged to hear about the ritual and music of the four dynasties. Thus it is said: “There has never been anyone who, without hearing of human nature and the Way of Heaven, could institute ritual and compose music.” Those ceremonies marked out with bundles of reeds and dances celebrating meritorious achievement pursue the branches and forget the root. What benefit do they offer to the cultivation of body and mind or the way of government [?]?

Second Session

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
論
人臣尊君之大
同考試官教諭丁　批　〔發意明盡措詞高古具得所以尊君之旨錄之〕
考試官教諭謝　批　〔詞不繁而意足〕
考試官教諭馮　批　〔宏博中有奇崛處〕
馮懋仁
論曰人臣之欲尊其君也無他焉亦曰以其所
難者望吾君而已矣夫人之情投其中之所溺
===
者易入而拂之以其情之所弗堪則拂徇其欲
之所趨者易合而道之以其力之所未易至焉
則阻諫也阻也在彼已之間猶或難之而吾為
人臣者又何樂乎拂與阻者以事吾君犯其中
之所諱而長其所不欲哉曰不如是不足以尊
吾君不如是不足以塞吾事君者之責而吾徇
君之名終無以自解於天下後世故寧拂也阻
也以其所難者望吾君而吾亦為其難以成吾
尊君之大而已矣范氏曰人臣尊君之大蓋所
punctuated:
論
人臣尊君之大
同考試官教諭丁　批　〔發意明盡，措詞高古，具得所以尊君之旨，錄之。〕
考試官教諭謝　批　〔詞不繁而意足。〕
考試官教諭馮　批　〔宏博中有奇崛處。〕
馮懋仁
論曰：人臣之欲尊其君也，無他焉，亦曰以其所難者望吾君而已矣。夫人之情，投其中之所溺者易入，而拂之以其情之所弗堪則拂；徇其欲之所趨者易合，而道之以其力之所未易至焉則阻。諫也，阻也，在彼已之間，猶或難之，而吾為人臣者，又何樂乎拂與阻者以事吾君，犯其中之所諱，而長其所不欲哉？曰：不如是，不足以尊吾君；不如是，不足以塞吾事君者之責，而吾徇君之名，終無以自解於天下後世。故寧拂也，阻也，以其所難者望吾君，而吾亦為其難，以成吾尊君之大而已矣。范氏曰：「人臣尊君之大」，蓋所
translation_en:
Discourse
The Highest Form of a Minister’s Honoring His Ruler

Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor, comments: 〔The ideas are expressed clearly and fully, and the diction is elevated and antique. It fully grasps the purport of how to honor the ruler. Selected for inclusion.〕
Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔The wording is concise, yet the meaning is complete.〕
Examiner Feng, Instructor, comments: 〔Within its breadth and comprehensiveness are passages of striking originality.〕

Feng Maoren

The discourse reads: A minister who wishes to honor his ruler has no other means than to expect of his ruler what is difficult for him. Such is human nature: words that cater to what someone inwardly indulges in readily find acceptance, but confronting him with what his feelings cannot bear provokes resistance. Complying with the direction of his desires readily wins agreement, but guiding him toward what his abilities cannot easily attain meets obstruction. Remonstrance [?] and obstruction are sometimes considered difficult enough even in dealings between oneself and another. Why, then, should I, as a minister, willingly serve my ruler through confrontation and obstruction, offending his inward aversions and fostering what he does not desire?

I reply: Unless I do so, I cannot adequately honor my ruler; unless I do so, I cannot discharge my responsibility in serving him. And I would ultimately have no way to clear myself before the world and posterity of the reputation of having pandered to my ruler. Thus I would rather confront him and encounter obstruction, expecting of him what is difficult, while also undertaking what is difficult myself, solely to fulfill the highest form of honoring my ruler. Master Fan spoke of “the highest form of a minister’s honoring his ruler”; this was intended to…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
以發孟子責難於君謂之恭之旨而以責難之
義望天下後世之爲人臣者予請得而申言之
禮有之曰天尊地卑君臣定矣書曰元后作民
父母曰天生下民作之君春秋繫王於天秦漢
以來事屬君則稱天君之尊也自古記之矣世
之爲人臣者孰不欲尊其君而所以尊其君者
豈不謂奔走捷給奉吾君爲尊巽順觀望徇吾
君爲尊迎合將承悅吾君爲尊哉殊不知爲之
衮冕以象天也越席錯衡以養安也寢兕持虎
===
彌龍以養威也是綿蕞之尊也夾道旁趨磬折
傴僂視息臣細惟所欲而畢致之是寺人之尊
也道之土木之役誘之輿馬之觀而誇之以封
石狼居胥之北是儉壬便佞之尊也其甚也欲
日益固而不可遏心日益驕而不可解政日益
非而不可回則桀紂其君而已矣幽厲其君而
已矣桓靈其君而已矣則亦何望於其臣也說
命曰若金汝作礪曰木從繩則直后從諫則聖
人臣尊君之大謂非以其所難者事吾君哉天
punctuated: 以發孟子「責難於君謂之恭」之旨，而以責難之義望天下後世之爲人臣者。予請得而申言之。禮有之曰：「天尊地卑，君臣定矣。」書曰：「元后作民父母。」曰：「天生下民，作之君。」春秋繫王於天。秦漢以來，事屬君則稱天。君之尊也，自古記之矣。世之爲人臣者，孰不欲尊其君？而所以尊其君者，豈不謂奔走捷給，奉吾君爲尊；巽順觀望，徇吾君爲尊；迎合將承，悅吾君爲尊哉？殊不知爲之衮冕以象天也，越席錯衡以養安也，寢兕持虎彌龍以養威也，是綿蕞之尊也；夾道旁趨，磬折傴僂，視息臣細，惟所欲而畢致之，是寺人之尊也；道之土木之役，誘之輿馬之觀，而誇之以封石狼居胥之北，是儉壬便佞之尊也。其甚也，欲日益固而不可遏，心日益驕而不可解，政日益非而不可回，則桀紂其君而已矣，幽厲其君而已矣，桓靈其君而已矣，則亦何望於其臣也？《說命》曰：「若金，汝作礪。」曰：「木從繩則直，后從諫則聖。」人臣尊君之大，謂非以其所難者事吾君哉？天
translation_en:
…serves to elucidate Mencius’s meaning in saying, “To demand difficult things of one’s ruler is called reverence,” and, through this principle, to set expectations for all who serve as ministers throughout the world and in later ages. Allow me to elaborate upon it.

The Book of Rites says: “Heaven is exalted and earth is lowly; the positions of ruler and minister are thereby established.” The Book of Documents says: “The sovereign acts as father and mother to the people.” It also says: “Heaven gave birth to the people below and established rulers for them.” The Spring and Autumn Annals connects the king with Heaven. Since the Qin and Han dynasties, matters pertaining to the ruler have been termed “heavenly.” The exalted status of the ruler has been recorded since antiquity.

Who among the world’s ministers does not wish to honor his ruler? Yet do they not suppose that honoring him means hurrying about and responding promptly in his service; being submissive, watching for his wishes, and complying with them; anticipating his desires, accommodating him, and pleasing him? They fail to understand that providing ceremonial robes and a crown to symbolize Heaven, rush mats and an ornamented carriage crossbar to nurture his ease, and reclining rhinoceros, standing tiger, and extended dragon ornaments [?] to nurture his majesty amounts merely to the honor afforded through ceremonial arrangements. Hurrying along either side of his path, bending like a musical stone and stooping low, attending minutely to his looks and breathing [?], and supplying everything he desires amounts merely to the honor afforded by palace eunuchs. Leading him into construction projects, enticing him with displays of carriages and horses, and boasting to him of erecting an inscribed stone north of Langjuxu amounts merely to the honor afforded by crafty flatterers [?].

At its worst, his desires grow daily more entrenched and cannot be restrained; his heart grows daily more arrogant and cannot be freed of its arrogance; his government grows daily more misguided and cannot be turned back. This merely makes one’s ruler into a Jie or Zhou, a You or Li, a Huan or Ling. What, then, can be expected of his ministers?

The “Charge to Yue” says: “If I am metal, you shall be the whetstone.” It also says: “Wood following the marking line becomes straight; a sovereign following remonstrance becomes a sage.” Can the greatest way for a minister to honor his ruler be anything other than serving him by demanding what he finds difficult? All under Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
下之事毀之易成之難人之情順之易逆之難
責人以難固其中之所弗堪而其情之所未易
入者也是故起居宴息君所習也而曰雞鳴視
朝日夕脩令則難矣肅肅宵征君所適也而曰
御見請期彤管載事則難矣宮室飲食君所安
也而曰茅茨土階損膳徹御則難矣莫難制如
欲心而約之使窒莫難降如驕心而強之使平
莫難忍如怒心而抑之使釋莫難辨如惑心而
開之使悟天下已定刑政已明而曰卑章於變
===
何以不如堯舜稽衆表正何以不若夏商如傷
敷佑何以不若文武求思刑措何以不若成康
則雖望治之主謙讓未遑而吾寧拂也閉以
事吾君者何哉此其心欲吾君為唐虞夏商為
文武成康使後之視吾君亦猶今之視唐虞夏
商視文武成康一人之唯唯孰與萬民之熙熙
一時之依違孰與萬世之瞻仰而吾尊君之心
始無一之不盡而為臣不易之責始足以自解
於天下後世如其不以道順之而已不以難約
punctuated: 下之事，毀之易，成之難；人之情，順之易，逆之難。責人以難，固其中之所弗堪，而其情之所未易入者也。是故起居宴息，君所習也，而曰雞鳴視朝，日夕脩令，則難矣；肅肅宵征，君所適也，而曰御見請期，彤管載事，則難矣；宮室飲食，君所安也，而曰茅茨土階，損膳徹御，則難矣。莫難制如欲心，而約之使窒；莫難降如驕心，而強之使平；莫難忍如怒心，而抑之使釋；莫難辨如惑心，而開之使悟。天下已定，刑政已明，而曰：「卑章於變，何以不如堯舜？稽衆表正，何以不若夏商？如傷敷佑，何以不若文武？求思刑措，何以不若成康？」則雖望治之主，謙讓未遑，而吾寧拂也閉以事吾君者，何哉？此其心欲吾君為唐虞夏商，為文武成康，使後之視吾君，亦猶今之視唐虞夏商、視文武成康。一人之唯唯，孰與萬民之熙熙？一時之依違，孰與萬世之瞻仰？而吾尊君之心，始無一之不盡，而為臣不易之責，始足以自解於天下後世。如其不以道順之而已，不以難約
translation_en:
…In the affairs of the world, destruction is easy and accomplishment difficult; with human feelings, compliance is easy and opposition difficult. To demand difficult things of someone is indeed to demand what he cannot bear inwardly and what his feelings do not readily admit. Thus, a ruler is accustomed to his daily routines and leisurely repose; yet to tell him to hold court at cockcrow and attend to his commands morning and evening is difficult. Going forth quietly by night is to his liking; yet to require that attendance upon him be scheduled and that events be recorded with the vermilion brush is difficult. Palaces, food, and drink give him comfort; yet to prescribe thatched roofs and earthen steps, reduced meals, and the withdrawal of his attendants is difficult. Nothing is harder to restrain than desire, yet one must curb it until it is checked; nothing harder to bring low than pride, yet one must compel it to become even-tempered; nothing harder to contain than anger, yet one must repress it until it dissolves; nothing harder to clarify than a deluded mind, yet one must enlighten it until it understands.

Though the realm is already settled and punishments and government already well ordered, one still asks: “In humbly ordering affairs [?] and transforming the people, why do you fall short of Yao and Shun? In consulting the multitude and setting an upright example, why do you fall short of Xia and Shang? In caring for the people as though they were injured and extending protection to them, why do you fall short of Kings Wen and Wu? In seeking good government until punishments can be set aside, why do you fall short of Kings Cheng and Kang?” Even a ruler who aspires to good government would scarcely have time to respond with humility. Why, then, do I prefer to offend him and thus serve my ruler [?]? It is because my heart desires that my ruler become like the sovereigns of Tang, Yu, Xia, and Shang, and like Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, so that later generations will regard him as we now regard those sovereigns and kings. How can saying “yes, yes” to one man compare with bringing joy to the myriad people? How can temporizing for a time compare with receiving the reverence of ten thousand generations? Only then will my desire to honor my ruler be fulfilled in every respect; only then can I adequately discharge, before the world and posterity, the difficult responsibility of being a minister. But if one merely complies with him without guiding him by the Way, and fails to restrain him through difficult demands…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之而已不以其所不能而從之而已是謂吾君
不可與於古先哲王之盛而吾之心已不免薄
視其君謂天下何謂後世何謂之不已縱欲敗
度遠賢棄民使天下後世謂吾君爲何如主如
是而爲徇其君乎尊其君乎夫是以進而不顧
其安强而不恤其所不欲吾非樂爲此也將以
免穪吾之所不敢不盡者也是故同一漢武矣
有以堯湯水旱之說進者有以內多欲而外施
仁義之說進者謂徇之也者尊之也則黯之尊
===
漢武不如弘矣同一貞觀也有於所愛樹則譽
之者有謂漸不克終者謂阿之也者尊之也則
徵之尊太宗不如宇文士及矣夫君爲堯舜則
吾爲臯陶稷契君爲夏商則吾爲伯益伊尹君
爲文武成康則吾爲呂望周召故爲折檻爲引
裾爲毀麻爲却座蓋其責誠有所不容諉其心
誠有所托而不敢以阿且易者效之吾君也嗚
呼自有君臣以來臣之所以尊其君者孰有大
於責難哉雖然責難尊君固也然要之貴於誠
punctuated:
之而已，不以其所不能而從之而已，是謂吾君不可與於古先哲王之盛，而吾之心已不免薄視其君。謂天下何？謂後世何？謂之不已，縱欲敗度，遠賢棄民，使天下後世謂吾君爲何如主？如是而爲徇其君乎？尊其君乎？夫是以進而不顧其安，强而不恤其所不欲。吾非樂爲此也，將以免穪吾之所不敢不盡者也。
是故同一漢武矣，有以堯湯水旱之說進者，有以內多欲而外施仁義之說進者。謂徇之也者尊之也，則黯之尊漢武不如弘矣。同一貞觀也，有於所愛樹則譽之者，有謂漸不克終者。謂阿之也者尊之也，則徵之尊太宗不如宇文士及矣。
夫君爲堯舜，則吾爲臯陶稷契；君爲夏商，則吾爲伯益伊尹；君爲文武成康，則吾爲呂望周召。故爲折檻，爲引裾，爲毀麻，爲却座，蓋其責誠有所不容諉，其心誠有所托，而不敢以阿且易者效之吾君也。嗚呼！自有君臣以來，臣之所以尊其君者，孰有大於責難哉？雖然，責難尊君固也，然要之貴於誠
translation_en:
…him, and leave it at that; merely accommodate him on the grounds of what he cannot do, and leave it at that. This amounts to saying that our ruler cannot share in the greatness of the wise kings of antiquity: in our hearts we already cannot avoid holding our ruler in low regard. What can we say to the world? What can we say to posterity? If we persist in saying this, indulging his desires and subverting proper standards, distancing the worthy and abandoning the people, what sort of sovereign will we cause the world and posterity to consider our ruler? Is acting thus indulging one’s ruler, or honoring him? This is why we advance our admonitions without regard for his ease, and press him without concern for his unwillingness. I do not delight in doing this; I seek thereby to discharge what I dare not leave unfulfilled [?].
Thus, under the very same Emperor Wu of Han, one man advanced the argument about the floods and droughts in the days of Yao and Tang; another advanced the criticism that the emperor inwardly harbored many desires while outwardly practicing benevolence and righteousness. If indulging a ruler means honoring him, then Ji An honored Emperor Wu less than Gongsun Hong did. Likewise, in the very same Zhenguan reign, one man praised a tree because the emperor loved it; another said that the emperor was gradually failing to carry his good beginnings through to the end. If flattering a ruler means honoring him, then Wei Zheng honored Taizong less than Yuwen Shiji did.
If our ruler becomes a Yao or Shun, then we become Gao Yao, Ji, and Xie; if our ruler becomes like the rulers of Xia and Shang, then we become Bo Yi and Yi Yin; if our ruler becomes like Kings Wen, Wu, Cheng, and Kang, then we become Lü Wang and the Dukes of Zhou and Shao. Hence there were those who broke a balustrade, tugged at the ruler’s robe, destroyed the hemp-paper edict, or pushed back a seat. Their responsibilities truly admitted of no evasion, and their hearts truly had a commitment: they dared not serve our ruler with flattery and easy acquiescence. Alas! Ever since rulers and ministers first existed, what means by which a minister honors his ruler has been greater than demanding difficult things of him? Nevertheless, although demanding difficult things of a ruler certainly honors him, what ultimately matters is sincerity…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而已矣使吾尊君之心出於至誠而不容已則
脩之家壞之天子之廷不敢爲也而則從退而
后言不忍爲也忠信以感通之盡力以維持之
優游而善導之朝夕而敬進之則其言未有不
入君心未有不悟始也責之以難終也將不苦
於其難者矣若吾之心不出於誠而徒自附於
責難之義以或吾觽觽之名或失則亢或失則
激或失則迂入君之義無當也故夫子曰臣事
君以忠
===
郝桂芳
同考試官司訓會 批〔以帝王望其君正人臣責難於君之心此作發揮得出宜錄〕
考試官教諭謝 批〔即子所論蓋亦知尊君之大者〕
考試官教諭馬 批〔氣象可觀〕
同前
古之所謂大臣者以天道事其君則其尊君也
如尊天而未可以世俗之尊君者例論矣何者
帝王之道天道也帝王以天道治天下吾而責
punctuated:
而已矣。使吾尊君之心出於至誠而不容已，則脩之家，壞之天子之廷，不敢爲也；而則從，退而后言，不忍爲也。忠信以感通之，盡力以維持之，優游而善導之，朝夕而敬進之，則其言未有不入，君心未有不悟。始也責之以難，終也將不苦於其難者矣。若吾之心不出於誠，而徒自附於責難之義，以或吾觽觽之名，或失則亢，或失則激，或失則迂，入君之義無當也。故夫子曰：「臣事君以忠。」

郝桂芳
同考試官司訓會批〔以帝王望其君，正人臣責難於君之心，此作發揮得出，宜錄。〕
考試官教諭謝批〔即子所論，蓋亦知尊君之大者。〕
考試官教諭馬批〔氣象可觀。〕

同前
古之所謂大臣者，以天道事其君，則其尊君也如尊天，而未可以世俗之尊君者例論矣。何者？帝王之道，天道也。帝王以天道治天下，吾而責
translation_en:
…and nothing more. If my desire to honor my ruler proceeds from the utmost sincerity and cannot be restrained, I would not dare cultivate something at home only to destroy it at the Son of Heaven’s court; nor could I bear to comply in his presence [?] and speak only after withdrawing. Through loyalty and trustworthiness I would move him and establish understanding; with all my strength I would sustain him; patiently and gently I would guide him well; morning and evening I would respectfully offer counsel. Then my words would invariably find acceptance, and the ruler’s mind would invariably awaken to understanding. Although at first I would require difficult things of him, in the end he would no longer find those difficulties burdensome. If, however, my heart does not proceed from sincerity, and I merely associate myself with the principle of requiring difficult things of the ruler in order to obtain a reputation for myself [?], my failings may take the form of overbearing conduct, excessive vehemence, or impracticality. This would not accord with the duty of guiding the ruler [?]. Thus the Master said: “A minister serves his ruler with loyalty.”

Hao Guifang
Associate Examiner Hui, an Assistant Instructor, comments: “To expect one’s ruler to equal the sage emperors and kings is precisely the intention with which a minister requires difficult things of his ruler. This composition brings that out successfully and merits inclusion.”
Examiner Xie, an Instructor, comments: “Judging from what you have argued, you indeed understand the greater meaning of honoring the ruler.”
Examiner Ma, an Instructor, comments: “Its overall bearing is impressive.”

Same topic as above
Those whom the ancients called great ministers served their rulers according to the Way of Heaven. They therefore honored their rulers as they honored Heaven, and cannot be discussed on the same terms as those who honor rulers in the conventional worldly manner. Why is this? The Way of the sage emperors and kings is the Way of Heaven. The sage emperors and kings governed all under Heaven according to the Way of Heaven. If I require…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
其君治天下以帝王之道則是舉其君於帝王
之隆而事其君以天道之尊雖其君自以爲難
而畏之因有所忌於其中而拂於其外吾寧犯
其所忌値其所拂而必以帝王之道責之此其
心何心哉惟欲使其君爲帝王而尊其君以天
道而后吾無所解於其心之義始盡無所逃於
天地之分始畢庶無愧於尊君如尊天之道而
與世俗之尊君者遠矣不然徒諛之曰君人者
之情每樂趨於其易而難是以太難中村之主
===
皆有所拂堪於是姑遷就焉以從其所欲吾見
本以樂易之情而秉以遷就之說則君日趨其
所易而日苦其所難帝王之道不復見於後世
者未必皆君人者之過而吾亦甚與有責焉耳
矣此豈國家之福哉蓋至是而后知大臣之所
以事君者必責之以甚難而後見其心之忠必
事之以天道而后見其尊之大彼世之所謂尊
君者祇見其卑焉耳矣孟子曰責難於君謂之
恭而范氏釋之曰此人臣尊君之大其善論臣
punctuated: 其君治天下以帝王之道，則是舉其君於帝王之隆，而事其君以天道之尊。雖其君自以爲難而畏之，因有所忌於其中而拂於其外，吾寧犯其所忌，値其所拂，而必以帝王之道責之。此其心何心哉？惟欲使其君爲帝王，而尊其君以天道，而后吾無所解於其心之義始盡，無所逃於天地之分始畢，庶無愧於尊君如尊天之道，而與世俗之尊君者遠矣。不然，徒諛之曰：「君人者之情，每樂趨於其易，而難是以太難，中村之主皆有所拂堪，於是姑遷就焉，以從其所欲。」吾見本以樂易之情，而秉以遷就之說，則君日趨其所易，而日苦其所難。帝王之道不復見於後世者，未必皆君人者之過，而吾亦甚與有責焉耳矣。此豈國家之福哉？蓋至是而后知大臣之所以事君者，必責之以甚難而後見其心之忠，必事之以天道而后見其尊之大。彼世之所謂尊君者，祇見其卑焉耳矣。孟子曰：「責難於君謂之恭。」而范氏釋之曰：「此人臣尊君之大。」其善論臣
translation_en:
…his ruler to govern the realm by the Way of the ancient emperors and kings, then he raises his ruler to their exalted stature and serves him with the reverence due to the Way of Heaven. Even if his ruler considers this difficult and fears it, inwardly harboring aversion and outwardly resisting, I would rather offend against his aversions and encounter his resistance, and insist on demanding that he follow the Way of the emperors and kings. What intention lies behind this? It is solely the desire to make his ruler an emperor or king of antiquity and to honor him according to the Way of Heaven. Only then can I fully discharge the moral obligation from which my heart cannot be released, and fulfill the duty that I cannot escape between Heaven and Earth. Thus I may be without shame in honoring my ruler as I honor Heaven, far removed from those who honor their rulers in the conventional manner.

Otherwise, one merely flatters him, saying: “Rulers are naturally inclined to take pleasure in pursuing what is easy; as for difficulty, it is considered too difficult, and rulers of middling ability [?] all find something they resist [?]. For now, therefore, let us accommodate them and follow their desires.” I see that when a natural liking for ease is reinforced by arguments for accommodation, the ruler increasingly pursues what is easy and increasingly finds what is difficult burdensome. That the Way of the emperors and kings is no longer seen in later ages is not necessarily entirely the fault of rulers: I too bear a substantial share of responsibility. How could this bring good fortune to the state?

Only at this point do we understand how a great minister serves his ruler: he must demand of him what is exceedingly difficult before the loyalty of his heart becomes apparent; he must serve him according to the Way of Heaven before the greatness of his reverence becomes apparent. What the world calls honoring the ruler reveals only its own baseness. Mencius said: “To demand difficult things of one’s ruler is called reverence.” Master Fan explained this by saying: “This is the highest form of a minister’s honoring his ruler.” How well he discusses the minister’s…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
道而立萬世之凖者哉請竟其說夫君臣之間
其相知以心其相濟而相成也以道是道也即
君臣之極盡乎人而合諸天者也盡斯道者惟
唐虞三代當是時其君神聖其治熙皡君臣上
下遊乎其天粹乎無以議而皐夔稷契伊傅之
徒猶有謨誥之訓戒命之篇吁咈俞嗟日皇皇
焉以勑其君必欲其君之若乎天而君之聽之
亦拱受而不疑敢爲而不替惟恐其有面從後
言之意所以致治之隆萬古莫及君臣之相成
===
以天道固如此也惟中才之主其患每恃其所
長而狃於其所快夫恃其所長則其智易逞狃
於其所快則其情易溺以易溺之情而附之以
易逞之智是故樂自是而惡至言喜道諛而憚
蹇諤臣又伺君之意迎其機而諛之售其所喜
而不責其所難故君得以惟其所欲爲而不聞
其過天下之治日替而不可挽此未必盡其君
之責亦臣之自拂其天道者有以成之也噫有
臣若此亦何取於臣哉且天下之臣不同固有
punctuated:
道而立萬世之凖者哉！請竟其說。夫君臣之間，其相知以心，其相濟而相成也以道。是道也，即君臣之極，盡乎人而合諸天者也。盡斯道者，惟唐虞三代。當是時，其君神聖，其治熙皡，君臣上下遊乎其天，粹乎無以議，而皐夔稷契伊傅之徒，猶有謨誥之訓、戒命之篇，吁咈俞嗟，日皇皇焉以勑其君，必欲其君之若乎天。而君之聽之，亦拱受而不疑，敢爲而不替，惟恐其有面從後言之意。所以致治之隆，萬古莫及。君臣之相成以天道，固如此也。
惟中才之主，其患每恃其所長而狃於其所快。夫恃其所長，則其智易逞；狃於其所快，則其情易溺。以易溺之情，而附之以易逞之智，是故樂自是而惡至言，喜道諛而憚蹇諤。臣又伺君之意，迎其機而諛之，售其所喜而不責其所難，故君得以惟其所欲爲而不聞其過，天下之治日替而不可挽。此未必盡其君之責，亦臣之自拂其天道者有以成之也。噫！有臣若此，亦何取於臣哉？且天下之臣不同，固有
translation_en:
…the way of the minister, establishing a standard for all ages—how well he has discussed it! Let me bring this explanation to its conclusion. Between ruler and minister, mutual understanding comes through the heart; mutual assistance and fulfillment come through the Way. This Way is the highest standard for ruler and minister: fully realizing what is human and according with Heaven. Only in the ages of Tang and Yu and the Three Dynasties was this Way fully realized. At that time, rulers were sagely and divinely wise, and their government was radiant and harmonious. Ruler and ministers, high and low, moved freely within their Heaven-given nature, so pure as to admit no criticism. Yet men such as Gao Yao, Kui, Ji, Xie, Yi Yin, and Fu Yue still offered instruction in counsels and proclamations, admonitions and charges. With exclamations of dissent and assent, they earnestly urged their rulers on each day, determined that their rulers should accord with Heaven. In listening to them, rulers likewise received their words respectfully and without doubt, acted boldly and without slackening, and feared only that their ministers might acquiesce to their faces while speaking otherwise behind their backs. Thus they brought government to a height unmatched through all the ages. Such, indeed, was the way ruler and ministers fulfilled one another through the Way of Heaven.
As for rulers of middling ability, their failing commonly lies in relying on their strengths and becoming habituated to what pleases them. Relying on their strengths, they readily give free rein to their cleverness; habituated to what pleases them, they readily become immersed in their desires. When desires so easily indulged are joined to cleverness so readily given free rein, they delight in considering themselves right and detest forthright counsel; they welcome flattering words and shrink from unbending remonstrance. Their ministers, moreover, watch for their intentions, anticipate their impulses and flatter them, plying them with what they enjoy rather than demanding what they find difficult. The ruler can therefore do whatever he wishes without hearing of his faults, while the government of the realm deteriorates daily beyond recovery. This is not necessarily entirely the ruler’s responsibility: ministers who themselves act against the Way of Heaven also help bring it about. Alas! With ministers such as these, what use is there in having ministers at all? Furthermore, the ministers of the realm are not all alike. There are certainly those who…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
受國委任出力效績令主有成功而毀譽利害
身任之而百不一恤則猷幹之臣有任繁劇肩
鉅重臨患難常則經施變則權濟一意奮往必
於就天下之事而不及顧則忠悃之臣至於涖
一官善一職因事效能無越位之思無瘝曠之
責者則奉公之臣此三臣者志在爲君有裨於
國皆於臣道無負然而大臣所以尊君之道固
不在是何者人君天下之本而正君者萬化之
原也故曰人不足適也政不足間也惟大人爲
===
能格君心之非大人者即所謂大臣是也大臣
非不欲悅君之心以行吾之言顧君之所付托
於我者至大而吾之所以期望其君者不可若
是小也帝王之奉若天道者至尊而吾之所以
奉若其君者不可若是卑也必思其君所以若
時齊政奠山濬川經緯天地者未能也則有勅
天之戒所以生穀奠居明刑敷敎保釐民心者
未能也則有安民之訓所以亮功考績黜幽陟
明進退百官者未能也則有知人之告所以立
punctuated:
受國委任，出力效績，令主有成功，而毀譽利害，身任之而百不一恤，則猷幹之臣；有任繁劇、肩鉅重、臨患難，常則經施，變則權濟，一意奮往，必於就天下之事而不及顧，則忠悃之臣；至於涖一官、善一職，因事效能，無越位之思，無瘝曠之責者，則奉公之臣。此三臣者，志在爲君，有裨於國，皆於臣道無負。然而大臣所以尊君之道，固不在是。何者？人君天下之本，而正君者萬化之原也。故曰：「人不足適也，政不足間也，惟大人爲能格君心之非。」大人者，即所謂大臣是也。
大臣非不欲悅君之心，以行吾之言，顧君之所付托於我者至大，而吾之所以期望其君者，不可若是小也。帝王之奉若天道者至尊，而吾之所以奉若其君者，不可若是卑也。必思其君所以若時齊政、奠山濬川、經緯天地者未能也，則有勅天之戒；所以生穀奠居、明刑敷敎、保釐民心者未能也，則有安民之訓；所以亮功考績、黜幽陟明、進退百官者未能也，則有知人之告；所以立
translation_en:
…those who accept the state's commission, exert themselves and achieve results, enabling their ruler to accomplish his work, while personally bearing blame and praise, benefit and harm, without giving any of these a thought: these are ministers of resourcefulness and ability. There are those who undertake complex and demanding duties, shoulder immense responsibilities, and confront danger and hardship; in ordinary circumstances they act according to established principles, and in changed circumstances they respond with expedient measures. Advancing with undivided resolve, they insist on bringing the affairs of the realm to completion, with no time to look to themselves: these are ministers of devoted loyalty. As for those who hold an office and discharge its duties well, demonstrating their ability as matters arise, neither contemplating encroachment upon another's position nor incurring blame for neglecting their own duties: these are ministers who serve the public good. These three kinds of ministers aspire to serve their ruler and benefit the state; none fails in the duties of a minister. Yet the way in which a great minister exalts his ruler does not, fundamentally, lie here. Why? The ruler is the foundation of the realm, and rectifying the ruler is the source of all transforming influence. Thus it is said: “It is not enough to criticize those employed, nor enough to find fault with policies. Only a great man can rectify what is wrong in the ruler's heart.” This “great man” is precisely what we call a great minister.
It is not that a great minister does not wish to please his ruler's heart so that his own counsel may be put into practice. Rather, what the ruler has entrusted to him is supremely great, and his expectations of his ruler cannot be so small. Emperors and kings, in reverently following the Way of Heaven, pursue the loftiest standard; the standard by which he reverently serves and follows his ruler cannot be so low. He must consider whether his ruler has yet succeeded in following the seasons and ordering government, securing the mountains and dredging the rivers, and bringing Heaven and Earth into order. If not, there must be admonitions to heed Heaven. If his ruler has yet to succeed in fostering grain production and securing the people's dwellings, clarifying punishments and spreading instruction, and safeguarding and ordering the people's hearts, there must be instruction on bringing peace to the people. If his ruler has yet to succeed in assisting their work and assessing their achievements, dismissing the unworthy and promoting the worthy, and advancing or removing the officials, there must be counsel on discerning men. As for the means by which he establishes…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
綱陳紀渙令布信總理萬幾者未能也則有兢
業之譽所以奉辭舞干昭德懷遠制禦戎狄者
未能也則有猾夏之喻此數者皆堯舜治天下
之道而吾君未能是堯舜以天道治天下而吾
弗克俾厥后爲堯舜則吾爲臣者之過也吾心
之未盡吾責之未塞吾懼焉君不堯舜治不唐
虞吾愚焉故所以開陳於前而匡其不逮者雖
苦鯁之言批鱗之諫君之意所不樂聞吾之力
所不能堪而吾之言則不容以不盡也吾惟知
===
有帝王其君而已吾惟知有天道事君而已此
大臣之心也推其心必欲吾君爲天之宗子爲
民之父母爲明哲聖神之主爲中國聖人之頌
與堯舜湯文竝軌方烈而後其願始畢則其尊
君也如尊天而世之所謂尊君者孰有大於此
哉孟子他日黜容悅小社稷之臣而獨有取於
大人正己而物正孔子亦曰所謂大臣者以道
事君孔孟之言一也觀其於魯哀衛靈齊宣梁
惠雖春秋戰國之庸君而仁義禮樂之道執極
punctuated: 綱陳紀，渙令布信，總理萬幾者未能也，則有兢業之譽；所以奉辭舞干，昭德懷遠，制禦戎狄者未能也，則有猾夏之喻。此數者，皆堯舜治天下之道，而吾君未能。是堯舜以天道治天下，而吾弗克俾厥后爲堯舜，則吾爲臣者之過也。吾心之未盡，吾責之未塞，吾懼焉；君不堯舜，治不唐虞，吾愚焉。故所以開陳於前而匡其不逮者，雖苦鯁之言、批鱗之諫，君之意所不樂聞，吾之力所不能堪，而吾之言則不容以不盡也。吾惟知有帝王其君而已，吾惟知有天道事君而已。此大臣之心也。推其心，必欲吾君爲天之宗子，爲民之父母，爲明哲聖神之主，爲中國聖人之頌，與堯舜湯文竝軌方烈，而後其願始畢。則其尊君也如尊天，而世之所謂尊君者，孰有大於此哉？孟子他日黜容悅、小社稷之臣，而獨有取於大人正己而物正。孔子亦曰：「所謂大臣者，以道事君。」孔孟之言一也。觀其於魯哀、衛靈、齊宣、梁惠，雖春秋戰國之庸君，而仁義禮樂之道，執極
translation_en:
…establishing guiding principles and setting out regulations, issuing commands and making good faith manifest, and overseeing the myriad affairs of government: when the ruler falls short in these, there is praise of vigilance and diligence. When he falls short in carrying out punitive commands and performing the shield dance, displaying virtue and winning over distant peoples, and controlling the Rong and Di, there is the admonition concerning their disturbance of the Chinese realm. These are all ways by which Yao and Shun governed All under Heaven, yet our ruler has not attained them. Yao and Shun governed All under Heaven according to the Way of Heaven; if I cannot enable my sovereign to become a Yao or Shun, then the fault lies with me as his minister. I fear that I have not fully devoted my heart or discharged my responsibility. If my ruler is no Yao or Shun, and his government is not that of Tang and Yu, I count myself foolish.

Thus, in setting matters forth before him and correcting his shortcomings, even though my words are painfully blunt and my remonstrance brushes against the dragon’s scales—even though the ruler is unwilling to hear them and their consequences exceed my strength to bear—I cannot fail to speak fully. I know only that I must make my ruler a true emperor or king; I know only that I must serve him according to the Way of Heaven. Such is the heart of a great minister. Pursuing this intention to its fullest extent, he must wish his ruler to become Heaven’s principal son, the father and mother of the people, a sovereign of enlightenment, wisdom, sageliness, and spiritual insight, and one acclaimed as a sage of the Central Realm [?]. Only when his ruler follows the same course and matches the achievements of Yao, Shun, Tang, and Wen is his wish fulfilled. He thus reveres his ruler as he reveres Heaven. Of all that the world calls reverence for the ruler, what could surpass this?

On another occasion, Mengzi rejected ministers who merely sought to please and those who treated the altars of soil and grain as of little consequence, while approving particularly of the great man who rectifies himself and thereby sets things right. Kongzi likewise said: “What is called a great minister serves his ruler according to the Way.” Kongzi and Mengzi spoke as one. Consider their dealings with Duke Ai of Lu, Duke Ling of Wei, King Xuan of Qi, and King Hui of Liang: although these were mediocre rulers of the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, in the Way of benevolence, righteousness, ritual, and music, they held fast to the supreme standard…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而不變雖終身不過而不少更焉聖賢者固尊
君之大而以天道自處以大臣自居孔孟之心
亦一也以此爲訓然後有治安之策不以長沙
之行而改其志天人之對不以好神僊土木而
易其言新法之議雖辭副樞隱巖穴而說終不
變三子者庶幾大臣歟惜三君者猶漢唐宋之
英主狃於其所快而終不堯舜也或者又曰臣
之於君分隔則難親言亢則難入故易有納約
自牖之象則就事論事而因明通蔽皆君者之
===
法也責之以難不將益滋其畏沮其進乎雖然
此遜就之說也君子寧言之不用而不可畀其
言以求合寧道之不行而不可小其道以求容
何者吾道之得於天者不可貶也若君之德可
以遜言而要其成則孔孟抱憂天下之志豈遑
久者與吾是以非信也
表
擬宋開天章閣召輔臣條對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
punctuated:
而不變，雖終身不過，而不少更焉。聖賢者固尊君之大，而以天道自處，以大臣自居，孔孟之心亦一也。以此爲訓，然後有治安之策，不以長沙之行而改其志；天人之對，不以好神僊土木而易其言；新法之議，雖辭副樞、隱巖穴，而說終不變。三子者庶幾大臣歟！惜三君者猶漢唐宋之英主，狃於其所快，而終不堯舜也。或者又曰：「臣之於君，分隔則難親，言亢則難入。故《易》有納約自牖之象，則就事論事，而因明通蔽，皆君者之法也。責之以難，不將益滋其畏、沮其進乎？」雖然，此遜就之說也。君子寧言之不用，而不可畀其言以求合；寧道之不行，而不可小其道以求容。何者？吾道之得於天者不可貶也。若君之德可以遜言而要其成，則孔孟抱憂天下之志，豈遑久者與？吾是以非信也。
表
擬宋開天章閣召輔臣條對謝表〔慶曆三年〕
translation_en:
…and did not change it. Even though throughout their lives they did not pass beyond this [?], they did not alter it in the slightest. The sages and worthies indeed honored their rulers in the greatest sense: they conducted themselves according to the Way of Heaven and took upon themselves the responsibilities of great ministers. In this, too, Kongzi and Mengzi were of one mind. Taking this as their guiding lesson, later men produced the policy essay on good government and security, its author not changing his resolve because of his departure for Changsha; the response on Heaven and humanity, its author not altering his words because of the ruler’s fondness for immortals and building projects; and the arguments concerning the New Policies, whose author never changed his position, even after resigning as Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs and retiring into the mountains. Did these three men not come close to being great ministers? Alas, their three rulers, though outstanding sovereigns of the Han, Tang, and Song, remained habituated to their own pleasures and never became a Yao or a Shun.
Someone else says: “When distinctions of rank separate minister and ruler, intimacy is difficult; when words are too lofty, they are difficult to accept. Thus the Book of Changes has the image of ‘presenting simple offerings through the window.’ Discussing each matter on its own terms and using what the ruler understands to penetrate what he does not—these are all methods for dealing with a ruler [?]. If we demand difficult things of him, will we not merely increase his apprehension and impede his progress?” Yet this is an argument for yielding and accommodation. A gentleman would rather his words go unused than surrender them to seek agreement; he would rather his Way remain unpracticed than diminish it to win acceptance. Why? Because our Way, received from Heaven, cannot be debased. If a ruler’s virtue could be brought to fulfillment through deferential words, then Kongzi and Mengzi, who cherished a concern for all under Heaven, would surely have had no leisure to linger so long [?]. This is why I do not believe that argument.
Memorial
A model memorial of thanks, written as though under the Song, for opening the Tianzhang Pavilion and summoning the chief ministers to present itemized responses. 〔Third year of Qingli [1043].〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
邱錦
同考試官教諭陳　批〔典則中能發揮忠愛之意可謂善頌善禱〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔精切得告君體〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔簡雅可誦〕
慶曆三年某月某日〔臣仲淹〕等蒙
恩召對天章閣者伏以
黃扉賜對康侯承晉接之儀
丹扆陳謨
===
聖主啓泰亨之運華流鼎鉉喜動朝紳〔臣〕等讓
懽誠忭稽首頓首上言竊惟上下交而志
同周易因之名卦明良際而喜起虞舜所
以登歌合宮闢則黃德愈光衢室開而堯
仁自廣都俞吁咈咨繇欺進其昌言鐘磬
鼓鞀大禹寔勤於嘉拜自尊君卑臣之禮
隔致訪道問政之念疎宣室之賈席空前
鬼神何補金商之邕對雖切倖幸愈張東
號追鋒徒急五時之召閣開天祿自讎七
punctuated:
邱錦

同考試官教諭陳批〔典則中能發揮忠愛之意，可謂善頌善禱。〕
考試官教諭謝批〔精切，得告君體。〕
考試官教諭馬批〔簡雅可誦。〕

慶曆三年某月某日，〔臣仲淹〕等蒙恩召對天章閣者。伏以黃扉賜對，康侯承晉接之儀；丹扆陳謨，聖主啓泰亨之運。華流鼎鉉，喜動朝紳。〔臣〕等讓懽誠忭，稽首頓首上言：竊惟上下交而志同，《周易》因之名卦；明良際而喜起，虞舜所以登歌。合宮闢則黃德愈光，衢室開而堯仁自廣。都俞吁咈，咨繇欺進其昌言；鐘磬鼓鞀，大禹寔勤於嘉拜。自尊君卑臣之禮隔，致訪道問政之念疎。宣室之賈席空前，鬼神何補？金商之邕對雖切，倖幸愈張。東號追鋒，徒急五時之召；閣開天祿，自讎七
translation_en:
Qiu Jin

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔Within a dignified and exemplary form, he develops sentiments of loyalty and devotion. This may be called skillful praise and skillful prayer.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔Precise and incisive; it achieves the proper manner of addressing the ruler.〕
Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: 〔Concise and elegant, worthy of recitation.〕

On a certain day of a certain month in the third year of Qingli [1043], 〔your servant Zhongyan〕 and his colleagues graciously received a summons to an audience in the Tianzhang Pavilion. We humbly reflect: granted an audience at the yellow doors, we received the ceremonial welcome accorded to the Prince of Kang in the hexagram Jin, “Advance”; presenting counsel before the vermilion throne screen, we witnessed our sagely sovereign inaugurate an era of peace and prosperity, as in the hexagram Tai. Splendor suffuses the highest ministers; joy stirs the officials of the court. 〔Your servants〕, filled with delight and rejoicing [?], bow our heads to the ground and submit these words:

We venture to reflect that when those above and below communicate, their purposes become one: the Changes of Zhou names a hexagram accordingly. When an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers meet, they joyfully rouse themselves to action: this is what Shun of Yu celebrated in song. When the Hegong palace opened, the Yellow Emperor’s virtue shone still more brightly; when the Qushi hall opened, Yao’s benevolence spread still farther. With expressions of approval and dissent, his counselors [?] advanced their excellent words; through bells, chime stones, drums, and hand drums, Great Yu diligently sought counsel and bowed in appreciation of good advice.

Once the ritual distinction that exalted the ruler and humbled his ministers became a barrier, the desire to inquire into the Way and consult about government grew faint. In the Xuanshi Hall, the ruler’s mat was drawn closer to Jia Yi in vain: what benefit came from discussing ghosts and spirits? Though Cai Yong’s replies at the Jinshang Gate were incisive, the power of imperial favorites [?] expanded still further. Under the Eastern dynasty [?], swift carriages merely hastened summons for the audiences of the five seasons; the Tianlu Pavilion was opened only for collating the Seven …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
略之書彼仁壽之賜見馬嚴止於註記而
朝元之耕揚厲豫僅以工詩徒飾彌文僅
成故事豈如
昭代獲覩
盛舉茲蓋伏遇
○○○
聖孝夙成
至仁天啓
曰慈曰儉億萬姓之欣戴攸同無怠無荒二
十年之憂勤如昔含淵而斥嫁義昭儆
而罷索燒羊從諫眞同轉圜爲民不敢暇
逸茲啓
===
先皇御書之閣趣召兩府承弼之臣精陞
恩綸俾從坐論從容接席談笑賜茶密邇
天顏皎如秋日之照覩聆
聖語藹若春風之溫臣得象臣殊各加慰勉謂
臣仲淹粗請西事甲兵叨具於胸中謂臣
弼再使北邊兒女悉遺於度外雖少善狀
punctuated:
略之書。彼仁壽之賜見，馬嚴止於註記；而朝元之耕，揚厲豫僅以工詩。徒飾彌文，僅成故事。豈如昭代獲覩盛舉！茲蓋伏遇○○○聖孝夙成，至仁天啓。曰慈曰儉，億萬姓之欣戴攸同；無怠無荒，二十年之憂勤如昔。含淵而斥嫁義，昭儆而罷索燒羊，從諫眞同轉圜，爲民不敢暇逸。
茲啓先皇御書之閣，趣召兩府承弼之臣，精陞恩綸，俾從坐論。從容接席，談笑賜茶，密邇天顏，皎如秋日之照；覩聆聖語，藹若春風之溫。臣得象、臣殊，殊各加慰勉；謂臣仲淹粗請西事，甲兵叨具於胸中；謂臣弼再使北邊，兒女悉遺於度外。雖少善狀，
translation_en:
…the book of summaries. At the audience granted at Renshou, Ma Yan did no more than make annotations; as for the occasion at Chaoyuan, Yang Liyu [?] merely displayed skill in poetry. These only embellished elaborate formalities and became precedents. How could they compare with the splendid occasion we have been privileged to witness in this illustrious age!
We have most reverently encountered Your Majesty, whose sagely filial devotion matured early and whose supreme benevolence was endowed by Heaven. Your compassion and frugality alike inspire the joyful allegiance of the countless people. Neither negligent nor given to excess, you remain as anxious and diligent after twenty years as at the beginning. You embraced profundity and rejected “jiayi” [?]; taking warning, you ceased requesting roast lamb. Your readiness to follow remonstrance is truly like turning a round object; for the people's sake, you dare not indulge in leisure.
Now you have opened the pavilion housing the late emperor's imperial writings and urgently summoned the ministers of the two chief councils who assist your rule. You issued a gracious imperial communication [?], allowing them to sit and discuss affairs. At ease, you received them beside your seat, conversing and smiling as you bestowed tea. Close to your heavenly countenance, they experienced its brightness like the autumn sun; hearing your sagely words, they felt their genial warmth like a spring breeze. Your servants Dexiang and Shu each received particular consolation and encouragement. You said that your servant Zhongyan had made some proposals concerning western affairs [?] and possessed, beyond his deserts, a command of military matters within his breast; you said that your servant Bi had twice served as envoy to the northern frontier, putting all thoughts of his children and family aside. Though we have few worthy accomplishments…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
頗餘朴忠允切咨詢獨承睿注恩固深乎
家人父子念實切乎天下蒼生傴僂循牆
雖不違顏於咫尺踴躍待旦敢忘圖報於
涓埃謹各抒十事二策之誠冀少備
九重乙夜之覽內而擇官精舉吏治庶乎可清
外而減役均田民生由之漸復黜幽柳幸
法自近行信令草恩德從上始財固以不
用爲富恒守節用之規兵固以不戰爲威
時存忘戰之戒盡披一得少佐
===
萬幾伏願
念四聰之難達愈加意於求賢畏一暴之易
寒務留神於去佞䕶敬大臣之道以體羣
臣小臣廉大臣法用不泄邇之心而不忘
遠邇者悅遠者來臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹具
表稱
謝以
punctuated:
頗餘朴忠，允切咨詢，獨承睿注。恩固深乎家人父子，念實切乎天下蒼生。傴僂循牆，雖不違顏於咫尺；踴躍待旦，敢忘圖報於涓埃？謹各抒十事二策之誠，冀少備九重乙夜之覽。內而擇官精舉，吏治庶乎可清；外而減役均田，民生由之漸復。黜幽柳幸，法自近行；信令草恩，德從上始。財固以不用爲富，恒守節用之規；兵固以不戰爲威，時存忘戰之戒。盡披一得，少佐萬幾。
伏願念四聰之難達，愈加意於求賢；畏一暴之易寒，務留神於去佞。䕶敬大臣之道，以體羣臣，小臣廉，大臣法；用不泄邇之心，而不忘遠，邇者悅，遠者來。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹具表稱謝以……
translation_en:
…we still retain some simple loyalty. You earnestly sought our counsel and bestowed upon us your particular imperial attention. Your favor is indeed as profound as the bonds between father and son within a family; your concern is truly heartfelt for all the common people under Heaven. Bowing low and keeping close to the wall, though we remain only a few feet from your countenance, we eagerly await the dawn: how could we forget to repay you even in the smallest measure? We have respectfully set forth our sincere intentions in ten proposals and two plans, hoping to furnish something for Your Majesty to read within the palace during the second watch of the night. Within the administration, select officials and make nominations carefully, so that official conduct may become honest; throughout the realm, reduce labor obligations and equalize landholding, so that the people's livelihood may gradually recover. Dismiss the unworthy and restrain favorites [?], enforcing the law first among those closest to you; make commands trustworthy and extend favor [?], so that virtue begins with those above. Wealth indeed lies in leaving resources unspent: constantly observe the rule of frugality. Military authority indeed lies in prevailing without battle: always remember the warning against forgetting warfare. We lay bare every modest insight, hoping to assist a little with your myriad affairs of state.
We humbly pray that you remember how difficult it is for information from all four quarters to reach the throne, and devote still greater attention to seeking worthy men; fear how easily a brief spell of warmth gives way to cold, and take care to remove flatterers. Uphold the way of respecting great ministers, and thereby show consideration for all your officials: lesser officials will be incorruptible, and great ministers will observe the law. With a heart that does not neglect those nearby, do not forget those far away: those nearby will rejoice, and those far away will come. Gazing toward Heaven and looking up to Your Sagely Majesty, we, your servants, cannot contain our fervent emotion and profound awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our thanks, and thereby…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
問
第叁場
策五道
第一問
馮懋仁
同考試官教諭丁　批
太子天下本義
皇祖及
今上著意甚切此作敷揚明悉且說輔翼左右處中肯綮宜錄以
獻
===
考試官教諭謝　批
〔青宮掌故子能條悉無遺其論〕
〔關係事最可置一通座右〕
考試官教諭楊　批
〔條對詳整有惓惓愛意〕
自賈誼所稱天下之命懸於太子太子之
善在於早諭教與選左右有味乎其言之
也雖然非自誼始也書尹之誥曰一人元
良萬邦以貞蓋言本也易蒙之象曰蒙以
養正聖功也蓋言學也唯禮與左史書大
punctuated:
問。
第叁場，策五道。第一問。
馮懋仁。
同考試官教諭丁批：太子，天下本義。皇祖及今上著意甚切。此作敷揚明悉，且說輔翼左右處中肯綮，宜錄以獻。
考試官教諭謝批：〔青宮掌故，子能條悉無遺。其論〕〔關係事，最可置一通座右。〕
考試官教諭楊批：〔條對詳整，有惓惓愛意。〕
自賈誼所稱「天下之命懸於太子，太子之善在於早諭教與選左右」，有味乎其言之也！雖然，非自誼始也。《書》尹之誥曰：「一人元良，萬邦以貞。」蓋言本也。《易》蒙之象曰：「蒙以養正，聖功也。」蓋言學也。唯《禮》與左史書大
translation_en:
Question.
Third Session: Five Policy Questions. First Question.
Feng Maoren.
Comment by Associate Examiner Ding, Instructor: The crown prince is the foundation of all under Heaven—this is the principle [?]. The Imperial Ancestor and His Majesty the reigning emperor have devoted particularly earnest attention to this matter. This composition expounds it clearly and fully, and its discussion of those who assist the crown prince and attend him strikes the essential point. It should be transcribed for presentation to the emperor.
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔You have systematically and exhaustively set out the precedents concerning the crown prince’s palace. Your discussion〕〔of matters bearing upon this subject particularly deserves to be copied and kept beside one’s seat.〕
Comment by Examiner Yang, Instructor: 〔The responses are detailed and orderly, expressing earnest affection and concern.〕
As Jia Yi said, “The destiny of all under Heaven hangs upon the crown prince; the crown prince’s goodness depends upon instructing him early and selecting those who attend him.” How much meaning there is in his words! Yet this did not begin with Jia Yi. Yin’s announcement in the Book of Documents says: “When the One Man is supremely good, the myriad states are set right.” This speaks of the foundation. The image of the hexagram Meng in the Book of Changes says: “To nurture rectitude amid youthful ignorance is the work of a sage.” This speaks of learning. The Book of Rites and the writings of the Scribe of the Left, the Grand … [?]

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
傅亦有之其畧曰古者后妊七月而就宴
室所求聲音非禮樂太師緼瑟而稱不習
滋味非正味太宰倚升而曰不敢以待王
太子所謂胎教也生而接以太牢士負之
有司齋肅端冕而見之南郊所謂襁褓之
教也能行立矣道之禮過闕則下過廟則
趨所謂童穉之教也少長始知色則出齒
於太學教之爲人臣焉教之爲人子焉教
之爲人幼焉毋使異日有一人之肆也十
===
八曰孟侯孟侯者於四方諸侯來朝迎於
郊問所不知毋使異日有洪居之悔也故
太子立而置太師太傅太保及乎既冠成
人則有記過之史徹膳之宰敢諫之鼓瞽
史誦詩工誦箴諫大夫進謀士傳民語愚
竊以爲其備官也非好縻祿也非欲其敵
儀於至尊也欲使左右前後皆正人以漸
摩其德也鷄鳴而起一日而三朝非欲故
勞之欲其習於勤也其與國人齒也非故
punctuated: 傅亦有之，其畧曰：古者后妊七月而就宴室，所求聲音非禮樂，太師緼瑟而稱不習；滋味非正味，太宰倚升而曰：「不敢以待王太子。」所謂胎教也。生而接以太牢，士負之，有司齋肅端冕而見之南郊，所謂襁褓之教也。能行立矣，道之禮，過闕則下，過廟則趨，所謂童穉之教也。少長，始知色，則出齒於太學，教之爲人臣焉，教之爲人子焉，教之爲人幼焉，毋使異日有一人之肆也。十八曰孟侯，孟侯者，於四方諸侯來朝，迎於郊，問所不知，毋使異日有洪居之悔也。故太子立而置太師、太傅、太保，及乎既冠成人，則有記過之史、徹膳之宰、敢諫之鼓，瞽史誦詩，工誦箴諫，大夫進謀，士傳民語。愚竊以爲，其備官也，非好縻祿也，非欲其敵儀於至尊也，欲使左右前後皆正人，以漸摩其德也。鷄鳴而起，一日而三朝，非欲故勞之，欲其習於勤也。其與國人齒也，非故
translation_en:
…the Grand Tutor also contains such an account [?]. Its outline reads: In antiquity, when the queen was seven months pregnant, she withdrew to a private chamber.
