If the sounds she requested were not ritually proper music, the Music Master wrapped up his zither and declared that he had not learned them. If the flavors she requested were not proper flavors, the Grand Steward set aside his ladle and said, “I dare not serve these to the royal heir apparent.” This was what was called prenatal instruction. At birth, he was received with a full sacrificial offering of ox, sheep, and pig. A serviceman carried him, and the responsible officials, purified by fasting and solemnly dressed in ceremonial robes and caps, presented him in the southern suburb. This was what was called instruction in swaddling clothes.

Once he could stand and walk, he was guided by ritual: when passing palace gate-towers he dismounted, and when passing an ancestral temple he quickened his steps. This was what was called instruction in childhood. When he grew somewhat older and began to understand sexual attraction, he went out to take his place by age among the students at the Imperial University. He was taught how to be a subject, how to be a son, and how to be a junior, so that in later days he would not indulge the unrestrained will of a sole ruler. At eighteen he was called the “eldest lord.” As eldest lord, when the regional lords from the four quarters came to court, he welcomed them in the suburbs and asked about what he did not know, so that in later days he would have no cause to regret dwelling in arrogance [?].

Thus, when an heir apparent was established, a Grand Preceptor, Grand Mentor, and Grand Guardian were appointed. Once he had undergone capping and attained adulthood, there were scribes to record his faults, stewards to withdraw his meals, and a drum for those who dared to remonstrate. Blind musicians and scribes recited poems; musicians recited admonitions and remonstrances; grandees offered counsel; and servicemen conveyed the people's words.

In my humble opinion, this full complement of officials was not appointed out of a fondness for wasting stipends, nor to give the heir ceremonial standing equal to the sovereign. It was intended to ensure that upright men surrounded him on every side, gradually nurturing and refining his virtue. Rising at cockcrow and paying his respects at court three times a day were not intended deliberately to weary him, but to accustom him to diligence. His taking his place by age among the people of the realm was not deliberately intended to…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
欲平之欲其習於恭也自周之末𦍒秦繼
之人主不盡能舉三代之所以教者爲教
而太子亦不盡能舉三代之所以學者爲
學其始也守道欽而躍龍之地或危其終
也君道缺而飛龍之地或亢是故秦之胡
亥受治獄於趙高最卽位而慕射人而望
夷之禍成矣漢之戾園開博望通賓客多
以異端進巫蠱起而長安兵而湖陰之禍
成矣開皇之際發于嬪嫡楊素進而房陵
===
之位不終矣德宗之末宮案無釋王伾叔
文進而永貞之治損矣至於漢靈唐僖之
季父張讓而毋趙珪定策國老而門生天
子帝位予奪於左貂人主食息於中涓宦
官之勢重而天下之大計移矣故溫嶠之
箴侍臣也則曰均士抗禮以𢍉厥情入學
齊齒言稱先生不以賢自臧不以貴爲榮
思有虞之蒸蒸尊周文之翼翼屛彼佞諛
納此亮直言太子之職所當盡也王褒之
punctuated:
欲平之，欲其習於恭也。自周之末𦍒秦繼之，人主不盡能舉三代之所以教者爲教，而太子亦不盡能舉三代之所以學者爲學。其始也，守道欽，而躍龍之地或危；其終也，君道缺，而飛龍之地或亢。是故秦之胡亥受治獄於趙高，最卽位而慕射人，而望夷之禍成矣。漢之戾園開博望，通賓客，多以異端進，巫蠱起而長安兵，而湖陰之禍成矣。開皇之際，發于嬪嫡，楊素進而房陵之位不終矣。德宗之末，宮案無釋，王伾、叔文進而永貞之治損矣。至於漢靈、唐僖之季，父張讓而毋趙珪，定策國老而門生天子，帝位予奪於左貂，人主食息於中涓，宦官之勢重而天下之大計移矣。
故溫嶠之箴侍臣也，則曰：「均士抗禮，以𢍉厥情。入學齊齒，言稱先生。不以賢自臧，不以貴爲榮。思有虞之蒸蒸，尊周文之翼翼。屛彼佞諛，納此亮直。」言太子之職所當盡也。王褒之
translation_en:
…wish to place him on an equal footing; the intention was to accustom him to respectfulness. From the end of the Zhou, when the Qin succeeded it [?], rulers could no longer fully employ the educational practices of the Three Dynasties, nor could crown princes fully adopt their methods of learning. At the outset, their adherence to the Way was deficient [?], and their position as the dragon poised to leap could become precarious; in the end, their practice of the ruler’s Way was incomplete, and their position as the flying dragon could become excessively exalted.
Thus Hu Hai of the Qin learned the handling of criminal cases from Zhao Gao. Upon ascending the throne [?], he took pleasure in shooting people, and the catastrophe at Wangyi came about. The Han crown prince commemorated at Liyuan opened the Bowang establishment and received guests, many of whom gained access through heterodox teachings. The witchcraft affair arose, fighting broke out in Chang’an, and the catastrophe at Huyin followed. During the Kaihuang reign, trouble arose over consorts and the legitimate heir [?]; Yang Su advanced, and the Prince of Fangling failed to retain his position. At the end of Dezong’s reign, a palace case remained unresolved [?]; Wang Pi and Wang Shuwen advanced, and the government of the Yongzhen reign suffered damage. By the closing years of Emperor Ling of the Han and Emperor Xizong of the Tang, Zhang Rang was treated as a father and Zhao Gui as a mother [?]; those who determined the succession were called elders of the state, while the Son of Heaven styled himself their pupil. The imperial throne was bestowed or taken away by eunuchs wearing sable ornaments, and the ruler depended on palace eunuchs even for his meals and rest. As the eunuchs’ power grew, control over the great affairs of the realm shifted into their hands.
Thus Wen Jiao’s admonition to attendant officials says: “Treat men of learning as equals and accord them equal courtesies, thereby regulating your dispositions [?]. On entering the school, take your place according to age and address your teachers as ‘Master.’ Do not esteem yourself for your worthiness or take pride in your noble rank. Reflect upon the ever-deepening filial devotion of the lord of Yu; revere the cautious reverence of King Wen of Zhou. Reject those flatterers and admit these faithful, upright men.” This speaks of the duties that a crown prince must fulfill. As for Wang Bao’s…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
箴太子也則曰勿謂居尊禍福無門勿謂
親賢王道無偏無爲慮始無爲事先損之
又損全之亦全言太子之地不易居也斯
二者皆所以語爲人臣子之道也唐文皇
製帝範十二則冠之以君體而建親求賢
審官納諫去讒戒盈崇儉賞罰務農閱武
崇文之類次焉皆所以語爲人主之道也
燦然備矣惜也其言繁詳而身教略也承
乾儲而不終高宗帝而不帝有以也
===
明興
高皇帝甫立
皇太子即建大本堂居之積武庫七略之書
而聚天下之英俊者碩從容談說經義賜
宴賦詩最後采經傳格言爲書曰
儲君昭鑒錄俾日進講曰若等務導之以正
他日勝重任也至
文皇帝而稍充廣其書益以
高帝之謨訓曰文華寶鑑召
punctuated:
箴太子也，則曰：「勿謂居尊，禍福無門；勿謂親賢，王道無偏。無爲慮始，無爲事先。損之又損，全之亦全。」言太子之地不易居也。斯二者，皆所以語爲人臣子之道也。唐文皇製《帝範》十二則，冠之以君體，而建親、求賢、審官、納諫、去讒、戒盈、崇儉、賞罰、務農、閱武、崇文之類次焉，皆所以語爲人主之道也。燦然備矣！惜也，其言繁詳而身教略也。承乾儲而不終，高宗帝而不帝，有以也。
明興，高皇帝甫立皇太子，即建大本堂居之，積武庫七略之書，而聚天下之英俊者碩，從容談說經義，賜宴賦詩。最後采經傳格言爲書，曰《儲君昭鑒錄》，俾日進講，曰：「若等務導之以正，他日勝重任也。」至文皇帝，而稍充廣其書，益以高帝之謨訓，曰《文華寶鑑》，召
translation_en:
…in his admonition to the Crown Prince, he said: “Do not suppose that, because you occupy an exalted position, misfortune and good fortune have no means of entry. Do not suppose that, because you associate with worthy men, the kingly Way cannot become partial. Do not take the lead in deliberations; do not put yourself first in affairs. Diminish and diminish again; preserve wholeness in its entirety.” This says that the Crown Prince’s position is not easily occupied. Both these admonitions explain the proper way to act as a subject and a son. Emperor Wen of Tang composed twelve sections of the Model for Emperors (Difan), placing “The Ruler’s Essential Character” first, followed by such topics as establishing imperial kinsmen, seeking worthy men, scrutinizing appointments, accepting remonstrance, rejecting slander, guarding against complacency, honoring frugality, rewards and punishments, promoting agriculture, reviewing military preparedness, and honoring civil culture. All explain the proper way to act as a sovereign. How splendidly comprehensive! Regrettably, his words were elaborate and detailed, while his teaching by personal example was scant. There were reasons why Chengqian became heir apparent but did not remain so, and why Gaozong became emperor yet failed to act as an emperor.
When the Ming arose, Emperor Gao, immediately upon establishing the Crown Prince, built the Hall of the Great Foundation (Dabentang) for him to reside in. He amassed books of military learning and of the seven bibliographical divisions [?], and gathered outstanding talents from throughout the realm [the character 碩 here is unclear]. At leisure they discussed the meaning of the classics; he bestowed banquets, and poems were composed. Finally, he selected exemplary sayings from the classics and their commentaries to make a book entitled Record of the Illustrious Mirror for the Heir Apparent (Chujun zhaojian lu), and ordered that it be expounded daily. He said: “You must guide him in what is right, so that in days to come he can bear his weighty responsibilities.” Under Emperor Wen, this book was somewhat expanded and supplemented with Emperor Gao’s counsels and instructions, and entitled Precious Mirror of Literary Splendor (Wenhua baojian). He summoned…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
皇太子授之曰脩己治人之要盡矣若其勉
之
宣宗之爲
帝訓也篇凡二十五始君德而終藥餌也
憲宗之爲
文華大訓也卷凡四進學也養德也厚倫也
明治也要之其命名與帝範同而章軌與
唐文異
明德隆隆嗣三代矣自青禁之制不講於
===
先朝朱邸之開僅同於藩國海內皇皇然若靡
所瞻望
上即位之初元即下
詔立
皇太子推
恩海內其明年復示出閣之期以十齡奏聞溫
文日新岐嶷天縱中外億兆臣庶咸欣欣
焉思獲奉盛美開天下萬世太平根本而
草莽下臣不勝私憂過計以爲太子之體
punctuated:
皇太子，授之曰：「脩己治人之要盡矣，若其勉之！」宣宗之爲《帝訓》也，篇凡二十五，始君德而終藥餌也。憲宗之爲《文華大訓》也，卷凡四：進學也，養德也，厚倫也，明治也。要之，其命名與《帝範》同，而章軌與唐文異。明德隆隆，嗣三代矣。
自青禁之制不講於先朝，朱邸之開僅同於藩國，海內皇皇然，若靡所瞻望。上即位之初元，即下詔立皇太子，推恩海內。其明年，復示出閣之期，以十齡奏聞。溫文日新，岐嶷天縱，中外億兆臣庶咸欣欣焉，思獲奉盛美，開天下萬世太平根本。而草莽下臣不勝私憂過計，以爲太子之體
translation_en:
…the heir apparent and presented it to him, saying: “The essentials of cultivating oneself and governing others are all here. Strive to put them into practice!” Xuanzong’s Imperial Instructions (Dixun) comprised twenty-five chapters, beginning with the ruler’s virtue and ending with medicines. Xianzong’s Great Instructions of Literary Brilliance (Wenhua daxun) comprised four volumes: advancing learning, nurturing virtue, strengthening human relationships, and illuminating government. In sum, their naming followed the Imperial Model (Difan), but their organization and guiding principles differed from the Tang text. The flourishing virtue of the Ming carried on the legacy of the Three Dynasties.
Since the institutions of the heir apparent’s palace had fallen into neglect in the preceding reign, and the establishment of his residence had been treated as scarcely different from that of a regional prince, all within the seas were anxious, as though they had nowhere to turn their hopes. In the first year of his reign, His Majesty issued an edict establishing the heir apparent and extended his grace throughout the realm. The following year, he further indicated when the prince would leave the inner palace to begin formal schooling; the age of ten was reported to the throne as the appointed time [?]. The prince’s gentleness and refinement grew daily, and his precocious intelligence was Heaven’s gift. The countless officials and common people, at court and throughout the empire, all rejoiced, hoping to uphold this magnificent promise and establish the foundation of peace for the world through ten thousand generations. Yet I, a lowly servant living beyond official circles, cannot restrain my private anxieties and excessive deliberations, considering that the heir apparent’s standing…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
不忠其不崇忠其崇而無所接異日君臣
之分不忠其不辨忠其辨而至於不相通
今雖未能猝復古制如所謂拜師而齒學
者亦宜少采貞觀至道儀節三師賓客見
則必假以殊禮從容燕閒啓沃治道其諸
寮案亦聽坐侍講讀反覆開陳以畢所見
所講讀諸書自六經四子及
先朝謨訓外別命儒臣條纂六曹職掌今時要
務如財用困乏民業艱難武備積廢綦士風
===
日卑及它一切吏弊國蠹分條附見務令
剴切不必宏深勒成一書專備詢覽
人主時時考問觀其進否而稍抗法於其左右
至於坊局諭賛之官必選清方直亮通明
該練者充之勿急才藻以長浮華勿廣遴
諸以滋躁競其內而保姆阿監必委長年
毋令見少麗以犯未定之戒服御居舍必
崇儉朴毋令見奇袤以開奢侈之漸率土
之臣皆其臣也毋以暬御僕從爲私人天
punctuated:
不忠其不崇，忠其崇而無所接；異日君臣之分，不忠其不辨，忠其辨而至於不相通。今雖未能猝復古制，如所謂拜師而齒學者，亦宜少采貞觀、至道儀節。三師賓客見，則必假以殊禮，從容燕閒，啓沃治道。其諸寮案，亦聽坐侍講讀，反覆開陳，以畢所見。所講讀諸書，自六經、四子及先朝謨訓外，別命儒臣條纂六曹職掌、今時要務，如財用困乏、民業艱難、武備積廢、綦士風日卑，及它一切吏弊國蠹，分條附見，務令剴切，不必宏深，勒成一書，專備詢覽。
人主時時考問，觀其進否，而稍抗法於其左右。至於坊局諭賛之官，必選清方直亮、通明該練者充之。勿急才藻，以長浮華；勿廣遴諸，以滋躁競。其內而保姆阿監，必委長年，毋令見少麗，以犯未定之戒。服御居舍，必崇儉朴，毋令見奇袤，以開奢侈之漸。率土之臣，皆其臣也，毋以暬御僕從爲私人。天
translation_en:
…the concern is not that his dignity will be insufficiently exalted, but that it will be so exalted that he has no contact with others [?]. As for the distinction between ruler and ministers in future, the concern is not that it will be unclear, but that it will be so sharply drawn that communication becomes impossible [?]. Although the ancient institutions cannot now be restored at once—such as formally acknowledging a teacher and taking one’s place in school according to age—some ceremonial practices of the Zhenguan and Zhidao reign periods should nevertheless be adopted. When the Three Preceptors and the Guests of the Heir Apparent attend audience, they must be accorded exceptional courtesy, so that in relaxed and informal surroundings they may instruct him in the way of government. His other staff members [?] should likewise be permitted to sit while attending him for lectures and readings, explaining matters repeatedly and fully expressing their views. Besides the Six Classics, the writings of the Four Masters, and the counsels and instructions of former reigns, Confucian officials should be separately commanded to compile, under distinct headings, the duties of the Six Ministries and the pressing affairs of the present day. These should include shortages of revenue, the hardships of the people’s livelihoods, the accumulated neglect of military preparedness, the daily decline in the conduct of scholars [?], and all other official abuses and evils injurious to the state. These matters should be appended under separate headings, with an emphasis on pertinence and directness rather than breadth or profundity, and compiled into a single book expressly for consultation and reading.
The sovereign should question and examine him from time to time, observing whether he has progressed, and somewhat more firmly uphold standards among his attendants. As for the officials charged with instruction and assistance in the establishments of the Heir Apparent, these posts must be filled by men who are incorruptible, upright, candid, discerning, broadly informed, and experienced. Do not prize literary talent and polish too eagerly, thereby encouraging superficial brilliance; nor broaden recruitment excessively [?], thereby encouraging impatient competition. Within his household, the duties of nurses and eunuch attendants [?] must be entrusted to persons of mature years. Do not let him encounter youthful beauties and thus transgress the restraint appropriate to one whose disposition is not yet settled. His clothing, personal furnishings, and dwelling must favor economy and simplicity. Do not let him encounter exotic luxuries [?], thereby opening the way to extravagance. The ministers throughout the realm are all his ministers; he must not regard his intimate attendants and servants as his private retainers. All under Heaven…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
下之有皆其有也毋請莊田店宅爲私藏
太子徧識萬類之情而不見其用尊在
一人之下而不廢其謙卑心無爲以守至正唐
虞三代之化端在於此雖然愚之私憂過
計猶有不能已者蓋
國家雍熙之治莫盛於宣德弘治間而及其
後也頗不滿於二正正之季彼其出而亂二
正之治爲振爲瑾若乃宣弘所用以侍青
宮之人也今六局丞郎而下縱無其人可
不預爲之所乎寧倜而毋愛其儇寧緩而
毋愛其捷寧樸無能而不必其有技寧目
不知書而不必其多識此在
人主及輔弼大臣加之意而已
===
第二問
陳功
同考試官教諭譚　批〔於經訓故不同作者類言之而無折衷此篇有斷案而末歸重於心其有本之學耶〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔因經義而及道統是識其大者〕
punctuated:
下之有，皆其有也，毋請莊田店宅爲私藏。太子徧識萬類之情，而不見其用，尊在一人之下，而不廢其謙，卑心無爲，以守至正。唐虞三代之化，端在於此。雖然，愚之私憂過計，猶有不能已者。蓋國家雍熙之治，莫盛於宣德、弘治間，而及其後也，頗不滿於二正。正之季，彼其出而亂二正之治，爲振、爲瑾，若乃宣、弘所用以侍青宮之人也。今六局丞郎而下，縱無其人，可不預爲之所乎？寧倜而毋愛其儇，寧緩而毋愛其捷，寧樸無能而不必其有技，寧目不知書而不必其多識。此在人主及輔弼大臣加之意而已。

第二問
陳功
同考試官教諭譚　批〔於經訓故不同，作者類言之而無折衷。此篇有斷案，而末歸重於心，其有本之學耶？〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔因經義而及道統，是識其大者。〕
translation_en:
…all that exists under Heaven is his; he should not request estates, shops, or residences as his private holdings. The heir apparent should understand fully the circumstances of all kinds of things without putting them to use himself. Though his exalted position is below only one man, he should retain his humility, humble his heart, and practice nonaction so as to preserve perfect rectitude. The transforming influence of the reigns of Tang Yao and Yu Shun and of the Three Dynasties has its very source in this. Nevertheless, there are private anxieties and excessive concerns that I, in my foolishness, cannot put aside.

The dynasty’s harmonious and flourishing government reached its height during the Xuande and Hongzhi reigns. Subsequently, however, it fell considerably short during the two Zheng reigns [Zhengtong and Zhengde]. In the latter part of Zheng [?], those who emerged to throw the government of these two reigns into disorder—[Wang] Zhen and [Liu] Jin—were precisely men employed during Xuande and Hongzhi to attend the heir apparent. Even if there are no such men today among the assistant officials of the Six Bureaus and below [?], should provision not be made beforehand? Better that they be aloof [?] than that their glib cleverness be prized; better that they be slow than that their quickness be prized. Better that they be plain and without ability than that special skills be required of them; better that they be unable to read than that extensive learning be required of them. This depends only on the ruler and his assisting high ministers giving the matter their attention.

Second Question
Chen Gong

Associate Examiner Tan, Instructor, comments: 〔Concerning differences in the interpretation of the Classics, writers generally recount them without adjudicating between them. This essay offers a definite judgment and, at its conclusion, places the ultimate emphasis on the heart-mind. Is this not learning that has a firm foundation?〕

Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔Proceeding from the meaning of the Classics to the transmission of the Way, this essay recognizes what is most important.〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎諭馬　批〔剖析精微讀之瞭然〕
六經其猶日月乎其體歷萬古而不虧而
其用亦將有所不爽故夫日有夕而月有
晦幽谷部屋之下雖容光而自遠勢不得
不假之於燭火燭者所以佐日月之光於
不及者也訓故之學翼而明之者也立言
之學廣而遍之者也皆所謂燭也取燭而
佐日月之光於不及則可以燭而配日月
之光而謂之三不可此楊雄王通氏之所
===
以失也楊氏之爲玄也凡三方九州二十
七部八十一家二百四十三表七百二十
九贊擬之以三摹闔之以休咎緯之以象
類播之以人事文之以五行擬之以道德
仁義禮智爲其太曼漶而不可知故有首
衝錯測攡瑩數文掜圖告十一篇皆以解
剝玄體離散其文雄之自敘云爾其意則
曰此非楊雄氏之玄而楊雄氏之易也要
之無易而後可以有玄有易矣玄何所用
punctuated:
考試官敎諭馬，批〔剖析精微，讀之瞭然。〕

六經其猶日月乎？其體歷萬古而不虧，而其用亦將有所不爽。故夫日有夕，而月有晦，幽谷部屋之下，雖容光而自遠，勢不得不假之於燭火。燭者，所以佐日月之光於不及者也。訓故之學，翼而明之者也；立言之學，廣而遍之者也，皆所謂燭也。取燭而佐日月之光於不及，則可；以燭而配日月之光而謂之三，不可。此楊雄、王通氏之所以失也。楊氏之爲玄也，凡三方、九州、二十七部、八十一家、二百四十三表、七百二十九贊，擬之以三摹，闔之以休咎，緯之以象類，播之以人事，文之以五行，擬之以道德仁義禮智。爲其太曼漶而不可知，故有首、衝、錯、測、攡、瑩、數、文、掜、圖、告十一篇，皆以解剝玄體，離散其文，雄之自敘云爾。其意則曰：「此非楊雄氏之玄，而楊雄氏之易也。」要之，無易而後可以有玄；有易矣，玄何所用
translation_en:
Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔The analysis is subtle and precise; reading it makes the matter perfectly clear.〕

Are the Six Classics not like the sun and moon? Their substance remains undiminished through myriad ages, and their efficacy likewise must remain unfailing. Yet the sun has its evenings, and the moon its dark phase. Deep valleys and secluded chambers [?], though admitting light, are remote from its reach; circumstances therefore compel reliance on candlelight. A candle supplements the light of the sun and moon wherever it cannot reach. The study of textual glosses supports and elucidates the Classics; the learning that produces enduring writings broadens and extends their reach. Both are what we call candles. To take a candle and supplement the light of the sun and moon where it cannot reach is permissible; to set candlelight on a par with their light and call them a triad is not. This is where Yang Xiong and Wang Tong went wrong.

In composing his Supreme Mystery (Taixuan), Yang established three regions, nine provinces, twenty-seven divisions, eighty-one houses, two hundred and forty-three indicators, and seven hundred and twenty-nine appraisals. He modeled it on three patterns [?], encompassed it with auspicious and inauspicious outcomes, interwove it with images and categories, distributed it across human affairs, patterned it with the Five Phases, and modeled it on the Way, virtue, benevolence, righteousness, ritual propriety, and wisdom. Because it was too diffuse and obscure to be understood, he provided eleven chapters: Heads (Shou), Conflicts (Chong), Interconnections (Cuo), Fathoming (Ce), Unfolding (Chi), Clarifying (Ying), Numbers (Shu), Patterns (Wen), Comparisons (Ni), Diagrams (Tu), and Pronouncements (Gao). These all serve to explicate and dissect the structure of the Mystery and to separate out its text. So Yang Xiong himself states in his preface. His intention amounts to saying: “This is not Master Yang Xiong’s Mystery; it is Master Yang Xiong’s Book of Changes.” Ultimately, only if there were no Book of Changes could there be a place for the Mystery. Since the Book of Changes already exists, what use is the Mystery …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之且玄之體方而易之體圓圓則不待擬
議而自成方則必待假借而後就故說者
謂楊雄僭也王氏之擬經也大抵以漢七
制續書以曹劉顏謝之篇續詩其所贊易
即關子明之說筮論其所定禮則叔孫氏
之綿蕞儀其筆春秋則止陳亡以配獲麟
其要如此而已其意則曰此非六經之經
而王氏之經也要之可以言傳而不可以
言經有六經矣夫安得而配之且其所謂
===
七制諸篇者何敢望典謨雅頌之藩籬而
關朗叔孫不過支離體粕之近似若元經
之帝兩魏黜蜀漢而夷江左大旨亦已悖
矣故說者謂通亦僭也至於法言中說雖
若有出於模擬剽竊而往往能尊正道發
微言於千載之後特所謂法言者言多遠
而指則近故不免於晦中說者說雖暢而
理或支故不免於雜至有謂通與李德明
不相及而唐初諸貴臣稱門人者不一舉
punctuated:
之？且玄之體方，而易之體圓。圓則不待擬議而自成，方則必待假借而後就，故說者謂楊雄僭也。王氏之擬經也，大抵以漢七制續書，以曹劉顏謝之篇續詩。其所贊易，即關子明之說筮論；其所定禮，則叔孫氏之綿蕞儀；其筆春秋，則止陳亡以配獲麟。其要如此而已。其意則曰：「此非六經之經，而王氏之經也。」要之，可以言傳，而不可以言經。有六經矣，夫安得而配之？且其所謂七制諸篇者，何敢望典謨雅頌之藩籬？而關朗、叔孫，不過支離體粕之近似。若元經之帝兩魏，黜蜀漢而夷江左，大旨亦已悖矣。故說者謂通亦僭也。

至於法言、中說，雖若有出於模擬剽竊，而往往能尊正道，發微言於千載之後。特所謂法言者，言多遠而指則近，故不免於晦；中說者，說雖暢而理或支，故不免於雜。至有謂通與李德明不相及，而唐初諸貴臣稱門人者，不一舉
translation_en:
…what use is it? Moreover, the structure of the Supreme Mystery is square, whereas that of the Changes is round. What is round completes itself without awaiting deliberation; what is square must depend on borrowing before it can be completed. Thus commentators call Yang Xiong presumptuous.

As for Master Wang’s imitation of the classics, he broadly used the Seven Reigns of the Han to continue the Documents, and compositions by Cao, Liu, Yan, and Xie to continue the Odes. His elucidation of the Changes was simply Guan Ziming’s Discourse on Divination; the rites he established were merely Shusun’s ceremonies rehearsed with bundles of reeds. His version of the Spring and Autumn Annals ended with the fall of Chen, to match the capture of the unicorn. These were its essentials, and nothing more. His intention amounted to saying: “These are not the classics of the Six Classics, but Master Wang’s own classics.” In sum, they may be called commentaries, but they cannot be called classics. Since the Six Classics already exist, how could his works rank alongside them? Moreover, how could his so-called Seven Reigns and other compositions even aspire to approach the outer precincts of the Canons and Counsels, or the Elegantiae and Hymns? Guan Lang and Shusun offer no more than a resemblance to disjointed remnants and dregs [?]. As for the Basic Classic (Yuan jing), its treatment of the rulers of the two Wei states as emperors, its demotion of Shu-Han, and its treatment of Jiangzuo as barbarian already render its central purport perverse. Thus commentators call Wang Tong presumptuous as well.

As for Model Sayings (Fayan) and Discussions of the Mean (Zhongshuo), although they seem in places to derive from imitation and plagiarism, they often manage to honor the correct Way and elucidate subtle teachings a thousand years later. Yet in Model Sayings, the language is often remote while its meaning is close at hand, so it cannot escape obscurity. In Discussions of the Mean, although the exposition is fluent, the reasoning sometimes strays, so it cannot escape a mixture of sound and unsound ideas. Some even argue that Wang Tong and Li Deming did not overlap in time, and that, among the eminent ministers of the early Tang who styled themselves his disciples, not a single mention is made …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
其名以爲阮逸之僞撰雖未必盡然要之
亦有可疑者矣宋興周程氏者出盖盡屛
諸儒之說而擇於道德醇如也周氏之爲
太極圖說也標理於極而推功於靜其爲
通書也表裏太極之說而加詳於聖賢之
學程氏之答定性書謂已性無內外動亦
定靜亦定也張氏之作西銘謂理一而分
殊人當以事親之道事天也邵氏之皇極
經世諸篇明天地之消長推日月之盈縮
===
與陰陽之度數剛柔之形體經之以元紀
之以會參之以運終之以世盖得易之變
而推廣之者也要之其爲說雖正大而纖
妙然豈有出於六經之外哉楊雄王通氏
急於得經之名而緩其實周程張邵氏精
於得經之實而避其名此所以異也而後
之持正論者必欲深文巧詆以中通雄之
罪至目之爲僭竊等之爲異類盖至於莽
大夫楊雄死而千秋不傳之統直接之孟
punctuated: 其名，以爲阮逸之僞撰。雖未必盡然，要之亦有可疑者矣。宋興，周程氏者出，盖盡屛諸儒之說而擇於道德，醇如也。周氏之爲《太極圖說》也，標理於極而推功於靜；其爲《通書》也，表裏太極之說而加詳於聖賢之學。程氏之《答定性書》，謂已性無內外，動亦定，靜亦定也。張氏之作《西銘》，謂理一而分殊，人當以事親之道事天也。邵氏之《皇極經世》諸篇，明天地之消長，推日月之盈縮，與陰陽之度數、剛柔之形體，經之以元，紀之以會，參之以運，終之以世，盖得《易》之變而推廣之者也。要之，其爲說雖正大而纖妙，然豈有出於六經之外哉？楊雄、王通氏急於得經之名而緩其實，周、程、張、邵氏精於得經之實而避其名，此所以異也。而後之持正論者，必欲深文巧詆，以中通、雄之罪，至目之爲僭竊，等之爲異類。盖至於莽大夫楊雄死，而千秋不傳之統直接之孟
translation_en:
…his name, and regard the work as a spurious composition by Ruan Yi. Although this may not be entirely so, there are, in any case, grounds for doubt.

With the rise of the Song, Zhou Dunyi and the Cheng brothers appeared. They largely set aside the teachings of the various scholars and selected what accorded with the Way and virtue; their learning was thoroughly pure. In his Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate (Taijitu shuo), Zhou located principle in the Supreme Ultimate and attributed efficacy to stillness. His Penetrating the Book of Changes (Tongshu) complemented his explanation of the Supreme Ultimate and elaborated on the learning of sages and worthies. Cheng Yi’s Reply on Settling the Nature maintained that one’s own nature [?] has neither an inside nor an outside: it is settled in activity and settled in stillness. Zhang Zai’s Western Inscription (Ximing) maintained that principle is one but its particular manifestations differ, and that people should serve Heaven as they serve their parents. The chapters of Shao Yong’s Supreme Principles Governing the World (Huangji jingshi) elucidated the waxing and waning of Heaven and Earth and investigated the advance and retardation of the sun and moon, together with the measures and numbers of yin and yang and the forms and substance of the firm and yielding. He ordered these by epochs (yuan), arranged them by conjunctions (hui), coordinated them by cycles (yun), and completed the scheme with generations (shi). He thus grasped the transformations of the Book of Changes and extended their application.

In sum, although their explanations were grand and correct, subtle and refined, how could any of them go beyond the Six Classics? Yang Xiong and Wang Tong were eager to obtain the name of a classic but gave less attention to its substance. Zhou, the Cheng brothers, Zhang, and Shao devoted themselves to attaining the substance of the classics while avoiding the name. This is what distinguishes them. Yet later proponents of orthodox judgments insisted on strained interpretations and artful disparagement to convict Wang Tong and Yang Xiong of wrongdoing. They went so far as to brand them usurpers and plagiarists and rank them among the heterodox. Indeed, they went so far as to declare Yang Xiong, Grand Master under Wang Mang, dead, and to connect the succession that had gone untransmitted for a thousand years directly to Meng…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
氏愚以爲六經至孔子而止矣即孟氏與
宋諸賢亦翼而明之廣而通之者也特所
謂爝者其光有大小而佐日月之功有隆
殺耳夫陽避其名而陰紹其統愚不得爲
通雄二氏稱亟也孰事謂六經自秦火之
後不能不有所遺錯以討定之責責雄通
氏愚謂非二氏所能辦也今請得而略言
之謂繫辭之十翼有非夫子所撰者序卦
之或强也而雜卦之或雜也謂乾坤之二
===
卦自彖象而外夫子所贊皆當屬之於繫
辭是一說也謂夫子曰放鄭聲而鄭衛淫
奔之詩不廢或曰放者聲耳存其篇以示
戒也或云非夫子之舊也周禮缺冬官矣
而河間獻王輒以考工記補之其能合於
聖人之政否也有謂五官之中如縣師廛
人之類皆在所少者惟王一條耳是一說
也大學缺格致矣而朱子輒取程子之意
補之其能合於聖人之心否也有謂知止
punctuated: 氏。愚以爲，六經至孔子而止矣，即孟氏與宋諸賢，亦翼而明之、廣而通之者也。特所謂爝者，其光有大小，而佐日月之功有隆殺耳。夫陽避其名而陰紹其統，愚不得爲通、雄二氏稱亟也。孰事謂六經自秦火之後，不能不有所遺錯，以討定之責責雄、通氏，愚謂非二氏所能辦也。今請得而略言之。謂繫辭之十翼有非夫子所撰者，序卦之或强也，而雜卦之或雜也；謂乾坤之二卦，自彖象而外，夫子所贊皆當屬之於繫辭，是一說也。謂夫子曰「放鄭聲」，而鄭衛淫奔之詩不廢，或曰：「放者聲耳，存其篇以示戒也。」或云：「非夫子之舊也。」周禮缺冬官矣，而河間獻王輒以考工記補之，其能合於聖人之政否也？有謂五官之中，如縣師、廛人之類皆在，所少者惟王一條耳，是一說也。大學缺格致矣，而朱子輒取程子之意補之，其能合於聖人之心否也？有謂知止
translation_en:
…Meng. In my humble view, the Six Classics reached their culmination with Confucius. Even Master Meng and the worthy scholars of the Song merely assisted and elucidated them, expanded their meaning and made it accessible. They were simply what one might call torches: their light varied in strength, and their contribution in assisting the sun and moon varied in degree. As for openly shunning the name while privately continuing the orthodox succession, I cannot praise Wang Tong and Yang Xiong on this account [?]. As for the claim [?] that, after the Qin burning of the books, the Six Classics inevitably contained omissions and errors, and that Yang Xiong and Wang Tong should be held responsible for examining and settling these, I consider this beyond the abilities of those two men. Let me now discuss the matter briefly.

It is said that some of the Ten Wings appended to the Book of Changes were not composed by the Master: the Sequence of the Hexagrams sometimes forces its explanations, while the Miscellaneous Hexagrams is sometimes confused. It is also said that, apart from the Commentaries on the Judgments and Images, all the Master's explanatory remarks on the two hexagrams Qian and Kun should be assigned to the Appended Statements. This is one interpretation.

It is said that the Master declared, “Banish the music of Zheng,” yet the poems of Zheng and Wei concerning licentious liaisons were not discarded. Some say: “What he banished was only the music; he preserved the texts to provide warnings.” Others say: “This is not what the Master originally left us.”

The Rites of Zhou lacks the section on the Minister of Works, yet Prince Xian of Hejian proceeded to supplement it with the Record of Artificers. Could this accord with the sage's government? Some maintain that officials such as the District Masters and the Market Officers are all present among the five ministries, and that only a single entry concerning the king is missing. This is one interpretation.

The Great Learning lacks its treatment of investigating things and extending knowledge, yet Master Zhu proceeded to draw on Master Cheng's ideas to supplement it. Could this accord with the sage's mind? Some maintain that the passage on knowing where to rest…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
末二條即格致之一章固不缺也是亦一
說也禮記所載大學中庸既別表爲一書
而其它篇多不出於夫子緇衣公孫尼子
所撰也月令呂不韋所脩也王制漢文時
博士所錄也其它檀弓儒行等篇要亦有
大醇而小疵者至於春秋一書左氏詳於
事而畧於旨公穀守其虛而忘其實穀梁
以衛輒拒父爲尊祖不納子糾爲內惡公
羊以祭仲廢君爲行權妾母稱夫人爲合
===
正蓋范甯固已言之至於胡安國而始以
其說探聖人之心於千載之上然聖人之
賞罰固已明而聖人之所以用其賞罰者
未免流於刻也夫所謂廣而通之者固不
暇論而所謂翼而明之者其亦有人矣乎
諸儒生遵
高皇之訓白首守其師說而不敢廢愚則何敢
言愚所謂書之有古文雖稍異其語易大
學之有古本雖稍更其序而大旨不甚遠
punctuated:
末二條，即格致之一章，固不缺也，是亦一說也。《禮記》所載《大學》《中庸》，既別表爲一書，而其它篇多不出於夫子。《緇衣》，公孫尼子所撰也；《月令》，呂不韋所脩也；《王制》，漢文時博士所錄也。其它《檀弓》《儒行》等篇，要亦有大醇而小疵者。至於《春秋》一書，左氏詳於事而畧於旨，公、穀守其虛而忘其實。《穀梁》以衛輒拒父爲尊祖，不納子糾爲內惡；《公羊》以祭仲廢君爲行權，妾母稱夫人爲合正。蓋范甯固已言之。至於胡安國，而始以其說探聖人之心於千載之上。然聖人之賞罰固已明，而聖人之所以用其賞罰者，未免流於刻也。夫所謂廣而通之者，固不暇論，而所謂翼而明之者，其亦有人矣乎？
諸儒生遵高皇之訓，白首守其師說而不敢廢，愚則何敢言？愚所謂《書》之有古文，雖稍異其語；《易》《大學》之有古本，雖稍更其序，而大旨不甚遠。
translation_en:
…the final two sections constitute the chapter on investigating things and extending knowledge, so that nothing was missing in the first place. This, too, is one interpretation. The Great Learning and the Doctrine of the Mean, contained in the Record of Rites, have already been singled out as separate books, while many of its other chapters did not originate with Confucius. “Black Robes” was composed by Gongsun Nizi; “Monthly Ordinances” was compiled by Lü Buwei; and “Royal Regulations” was recorded by Erudites during the reign of Emperor Wen of Han. Other chapters, such as “Tan Gong” and “The Conduct of Scholars,” likewise include some that are largely sound but have minor flaws. As for the Spring and Autumn Annals, Zuo’s commentary is detailed about events but brief about their meaning, while the Gongyang and Guliang commentaries cling to abstractions and lose sight of actual circumstances. The Guliang Commentary treats Zhe of Wei’s rejection of his father as honoring his grandfather, and the failure to admit Zijiu as wrongdoing within the state. The Gongyang Commentary treats Ji Zhong’s deposition of his ruler as an exercise of discretionary judgment, and the designation of a ruler’s mother who had been a concubine as “Lady” as conforming to what is proper. Fan Ning had already spoken of these matters. Only with Hu Anguo was an interpretation advanced that sought to fathom the mind of the Sage more than a thousand years earlier. Yet, although the Sage’s rewards and punishments were thereby made clear, the account of his reasons for applying them could not avoid tending toward excessive severity. As for what is called expanding upon the classics and comprehending them thoroughly, there is certainly no time to discuss it; but have there indeed been people who have accomplished what is called supplementing and elucidating them?
The scholars obey the instructions of Emperor Gao, keeping to their teachers’ interpretations until their hair turns white and not daring to abandon them. How, then, would I dare to speak? What I mean is that, although the ancient-script text of the Book of Documents differs somewhat in wording, and although the ancient versions of the Book of Changes and the Great Learning differ somewhat in their arrangement, their principal meanings do not diverge very far …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
固無可論詩之淫風存者出於夫子之手
孰得而議之第在鄭衛則絀它說而附於
淫在異國則又絀其淫而附於它說不知
可更一裁定否也周禮之冬官或悉取五
官之屬者而補之簡升劉歆之傳會合儀
禮禮記而爲一經可乎取月令檀弓緇衣
王制儒行之類稍未醇者取家語及魯論
之爲門弟子言者各降而爲傳以與孟氏
並傳可乎取左氏之事而絀其浮取公羊
===
之例而絀其鑿取穀梁之旨而絀其偏裁
以胡氏之法而絀其刻更定爲一書可乎
要之非其急者自强不息而吾心之易在
矣允執厥中而吾心之書在矣思無邪而
吾心之詩在矣毋不敬而吾心之禮在矣
春王正月而吾心之春秋在矣得其要則
六經爲吾用而其語皆筌蹄不得其要則
吾爲六經役老死而汩汩於章句雖然愚
之所甚憂則不在此今世之學者於書偶
punctuated:
固無可論。詩之淫風存者，出於夫子之手，孰得而議之？第在鄭衛，則絀它說而附於淫；在異國，則又絀其淫而附於它說，不知可更一裁定否也？周禮之冬官，或悉取五官之屬者而補之，簡升劉歆之傳會，合儀禮、禮記而爲一經，可乎？取月令、檀弓、緇衣、王制、儒行之類稍未醇者，取家語及魯論之爲門弟子言者，各降而爲傳，以與孟氏並傳，可乎？取左氏之事而絀其浮，取公羊之例而絀其鑿，取穀梁之旨而絀其偏，裁以胡氏之法而絀其刻，更定爲一書，可乎？

要之，非其急者。自强不息，而吾心之易在矣；允執厥中，而吾心之書在矣；思無邪，而吾心之詩在矣；毋不敬，而吾心之禮在矣；春王正月，而吾心之春秋在矣。得其要，則六經爲吾用，而其語皆筌蹄；不得其要，則吾爲六經役，老死而汩汩於章句。雖然，愚之所甚憂則不在此。今世之學者，於書偶
translation_en:
…there is certainly nothing to dispute. The licentious airs preserved in the Book of Odes passed through the Master's hands: who could question them? Yet for those of Zheng and Wei, other interpretations are rejected and the poems assigned to licentiousness; for those of other states, licentiousness is rejected and other interpretations adopted. I wonder whether these judgments might be reconsidered. As for the missing Offices of Winter in the Rites of Zhou, might one gather all the relevant offices subordinate to the other five ministries to fill the gap, sift out Liu Xin's forced associations [?], and combine the Ceremonies and Rites and the Record of Rites into a single classic? Might one take such somewhat less pure chapters as the Monthly Ordinances, Tan Gong, the Black Robes, Royal Regulations, and the Conduct of Scholars, together with those portions of the Family Sayings of Confucius and the Lu Analects that consist of disciples' words, and demote each to the status of commentary, to be transmitted alongside the works of Master Meng? Might one take the historical accounts of Master Zuo while rejecting their extravagances, the interpretive precedents of Gongyang while rejecting their strained explanations, and the purport of Guliang while rejecting its partiality, judging them by Master Hu's methods while rejecting his harshness, and revise them into a single book?

In any event, these are not the urgent matters. Through unceasing self-strengthening, the Changes is present within my heart; through sincerely holding to the mean, the Documents is present within my heart; through having no wayward thoughts, the Odes is present within my heart; through being reverent in all things, the Rites is present within my heart; through understanding “Spring, the king's first month,” the Spring and Autumn Annals is present within my heart. If I grasp their essentials, the Six Classics serve my purposes, and their words are merely fish traps and rabbit snares—means to an end. If I fail to grasp their essentials, I become a slave to the Six Classics, growing old and dying immersed in chapters and phrases. Nevertheless, what concerns me most deeply does not lie here. Scholars of the present day, when in their reading they happen to…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
有所窺則欲盡廢先儒之說而出其上於
道未有所得則已力排先儒之詰而閏其
統不學則借聖門之一以文其陋無行則
逃之性命之鄉以使人不可詰此又宋賢
之罪人而楊雄王通氏之所近似而不取
者也愚之所甚憂者此也
第三問
同考試官教諭李　批　〔從祀重典未易輕議子能考究〕
渠兆昌
考試官教諭謝　批　〔斟酌且懷懷致望之意溢於言外宜取以式　議有體且忠存重〕
考試官教諭馬　批　〔條對精悉可與言禮〕
===
明功德可取
太廟之有從祀者謂能佐其主行斯世之治統
也以報功也文廟之有從祀者謂能佐其
師行斯世之道統也亦以報功也其典歸
之秩宗而其議掌之太常雖德之者不能
舉無功之祀怨之者不能廢應祀之功斯
punctuated:
有所窺，則欲盡廢先儒之說而出其上；於道未有所得，則已力排先儒之詰而閏其統。不學，則借聖門之一以文其陋；無行，則逃之性命之鄉，以使人不可詰。此又宋賢之罪人，而楊雄、王通氏之所近似而不取者也。愚之所甚憂者，此也。

第三問

同考試官教諭李，批：〔從祀重典，未易輕議，子能考究〕

渠兆昌

考試官教諭謝，批：〔斟酌且懷懷致望之意溢於言外，宜取以式。議有體且忠存重〕

考試官教諭馬，批：〔條對精悉，可與言禮〕

明功德，可取。

太廟之有從祀者，謂能佐其主行斯世之治統也，以報功也。文廟之有從祀者，謂能佐其師行斯世之道統也，亦以報功也。其典歸之秩宗，而其議掌之太常。雖德之者不能舉無功之祀，怨之者不能廢應祀之功。斯
translation_en:
…gain some glimpse of understanding in books, they wish to discard all the explanations of earlier Confucian scholars and rise above them. Before gaining any understanding of the Way, they already vigorously reject the earlier scholars’ challenges [?] and insert themselves irregularly into their succession. Without learning, they borrow the sage’s teaching of “the one” to disguise their ignorance; without virtuous conduct, they retreat into the realm of human nature and destiny so that others cannot question them. Such people also offend against the worthies of the Song; theirs is the kind of superficial resemblance that Yang Xiong and Wang Tong rejected [?]. This is what concerns me most.

Third Question

Associate Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“Associated worship is a major rite and cannot readily be discussed lightly. You have been able to investigate it.”〕

Qu Zhaochang

Examiner Xie, Instructor, comments: 〔“Carefully weighed, and the sense of concern and expectation [?] overflows beyond the words. It should be selected as a model. The discussion is properly framed, loyal, and mindful of the gravity of the matter [?].”〕

Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: 〔“The responses to the individual points are precise and thorough. This is someone with whom one can discuss ritual.”〕

“Clarifies achievement and virtue; worthy of selection.”

Those accorded associated worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple are so honored because they were able to assist their rulers in carrying forward the succession of governance in this world: it is to repay their service. Those accorded associated worship in the Temple of Confucius are so honored because they were able to assist their teachers in carrying forward the succession of the Way in this world: this too is to repay their service. The regulations governing these rites fall to the Minister of Rites, and deliberations concerning them are entrusted to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices. Even those grateful to a person cannot institute worship for one without merit; those who resent a person cannot abolish worship warranted by that person’s service. This…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
禮也人主行之以厚道而待之以公道者
也蓋愚嘗讀商盤庚之告曰茲予大饗於
先王爾祖其從饗之及洛誥曰記功宗以
功作元祀而後知先王之用情於其臣也
又嘗讀周禮大司樂以治建國之學政而
合國之子弟凡有道有德者使敎焉死則
以爲樂祖祭於瞽宗而後知先王之用情
於其師也生而共其祿於朝死而共其饗
於廟而君臣之體一矣生而以茲地嗣其
===
敎沒而以茲地配其饗而師弟子之體一
矣夫禮有其舉之莫敢廢也禮舉矣而不
備於盛世君子之所以爲禮恥也禮備矣
而世無其人以應之君子之所以爲盛世
恥也
太廟之有從祀其制見於周而其議詳於高堂
隆任茂大抵以一代之臣配一代之君而
已至唐而可考者淮安靖王神通梁文昭
公房玄齡而下距太尉李愬凡三十二人
punctuated:
禮也，人主行之以厚道，而待之以公道者也。蓋愚嘗讀商盤庚之告曰：「茲予大饗於先王，爾祖其從饗之。」及洛誥曰：「記功，宗以功作元祀。」而後知先王之用情於其臣也。又嘗讀周禮大司樂：「以治建國之學政，而合國之子弟。凡有道有德者，使敎焉；死則以爲樂祖，祭於瞽宗。」而後知先王之用情於其師也。生而共其祿於朝，死而共其饗於廟，而君臣之體一矣；生而以茲地嗣其敎，沒而以茲地配其饗，而師弟子之體一矣。夫禮有其舉之，莫敢廢也。禮舉矣，而不備於盛世，君子之所以爲禮恥也；禮備矣，而世無其人以應之，君子之所以爲盛世恥也。

太廟之有從祀，其制見於周，而其議詳於高堂隆、任茂，大抵以一代之臣配一代之君而已。至唐而可考者，淮安靖王神通、梁文昭公房玄齡，而下距太尉李愬，凡三十二人
translation_en:
…is ritual: the ruler carries it out with generosity and treats those concerned with impartiality. I have read the declaration of Pan Geng of Shang: “Now, when I offer the great sacrifice to the former kings, your ancestors shall share in their offerings”; and the Announcement concerning Luo: “Record achievements, and honor merit by instituting the great sacrifices” [?]. Only then did I understand the former kings’ affection for their ministers. I have also read, in the section on the Music Master in the Rites of Zhou: “He administers the educational affairs of the capital and assembles the sons and younger brothers of the state. All who possess the Way and virtue are employed as teachers; after their deaths, they are made ancestral masters of music and receive sacrifices at the Hall of the Blind Musicians.” Only then did I understand the former kings’ affection for their teachers. In life, ministers share in their ruler’s emoluments at court; in death, they share in his sacrificial offerings in the ancestral temple. Thus ruler and ministers form one body. While a teacher lives, his teaching is carried on in this place; after his death, he shares in the sacrificial offerings made there. Thus teacher and disciples form one body. Once a rite has been instituted, none dares abolish it. When rites have been instituted but remain incomplete in a flourishing age, the gentleman regards this as a disgrace to ritual. When rites are complete but the age produces no one worthy of them, the gentleman regards this as a disgrace to the flourishing age.

The institution of associated worship in the Imperial Ancestral Temple is attested under the Zhou, and its discussion is elaborated by Gaotang Long and Ren Mao. Broadly speaking, it simply associates the ministers of a dynasty with the rulers of that dynasty in worship. Under the Tang, those who can be verified begin with Shentong, Prince Jing of Huai’an, and Fang Xuanling, Duke Wenzhao of Liang, and extend down to the Defender-in-Chief Li Su, thirty-two men in all…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
也至宋而可考者韓忠獻王趙普濟陽忠
武王曹彬而下距承相葛邲凡二十四人
也其它固代不絕也夫金裔夷耳而猶能
舉斜也粘沒喝兀朮張浩董之祀而況不
爲金者乎文廟之有從祀其禮起於漢延
光而其議定於唐貞觀大抵以其有功於
聖經而已而不必盡論其人也故貞觀之
詔自左丘明卜子夏而下距范甯賈逵人
蓋二十二也宋至元豐而益者荀況楊雄
韓愈也至淳祐而益者周敦頤張載程顥
程頤朱熹也至景定而益者邵雍司馬光
也其它固代不乏也夫元荒虜耳尚能進
董仲舒而其人有許衡吳澄者應之而況
不爲元者乎
===
明興
高皇帝之初念無以昭宣諸功臣之烈建
太廟首議以李韓公善長等六公及胡越公大
海等從饗最後韓公坐嫌死而六公亦間
punctuated:
也。至宋而可考者，韓忠獻王趙普、濟陽忠武王曹彬，而下距承相葛邲，凡二十四人也。其它固代不絕也。夫金，裔夷耳，而猶能舉斜也、粘沒喝、兀朮、張浩、董之祀，而況不爲金者乎？
文廟之有從祀，其禮起於漢延光，而其議定於唐貞觀，大抵以其有功於聖經而已，而不必盡論其人也。故貞觀之詔，自左丘明、卜子夏而下距范甯、賈逵，人蓋二十二也。宋至元豐而益者，荀況、楊雄、韓愈也；至淳祐而益者，周敦頤、張載、程顥、程頤、朱熹也；至景定而益者，邵雍、司馬光也。其它固代不乏也。夫元，荒虜耳，尚能進董仲舒，而其人有許衡、吳澄者應之，而況不爲元者乎？
明興，高皇帝之初，念無以昭宣諸功臣之烈，建太廟，首議以李韓公善長等六公及胡越公大海等從饗。最後韓公坐嫌死，而六公亦間
translation_en:
… in all. In the Song, those whose cases can be traced range from Zhao Pu, Prince Zhongxian of Han, and Cao Bin, Prince Zhongwu of Jiyang, down to Chief Councilor Ge Bi: twenty-four men in all. Other instances certainly continued in every dynasty. The Jin were merely barbarians from the distant margins, yet even they could institute sacrifices to Xieye, Nianmohe, Wuzhu, Zhang Hao, and Dong [?]. How much more should those who are unlike the Jin do so?
As for associated worship in the Temple of Confucius, the rite originated in the Yanguang era of the Han, and deliberations concerning it were settled in the Zhenguan era of the Tang. Broadly speaking, inclusion rested simply on contributions to the sages’ classics; it did not necessarily require a comprehensive assessment of each man’s character. Thus the Zhenguan edict named some twenty-two men, from Zuo Qiuming and Bu Zixia down to Fan Ning and Jia Kui. Under the Song, Xun Kuang, Yang Xiong, and Han Yu were added in the Yuanfeng era; Zhou Dunyi, Zhang Zai, Cheng Hao, Cheng Yi, and Zhu Xi in the Chunyou era; and Shao Yong and Sima Guang in the Jingding era. Other instances certainly were not lacking in any dynasty. The Yuan were merely uncivilized barbarians, yet they could still elevate Dong Zhongshu to associated worship, and among their own men there were Xu Heng and Wu Cheng to meet this standard. How much more should those who are unlike the Yuan do so?
When the Ming arose, in the early years of Emperor Gao’s reign, he reflected that there was no means of making manifest the achievements of his meritorious ministers. He built the Imperial Ancestral Temple and first proposed that six dukes, including Li Shanchang, Duke of Han, together with Hu Dahai, Duke of Yue, and others, share in its sacrificial offerings. Eventually the Duke of Han was put to death on suspicion, and the six dukes also at times …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
不得與遂永樂而始定自中山開平二王
而下距永義侯世傑凡六王五公一侯十
二人從
文皇帝祀者至洪熙而定文武臣惟河間王玉
東平王能寧國公眞榮國公廣孝二王二
公而已
先皇帝之世於
宗廟大典蓋惓惓焉首上
太祖徽號及追上
===
文皇帝祖號已采禮官言進誠意伯基從祀
太祖位六王下而以僧故斥廣孝使祀大興隆
寺尋用翊國公勛請進其祖營國公英于天
下不以私病英而以公快基廣孝謂英功
足稱也獨
仁宣而後寥寥無聞者過也夫承平之世先文
德而後武功則
列聖之丕承宣明治道抑何章章著隆也忍使
萬世之後謂
punctuated:
不得與，遂永樂而始定：自中山、開平二王而下，距永義侯世傑，凡六王、五公、一侯，十二人。從文皇帝祀者，至洪熙而定，文武臣惟河間王玉、東平王能、寧國公眞、榮國公廣孝，二王二公而已。
先皇帝之世，於宗廟大典蓋惓惓焉。首上太祖徽號，及追上文皇帝祖號，已采禮官言，進誠意伯基從祀太祖，位六王下，而以僧故斥廣孝，使祀大興隆寺。尋用翊國公勛請，進其祖營國公英。于天下，不以私病英，而以公快基、廣孝，謂英功足稱也。獨仁宣而後，寥寥無聞者，過也。夫承平之世，先文德而後武功，則列聖之丕承宣明治道，抑何章章著隆也！忍使萬世之後謂
translation_en:
…were denied participation, and only in the Yongle reign was the arrangement finally settled: from the two princes of Zhongshan and Kaiping down to Shijie, Marquis of Yongyi, there were twelve men in all—six princes, five dukes, and one marquis. Those receiving sacrifices alongside Emperor Wen were determined in the Hongxi reign. Among the civil and military ministers, they comprised only Yu, Prince of Hejian; Neng, Prince of Dongping; Zhen, Duke of Ningguo; and Guangxiao, Duke of Rongguo—two princes and two dukes.
During the late emperor’s reign, he devoted earnest attention to the great rites of the imperial ancestral temple. First he conferred an honorific title upon Taizu and posthumously conferred upon Emperor Wen a temple title designating him an ancestral founder. Subsequently, adopting the ritual officials’ advice, he admitted Ji, Earl of Chengyi, to receive sacrifices alongside Taizu, placing him below the six princes. He excluded Guangxiao because he had been a Buddhist monk and directed that sacrifices to him be offered at Daxinglong Temple. Soon afterward, acting on the petition of Xun, Duke of Yi, he admitted Xun’s ancestor Ying, Duke of Ying. Throughout the realm, people did not condemn Ying’s admission as favoritism, but applauded the fairness of the decisions concerning Ji and Guangxiao [?], holding that Ying’s achievements sufficiently warranted recognition. Yet it is a failing that, after the Ren and Xuan reigns, so few such cases have been heard of. In times of peace, civil virtue takes precedence over military achievement. How conspicuously, then, did the successive sage emperors, in their grand continuation of the imperial inheritance, manifest and exalt the principles of good government! Can we bear to let people, ten thousand generations hence, say…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
明有君而無臣不得比於唐高宋眞之季耶夫
以楊文貞李文達商文毅劉文靖楊文忠
之賢於輔而不得從蹇忠定王忠肅王端
毅馬端肅之賢於銓而不得從于肅愍之
賢於樞而不得從張定興輔之三下南交
朱宣平彖之八佩將印皆位太師握環衛
爲心膂而不得從何也其人縱不能
與中山開平等豈盡出世傑眞下耶愚以
爲禮官臺臣當一建白下公卿大夫博議
===
而精覈之進其灼然者不爲過也
高皇帝又念無以表楊我先師之道
詔革天下神號而獨不以及夫子且謂所封爵
及諸從祀者俱如故至正統而益以胡安
國蔡沈眞德秀吳澄
先皇帝之世於文廟大禮愈惓惓焉凡再釋奠
幸太學爵改王而爲師神改像而爲主佾改
八而爲六藿前是從祀者奪楊雄矣已采
輔臣言退荀況馬融劉向賈逵王弼何休
punctuated:
明有君而無臣，不得比於唐高宋眞之季耶？夫以楊文貞、李文達、商文毅、劉文靖、楊文忠之賢於輔而不得從，蹇忠定、王忠肅、王端毅、馬端肅之賢於銓而不得從，于肅愍之賢於樞而不得從，張定興輔之三下南交、朱宣平彖之八佩將印，皆位太師，握環衛，爲心膂而不得從，何也？其人縱不能與中山、開平等，豈盡出世傑、眞下耶？愚以爲禮官臺臣當一建白，下公卿大夫博議而精覈之，進其灼然者，不爲過也。
高皇帝又念無以表楊我先師之道，詔革天下神號，而獨不以及夫子，且謂所封爵及諸從祀者俱如故。至正統而益以胡安國、蔡沈、眞德秀、吳澄。先皇帝之世，於文廟大禮愈惓惓焉。凡再釋奠，幸太學，爵改王而爲師，神改像而爲主，佾改八而爲六。藿前是從祀者奪楊雄矣，已采輔臣言，退荀況、馬融、劉向、賈逵、王弼、何休
translation_en:
…that the Ming had rulers but no worthy ministers, and could not compare with the times of Gaozu of Tang and Zhenzong of Song? Consider the worthiness of Yang Wenzhen, Li Wenda, Shang Wenyi, Liu Wenjing, and Yang Wenzhong as grand secretaries, yet none has been admitted to accompanying worship. Consider Jian Zhongding, Wang Zhongsu, Wang Duanyi, and Ma Duansu, so worthy in administering official appointments, yet likewise excluded; and Yu Sumin, so worthy in directing military affairs, yet also excluded. Zhang Fu, Duke of Dingxing, subdued Nanjiao three times; Zhu Tuan [?], Earl of Xuanping, bore a general’s seal eight times. Both held the rank of Grand Preceptor, commanded the palace guards, and served as the sovereign’s trusted mainstays, yet neither has been admitted to accompanying worship. Why? Even if these men cannot equal the dukes of Zhongshan and Kaiping, can they all rank below Shijie and Zhen [?]? In my humble opinion, the ritual officials and censorial officials should submit a proposal, referring the matter to the high ministers and other officials for broad deliberation and careful scrutiny. Admitting those whose merits are unmistakable would not be excessive.
Emperor Gao also reflected that there was no adequate means of making manifest the Way of our First Teacher. He decreed the abolition of divine titles throughout the realm, but expressly exempted the Master, stating moreover that his conferred noble title and all those receiving accompanying worship should remain as before. In the Zhengtong reign, Hu Anguo, Cai Shen, Zhen Dexiu, and Wu Cheng were added. In the late emperor’s reign, still greater solicitude was shown toward the great rites of the Confucian Temple. Twice he performed the sacrificial offering ceremony and visited the Imperial University. The title was changed from king to teacher, the sacred image was replaced with a spirit tablet, and the ranks of dancers were reduced from eight to six. Previously [?], Yang Xiong had already been removed from accompanying worship. Subsequently, adopting the advice of his grand secretaries, he removed Xun Kuang, Ma Rong, Liu Xiang, Jia Kui, Wang Bi, He Xiu…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
戴聖王肅杜預吳澄而能其祀抑鄭衆盧
植鄭玄服虔范甯而祀於鄉進王通胡瑗
楊時蔡元定最後以濮議故進歐陽脩天
下不以私訾脩而以公許王通等謂脩學
足稱也然此皆先世儒耳至於
明而獨寥寥著過也夫治統與道統而俱盛即
列聖之嗣德揚謝教化抑何孜孜不替也忍使
萬世之後謂
明以功而不以德至不獲比於元馬上之俗耶
當嘉靖中言者請進薛文清瑄從祀會議
且定矣一二沮之者謂其鮮著述無大裨
益
天子伸其說而屈其請令
上初言者欲併合王文安守仁陳檢討獻章而
祀之復下羣臣議其許瑄者十而九其許
守仁獻章者十而二三而卒莫定也豈非
以瑄經行淳備篤信守死出處以道有功
聖門至於守仁則因其致知而疑其慧於
punctuated:
戴聖、王肅、杜預、吳澄，而能其祀；抑鄭衆、盧植、鄭玄、服虔、范甯，而祀於鄉；進王通、胡瑗、楊時、蔡元定。最後以濮議故進歐陽脩，天下不以私訾脩，而以公許王通等，謂脩學足稱也。然此皆先世儒耳，至於明而獨寥寥，著過也。夫治統與道統而俱盛，即列聖之嗣德揚謝，教化抑何孜孜不替也！忍使萬世之後謂明以功而不以德，至不獲比於元馬上之俗耶？
當嘉靖中，言者請進薛文清瑄從祀，會議且定矣。一二沮之者謂其鮮著述，無大裨益。天子伸其說而屈其請。令上初，言者欲併合王文安守仁、陳檢討獻章而祀之，復下羣臣議。其許瑄者十而九，其許守仁、獻章者十而二三，而卒莫定也。豈非以瑄經行淳備，篤信守死，出處以道，有功聖門；至於守仁，則因其致知而疑其慧；於
translation_en:
…Dai Sheng, Wang Su, Du Yu, and Wu Cheng, and [discontinued?] their sacrificial honors [?]; he demoted Zheng Zhong, Lu Zhi, Zheng Xuan, Fu Qian, and Fan Ning, assigning them sacrifices in their native localities, and admitted Wang Tong, Hu Yuan, Yang Shi, and Cai Yuanding to accompanying worship. Finally, on account of the controversy over the Prince of Pu, he admitted Ouyang Xiu. People throughout the realm did not disparage Xiu out of private prejudice; rather, they approved Wang Tong and the others impartially and considered Xiu’s learning worthy of recognition. Yet these were all scholars of earlier ages. That the Ming alone should have so few is a manifest fault. Both the succession of governance and the transmission of the Way have flourished together. Our successive sage emperors have carried forward virtue and promoted it [?]; how tirelessly and unceasingly they have pursued moral instruction! Could we bear to let later generations say that the Ming excelled in achievement but not in virtue, and that it could not even match the horseback customs of the Yuan?
During the Jiajing reign, petitioners requested that Xue Xuan, posthumously titled Wenqing, be admitted to accompanying worship. The joint deliberations were nearly settled, but one or two opponents argued that he had written little and had made no great contribution. The Son of Heaven upheld their argument and rejected the petition. At the beginning of the present emperor’s reign [?], petitioners wished to include Wang Shouren, posthumously titled Wen’an [?], and Chen Xianzhang, an Examining Editor, in the sacrifices alongside him. The matter was again referred to the assembled officials for deliberation. Nine out of ten approved Xuan, while only two or three out of ten approved Shouren and Xianzhang; in the end, no decision was reached. Was this not because Xuan’s classical learning and conduct were pure and complete, because he held firm to his convictions and would defend the Way unto death, because he followed the Way both in taking office and in withdrawing, and because he had rendered service to the Confucian tradition? As for Shouren, his teaching of extending knowledge led them to suspect Buddhist wisdom in it; as for…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
獻章因其主靜而疑其寂耶其近於慧與
寂若其流之罪也非其師說也是三人者
縱不得與二程朱氏等豈盡出胡瑗楊時
下耶愚以爲禮官臺臣當再一建白下公
卿大夫博議而精覈之進其確然者不爲
過也然自
高帝諸功臣而下尚有說焉李韓公之佐開創
國不下鄭侯雖以嫌死
帝尚爲諱之若馮宋公勝之佐大將軍取中原
===
下秦隴降納哈出二十萬之衆傅穎公友
德之從大將軍取山東其平蜀功冠諸徹
侯而開滇南二百年之地惜其終於
帝之末遘革除之變而未有舉也勳烈固伯仲
岐陽而予永義矣縱不得從
太廟祀亦宜别於其鄉隆其贈謚而錄其後不
宜使子文之勳爲若敖氏之餒鬼也彼於
聖門而稱學者若吳聘君與弼之介胡布
衣居仁之敬魏恭簡校之端羅文毅倫文
punctuated:
獻章因其主靜而疑其寂耶？其近於慧與寂，若其流之罪也，非其師說也。是三人者，縱不得與二程朱氏等，豈盡出胡瑗楊時下耶？愚以爲禮官臺臣當再一建白，下公卿大夫博議而精覈之，進其確然者，不爲過也。
然自高帝諸功臣而下，尚有說焉。李韓公之佐開創國，不下鄭侯，雖以嫌死，帝尚爲諱之。若馮宋公勝之佐大將軍取中原，下秦隴，降納哈出二十萬之衆；傅穎公友德之從大將軍取山東，其平蜀功冠諸徹侯，而開滇南二百年之地，惜其終於帝之末，遘革除之變，而未有舉也。勳烈固伯仲岐陽，而予永義矣。縱不得從太廟祀，亦宜别於其鄉，隆其贈謚而錄其後，不宜使子文之勳爲若敖氏之餒鬼也。
彼於聖門而稱學者，若吳聘君與弼之介、胡布衣居仁之敬、魏恭簡校之端、羅文毅倫、文
translation_en:
…As for Xianzhang, is his emphasis on stillness grounds for suspecting him of quietism? If their teachings approach intuitive illumination and quietism, that would be the fault of their followers, not the teachings of the masters themselves. Even if these three men cannot rank alongside the two Cheng masters and Master Zhu, could they all rank below Hu Yuan and Yang Shi? In my humble opinion, the ritual officials and censorial officials should submit another proposal, referring it to the high ministers and other officials for broad deliberation and careful scrutiny. Advancing those whose qualifications are firmly established would not be excessive.
There is also something to be said concerning the meritorious servants of Emperor Gao and those who followed them. The assistance that Li, Duke of Han, gave in founding the state was no less than that of the Marquis of Zheng. Although he died under suspicion, the emperor still concealed the matter on his behalf. Consider Feng Sheng, Duke of Song, who assisted the General-in-Chief in taking the Central Plain, subduing Qin and Long, and securing the surrender of Nahachu’s force of two hundred thousand; or Fu Youde, Duke of Ying, who followed the General-in-Chief in taking Shandong, whose achievements in pacifying Shu surpassed those of all the marquises, and who opened up the territory of southern Yunnan that we have held for two hundred years. Alas, their lives ended in the emperor’s final years, they encountered the upheaval of the era subsequently expunged from the records [?], and no proposal has yet been made for them. Their glorious achievements certainly rivaled those of the Prince of Qiyang, but “bestow eternal righteousness” [?]. Even if they cannot receive accompanying sacrifices in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, separate sacrifices should be established in their native places, their posthumous honors and titles enhanced, and their descendants enrolled for official privilege. Men with merits like Ziwen’s should not be left as hungry ghosts of the Ruo’ao clan.
Among those acclaimed as scholars within the Confucian tradition are Wu Yubi, the scholar summoned to office, for his integrity; Hu Juren, a man without official rank, for his reverent attentiveness; Wei Jiao, posthumously titled Gongjian, for his uprightness; Luo Lun, posthumously titled Wenyi; and Wen…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
恭洪先之守似亦可祀於其鄉今恭簡有
專祀而諸君子未備不可一次第舉乎而
愚又有進於此者
先朝之黜漢儒凛乎斧鉞矣夫異漢者所以尊
宋而不知其背宋儒於背本也今令訓故之
學不傳卽明哲如二程朱子亦何所自而
釋其義乎愚以爲若盧鄭等者復其祀於
學而劉向吳澄輩專其祀於鄉可也斯禮
也愚能言之卽執事能聽之而議者未必
===
許也今天下難其典而易其人者何也遠
者不能悉其實而近者有所疑於心也愚
故曰斯禮也人主行之以厚道而持之以
公道者也
第四問
郝梴芳
同考試官教諭曾　批〔能發揮理財之所以難處而偶詳於節省夫亦不得已之意耶宏博而辨錄之〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔理財無奇策節儉其本也此作〕
punctuated:
恭洪先之守，似亦可祀於其鄉。今恭簡有專祀，而諸君子未備，不可一次第舉乎？而愚又有進於此者：先朝之黜漢儒，凛乎斧鉞矣。夫異漢者，所以尊宋，而不知其背宋儒於背本也。今令訓故之學不傳，卽明哲如二程、朱子，亦何所自而釋其義乎？愚以爲若盧、鄭等者，復其祀於學，而劉向、吳澄輩，專其祀於鄉，可也。斯禮也，愚能言之，卽執事能聽之，而議者未必許也。今天下難其典而易其人者，何也？遠者不能悉其實，而近者有所疑於心也。愚故曰：斯禮也，人主行之以厚道，而持之以公道者也。
第四問
郝梴芳
同考試官教諭曾　批〔能發揮理財之所以難處，而偶詳於節省，夫亦不得已之意耶？宏博而辨，錄之。〕
考試官教諭謝　批〔理財無奇策，節儉其本也。此作〕
translation_en:
…the steadfastness of Hongxian, posthumously honored as Wengong: it seems that they too might receive sacrifices in their native places. Gongjian now has a dedicated shrine, but provision for the other gentlemen remains incomplete. Could these observances not be instituted in succession? I have a further point to advance. The previous reign’s exclusion of the Han Confucians was as chilling as the executioner’s axe. Rejecting the Han scholars was intended to honor those of the Song, yet its proponents did not realize that, by abandoning the foundations, they were turning their backs on the Song Confucians themselves [?]. Suppose that the learning of textual glosses were no longer transmitted: even thinkers as enlightened as the two Cheng masters and Master Zhu would have no basis from which to elucidate the meaning of the texts. In my humble opinion, it would be appropriate to restore sacrifices to such men as Lu and Zheng in the schools, while providing dedicated sacrifices to men such as Liu Xiang and Wu Cheng in their native places. I can speak about this ritual, and you, sir, may be willing to listen; yet those deliberating the matter will not necessarily approve. Why is it that people today treat the establishment of these rites as difficult, yet treat the men themselves lightly? For those distant in time, they cannot fully ascertain the facts; concerning those nearer their own time, they harbor doubts. Thus I say: these rites are something the ruler should institute with generosity and uphold with impartiality.
Fourth Question
Hao Chanfang
Comment by Associate Examiner Zeng, Instructor: 〔He brings out the reasons why managing finances is difficult, though at points he dwells on economizing. Perhaps this too expresses the sense that there is no alternative? Broad in scope and discerning: accept it.〕
Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔There is no extraordinary strategy for managing finances; frugality is its foundation. This composition…〕

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
得之宜錄以俟主計者采焉
考試官教諭馬　批　節財盡矣文奇而愈取之
執事拳拳以理財之要下詢不佞書生也
授之握算不知縱横其何以仰佐末議干
主計者雖然敢不罄所見聞以對大抵富
國易富天下難富未開利之天下易富已
開利之天下難得人而專聽其法易以法
而強授之人難夫管子者古所稱能富國
者也今其書曰錯國於不傾之地積於不
===
涸之倉藏於不竭之府所謂倉與府者五
穀桑麻六畜而已其外則官山海所謂官
海者海鹽山鑄山籠百姓之利而收之官
而已又其外則制罪大小入以兵甲鈞金
奉矢而足五兵而已財有餘則借以使敵
知貴買莒楚代衡山之物以疲其上下之
力於物而已故天下弱於齊之富而齊霸
所謂能富國者也其次莫若計然計然之
書曰知鬭則脩備時用則知物二者形而
punctuated:
得之，宜錄以俟主計者采焉。
考試官教諭馬批：節財盡矣，文奇而愈取之。
執事拳拳以理財之要下詢，不佞書生也，授之握算，不知縱横，其何以仰佐末議，干主計者？雖然，敢不罄所見聞以對？大抵富國易，富天下難；富未開利之天下易，富已開利之天下難；得人而專聽其法易，以法而強授之人難。夫管子者，古所稱能富國者也。今其書曰：「錯國於不傾之地，積於不涸之倉，藏於不竭之府。」所謂倉與府者，五穀桑麻六畜而已。其外則官山海，所謂官海者，海鹽山鑄，山籠百姓之利而收之官而已。又其外則制罪大小，入以兵甲、鈞金、奉矢，而足五兵而已。財有餘，則借以使敵知貴，買莒、楚、代、衡山之物，以疲其上下之力於物而已。故天下弱於齊之富，而齊霸，所謂能富國者也。其次莫若計然。計然之書曰：「知鬭則脩備，時用則知物，二者形而
translation_en:
…has grasped it. This should be selected and retained for those in charge of finances to draw upon.
Examiner Ma, Instructor, comments: The subject of economizing on expenditure is exhaustively treated. The writing is striking, giving still more reason to select it [?].
You have earnestly condescended to ask about the essentials of managing finances. I am merely an unworthy student: give me counting rods to hold, and I would not know how to arrange them vertically or horizontally. How could I contribute even a humble opinion and venture to address those responsible for finances? Nevertheless, dare I fail to offer all that I have seen and heard in reply? Broadly speaking, enriching a state is easy; enriching all under Heaven is difficult. Enriching a realm whose sources of profit have yet to be developed is easy; enriching one whose sources of profit have already been developed is difficult. Finding the right person and giving his methods an exclusive hearing is easy; taking a method and forcing it upon someone is difficult.
Master Guan was renowned in antiquity for his ability to enrich a state. His book says: “Establish the state upon ground that cannot collapse; accumulate stores in granaries that cannot run dry; keep wealth in treasuries that cannot be exhausted.” These granaries and treasuries mean simply the five grains, mulberry and hemp, and the six kinds of livestock. Beyond these, there was state control of the mountains and seas. What is called control of the seas meant sea salt and mountain metal-casting, gathering the people’s sources of profit into official hands [?], and nothing more. Beyond this, penalties were graded according to the seriousness of offenses, with payments in weapons and armor, metal by the jun-weight, and arrows [?], thereby furnishing the five types of weapons, and nothing more. When there was surplus wealth, he used it to make enemy states recognize the high value of their goods [?], purchasing the products of Ju, Chu, Dai, and Hengshan so that both rulers and subjects exhausted their energies on those products. Thus the other states were weakened by Qi’s wealth, and Qi attained hegemony. This is what is meant by being able to enrich a state.
Next to him, none could compare with Ji Ran. Ji Ran’s book says: “Knowing of conflict, one makes preparations; knowing seasonal uses, one understands goods [?]. When these two become manifest, then…”

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
萬貨之情得故積著之理務完物無息幣
以物相貿易貴上極則反賤賤下極則反
貴貴出如糞土賤取如珠玉財幣欲其行
如流水行之十年而越大富以其貫傾吳
而橫行江淮間所謂能富國者也然此一
方耳四封之內皆鄰敵也其流易達而輸
易委盈縮易曉也我故得而發我之贏而
時中彼之急收彼之無用而爲我之有用
毋之權長在我而子之息長在彼肥我而
===
不憂彼之瘠損彼而不爲我之累故曰富
國易也若夫天下則不然盡四封之內外
而皆吾地也其人則皆吾人也肥在左則
瘠在右損在遠則累在近管子計然之策
有所�country而不必盡達也故曰富天下難也
漢武帝因文景之遺貲不勝其溢而侈怨
於匈奴已侈威於東韓西域南夷已又侈
其欲於宮室帷帳遊幸之事河决歲浸又
從而齮齕之蓋不數年而大農少府水衡
punctuated:
萬貨之情得。故積著之理，務完物，無息幣，以物相貿易。貴上極則反賤，賤下極則反貴。貴出如糞土，賤取如珠玉。財幣欲其行如流水。行之十年，而越大富，以其貫傾吳，而橫行江淮間，所謂能富國者也。然此一方耳，四封之內皆鄰敵也，其流易達而輸易委，盈縮易曉也。我故得而發我之贏，而時中彼之急，收彼之無用而爲我之有用。毋之權長在我，而子之息長在彼，肥我而不憂彼之瘠，損彼而不爲我之累，故曰富國易也。若夫天下則不然，盡四封之內外而皆吾地也，其人則皆吾人也。肥在左則瘠在右，損在遠則累在近。管子、計然之策，有所�country而不必盡達也，故曰富天下難也。
漢武帝因文景之遺貲，不勝其溢，而侈怨於匈奴，已侈威於東韓、西域、南夷，已又侈其欲於宮室、帷帳、遊幸之事。河决歲浸，又從而齮齕之。蓋不數年，而大農、少府、水衡
translation_en:
…the conditions governing all commodities can be understood. Thus, the principle of accumulating stocks is to keep goods in sound condition and never let money lie idle, exchanging goods for one another. When prices reach their highest point, they turn downward; when they reach their lowest point, they turn upward. When goods are dear, dispose of them as though they were dung and earth; when cheap, acquire them as though they were pearls and jade. Wealth and currency should circulate like flowing water. After these methods had been practiced for ten years, Yue became immensely wealthy. With its strings of cash it overthrew Wu and ranged unchecked between the Yangzi and Huai rivers. This is what is meant by being able to enrich a state. Yet this concerned only one region, surrounded on its four borders by neighboring enemies. The circulation of goods could readily get through, shipments could readily be brought together, and surpluses and shortages were easy to ascertain. Thus we could release our surplus to meet their urgent needs at the right moment, taking what was useless to them and making it useful to us. Control of the principal [?] would always remain with us, while the interest would continually come from them. We could enrich ourselves without worrying about their impoverishment, and diminish them without burdening ourselves. Hence it is said that enriching a state is easy. With all under Heaven, however, it is otherwise. Everything within and beyond the four borders is our territory, and all its people are our people. Enrichment on the left means impoverishment on the right; losses far away mean burdens close at hand. The policies of Guanzi and Ji Ran have their [text corrupt: �country] and do not necessarily apply in every circumstance. Hence it is said that enriching all under Heaven is difficult.
Emperor Wu of Han inherited the wealth left by Emperors Wen and Jing. Unable to contain its abundance, he indulged his enmity against the Xiongnu; then he made extravagant displays of might against Han in the east, the Western Regions, and the southern peoples; then again he indulged his desires for palaces, curtains and canopies, and imperial tours. Breaches of the Yellow River and yearly inundations further gnawed away at this wealth. In scarcely a few years, the Chamberlain for the National Treasury, the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, and the Chief Commandant of Waterways and Parks…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
之金錢米粟盡矣於是桑弘羊爲治粟都
尉筦天下鹽鐵乃請置大農郡丞分部主
郡國各往往縣置均輸鹽鐵官令遠方各
以其物貴時商賈所轉販者爲賦而相灌
輸置平準於京師大農之諸官盡籠天下
之貨物貴卽賣之賤則買之抑天下物名
曰平準又令吏入粟補官罪人得贖罪禁
盜鑄告緡錢算軺車船賈人一歲之中太
倉甘泉滿邊餘穀諸物均輸帛五百萬匹
===
民不益賦而天下用饒令世諸儒者掩口
不欲道弘羊弘羊故心計臣非諸齷齪儒
者比也雖然謂弘羊能開之則可謂弘羊
能生之則不可蓋漢興人主世世守共儉
宮室之湯沐不以煩大農而悉推山澤關
梁之利以予民民得恣取而無禁故農利
十一工利十二而商利十九至武帝國家
之用始不足而弘羊輩始得以其心計而
通利孔執事試屈指而籌令之天下於漢
punctuated:
之金錢米粟盡矣。於是桑弘羊爲治粟都尉，筦天下鹽鐵，乃請置大農郡丞，分部主郡國，各往往縣置均輸鹽鐵官，令遠方各以其物貴時商賈所轉販者爲賦，而相灌輸。置平準於京師，大農之諸官盡籠天下之貨物，貴卽賣之，賤則買之，抑天下物，名曰平準。又令吏入粟補官，罪人得贖罪，禁盜鑄，告緡錢，算軺車船賈人。一歲之中，太倉、甘泉滿，邊餘穀，諸物均輸，帛五百萬匹。民不益賦，而天下用饒。令世諸儒者掩口，不欲道弘羊。弘羊故心計臣，非諸齷齪儒者比也。

雖然，謂弘羊能開之則可，謂弘羊能生之則不可。蓋漢興，人主世世守共儉，宮室之湯沐不以煩大農，而悉推山澤關梁之利以予民。民得恣取而無禁，故農利十一，工利十二，而商利十九。至武帝，國家之用始不足，而弘羊輩始得以其心計而通利孔。執事試屈指而籌，令之天下於漢
translation_en:
…the money and grain held by the Chamberlain for the National Treasury, the Chamberlain for the Palace Revenues, and the Chief Commandant of Waterways were exhausted. Sang Hongyang then became Chief Commandant for Grain Management, controlling the empire’s salt and iron. He requested the appointment of commandery assistants under the Chamberlain for the National Treasury, each assigned a region and responsible for its commanderies and kingdoms, with equitable-transport and salt-and-iron officials established in counties at various locations. Distant regions were ordered to pay their levies in local goods that merchants transported and sold when prices were high, and these goods were circulated among the regions. A price-stabilization office was established in the capital. The offices under the Chamberlain for the National Treasury gathered the empire’s commodities into their control, selling when prices were high and buying when prices were low, thereby restraining commodity prices throughout the empire. This was called “price stabilization.” Officials were also permitted to obtain appointments by contributing grain, and convicted persons to redeem their punishments. Illicit minting was prohibited; concealment of taxable cash assets was subject to denunciation; and taxes were assessed on light carriages, boats, and merchants. Within a year, the Grand Granary and the granaries at Ganquan were full, the frontier had surplus grain, and goods of all kinds were supplied through equitable transport, including five million bolts of silk. Without increasing the people’s levies, the empire had abundant resources for its expenses. The Confucian scholars of the present age [?] cover their mouths and refuse to speak of Hongyang. Hongyang was indeed a minister skilled in financial calculation, beyond comparison with these petty, narrow-minded scholars.

Nevertheless, one may say that Hongyang could open up these resources, but not that he could create them. From the founding of the Han, successive rulers maintained reverent frugality. The palace’s personal revenues did not burden the Chamberlain for the National Treasury, and all the benefits of mountains, marshes, passes, and bridges were conceded to the people. The people could draw upon them freely, without prohibition. Thus agriculture yielded a profit of one tenth, crafts two tenths, and commerce nine tenths. Only under Emperor Wu did resources for state expenditure begin to fall short; only then did Hongyang and his fellows have the opportunity to use their financial calculations to open up channels of revenue. Sir, try counting on your fingers and reckoning how the empire of the present day [?], compared with the Han…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
賦財法禦所稱有一之不備者乎弘羊而
在吏何所加故曰富末開利之天下易富
已開利之天下難也當肅代時戶口之耗
十八九人主而下至六師供邊之費悉仰
給於劉晏之十五道晏好用廉勤之士先愛
民故非弘羊比也然其大旨不過在於捷
得四方之物價使食貨輕重之權使司恒
爲之掌握利在官而害不在民其所謂愛
民者又不過捷得四方之豐歉豐則糴歉
===
則糶以兩利而相濟其所謂理財者不過
寬予鹽商之賚以收鹽利厚處漕艘之費
以收漕實而已故謂晏能整齊之則可謂
晏能生之則不可執事試籌今之天下即
有如弘羊晏者在能捐百萬金而不之問
乎能聽其自辟召立富貴人乎左右不中
制而臺省不外議乎故曰得人而專聽其
法易以法而強授之人難也邇年
國用乏大司農不能當中旨數更易中外士
punctuated: 賦財法禦所稱，有一之不備者乎？弘羊而在，吏何所加？故曰：富末開利之天下易，富已開利之天下難也。當肅代時，戶口之耗十八九，人主而下至六師供邊之費，悉仰給於劉晏之十五道。晏好用廉勤之士，先愛民，故非弘羊比也。然其大旨不過在於捷得四方之物價，使食貨輕重之權，使司恒爲之掌握，利在官而害不在民。其所謂愛民者，又不過捷得四方之豐歉，豐則糴，歉則糶，以兩利而相濟。其所謂理財者，不過寬予鹽商之賚以收鹽利，厚處漕艘之費以收漕實而已。故謂晏能整齊之則可，謂晏能生之則不可。執事試籌今之天下，即有如弘羊、晏者在，能捐百萬金而不之問乎？能聽其自辟召，立富貴人乎？左右不中制而臺省不外議乎？故曰：得人而專聽其法易，以法而強授之人難也。邇年國用乏，大司農不能當，中旨數更易，中外士
translation_en:
…of the aforementioned arrangements for taxation, finance, and administration [?], is there a single one that is not already in place? Were Hongyang here serving as an official, what could he add? Thus I say: it is easy to enrich a realm whose sources of profit have not yet been opened [?]; it is difficult to enrich one whose sources of profit have already been opened.

During the reigns of Suzong and Daizong, the registered population had fallen by eight or nine tenths. Expenditure, from that of the sovereign down to provisioning the imperial armies at the frontier, depended entirely on supplies from Liu Yan’s fifteen circuits. Yan preferred to employ honest and diligent men and put care for the people first; thus he was unlike Hongyang. Yet his principal method amounted merely to obtaining prompt information about commodity prices throughout the realm and keeping control over the relative values of foodstuffs and other goods constantly in the hands of the responsible office [?], so that the government gained without harming the people. What he called caring for the people likewise amounted merely to promptly learning where harvests were abundant or poor: buying grain in plentiful years and selling it in lean ones, thereby benefiting both sides and using each to relieve the other. What he called managing finances amounted merely to allowing salt merchants generous returns in order to secure salt revenues, and generously funding grain-transport vessels in order to secure actual deliveries of grain. Thus one may say that Yan could bring finances into order, but not that he could create wealth.

Consider, sir, the realm today. Even if men like Hongyang and Yan were present, could one commit a million in gold to them without questioning their use of it? Could one allow them to recruit their own subordinates and immediately confer wealth and rank upon others? Could the sovereign’s attendants refrain from obstructing them at court, and the censorial and administrative offices refrain from criticizing them outside it? Thus I say: it is easy to obtain the right man and entrust oneself wholly to his methods; it is difficult to take a prescribed method and force it upon a man.

In recent years, funds for state expenditure have been insufficient. The Minister of Revenue has been unable to meet the need, and palace orders have repeatedly replaced him. Officials at court and in the provinces…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
大夫朝夕以用爲憂公車之犢至累月不
能竟十道之使旁午而未久輒報罷鹽政
壞而思復其舊計開中之入歲損二十萬
緡且中止矣屯政壞而思飭其舊計其羨
僅足以供本軍行之三年而復廢專官矣
欲鑄錢而計鑄之入不能當其損矣欲設
官會行鈔法而
國家不能出數十萬金以爲之母矣累世之
蓄困於
===
先朝之工禱而天府竭矣焚贖之所積困於頻
年之蠲解而郡邑倉庫竭矣水旱蟲蝗加
以無名之賦而閭閻竭矣廣盜起而所費
者歲以數十萬計而五嶺之公私貧矣河
決而所費歲以百萬計而青徐兗豫之公
私貧矣外有日重而必不可已之邊計内
有日益而必不肯已之
宗藩然則如之何曰此在
人主精思之委計於大臣而後可也邊計不可
punctuated: 大夫朝夕以用爲憂，公車之犢至累月不能竟，十道之使旁午而未久輒報罷。鹽政壞而思復其舊，計開中之入，歲損二十萬緡，且中止矣。屯政壞而思飭其舊，計其羨，僅足以供本軍，行之三年而復廢專官矣。欲鑄錢，而計鑄之入不能當其損矣。欲設官會，行鈔法，而國家不能出數十萬金以爲之母矣。累世之蓄困於先朝之工禱，而天府竭矣。焚贖之所積困於頻年之蠲解，而郡邑倉庫竭矣。水旱蟲蝗，加以無名之賦，而閭閻竭矣。廣盜起，而所費者歲以數十萬計，而五嶺之公私貧矣。河決，而所費歲以百萬計，而青徐兗豫之公私貧矣。外有日重而必不可已之邊計，内有日益而必不肯已之宗藩。然則如之何？曰：此在人主精思之，委計於大臣而後可也。邊計不可
translation_en:
…officials worry morning and evening about expenditure. Documents submitted to the throne [?] remain unresolved for months; envoys to the ten circuits come and go in rapid succession, yet before long their missions are reported discontinued. The salt administration has deteriorated, and there is a wish to restore its former arrangements. Yet receipts from the system of supplying grain in exchange for salt certificates have fallen by 200,000 strings of cash annually, and that system too has been suspended. Military agricultural administration has deteriorated, and there is a wish to put its former arrangements back in order. Yet its calculated surplus barely suffices to supply the troops stationed there; after three years of implementation, the specially appointed officials have again been abolished. There is a wish to mint coins, but the projected receipts cannot offset the losses. There is a wish to establish government-issued notes [?] and implement a paper-currency system, but the state cannot produce the several hundred thousand in silver needed as its backing.

The reserves accumulated over successive reigns were drained by construction and prayers [?] under the preceding reign, and the imperial treasury is exhausted. Funds accumulated from redemption payments [?] have been depleted by repeated annual remissions and remittances, and prefectural and county storehouses are exhausted. Floods, droughts, insect infestations, and locusts, compounded by levies without legitimate grounds, have exhausted the common people. Banditry has arisen in Guang, requiring annual expenditure reckoned in the hundreds of thousands, impoverishing both public finances and private households throughout the Wuling region. The river has breached its banks, requiring annual expenditure reckoned in the millions, impoverishing both public finances and private households in Qing, Xu, Yan, and Yu. Externally, frontier expenses grow heavier daily and cannot possibly be discontinued; internally, the imperial princely establishments multiply daily, and there is certainly no willingness to discontinue them.

What, then, is to be done? I say: only when the ruler considers this deeply and entrusts the planning to his great ministers can the matter be resolved. Since frontier expenses cannot…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
已則加重於主兵而少調客兵使兵得息
而食減
宗藩不可已則漸限其封爵而聽其從四民
之利使人自便而祿減罷不時宣索則
六宮之用簡而戶部舒停非時工役則將作
之用簡而冬官裕清內府工匠力勇之數
覈錦衣騰衛府軍之籍則冗食省而漕糧
有餘毋輕以一人言而遽興毋輕以一人
言而遽革則
===
國是定而司農得少展其技嗟夫入利之孔
開已盡矣然細而不勝其出利之孔語云
涓涓不竭將成江河況若江河之決乎哉
故其德莫大乎節儉夫節儉者
明主之所優爲而左右之所不甚喜者也
主慎於賞賜則左右見以爲寡於澤
主難於興作則左右見以爲窮於使
主精於搜覈則左右見以爲無所匿其弊故自
古中外之臣言及利計好論其可否也朝
punctuated:
已，則加重於主兵而少調客兵，使兵得息而食減。宗藩不可已，則漸限其封爵，而聽其從四民之利，使人自便而祿減。罷不時宣索，則六宮之用簡而戶部舒；停非時工役，則將作之用簡而冬官裕。清內府工匠力勇之數，覈錦衣騰衛府軍之籍，則冗食省而漕糧有餘。毋輕以一人言而遽興，毋輕以一人言而遽革，則國是定而司農得少展其技。
嗟夫！入利之孔開已盡矣，然細而不勝其出利之孔。語云：「涓涓不竭，將成江河。」況若江河之決乎哉！故其德莫大乎節儉。夫節儉者，明主之所優爲而左右之所不甚喜者也。主慎於賞賜，則左右見以爲寡於澤；主難於興作，則左右見以爲窮於使；主精於搜覈，則左右見以爲無所匿其弊。故自古中外之臣言及利計，好論其可否也，朝
translation_en:
…cannot be discontinued, then greater reliance should be placed on locally stationed troops and fewer troops transferred from elsewhere, allowing the soldiers respite and reducing expenditure on provisions. Since support for the imperial princes cannot be discontinued, gradually restrict the granting of princely titles and permit members of the imperial clan to pursue livelihoods in the four occupations, allowing them to provide for themselves and reducing expenditure on stipends. Abolish irregular palace requisitions: expenditure in the Six Palaces will diminish, easing the burden on the Ministry of Revenue. Suspend untimely construction projects: expenditure on imperial building works will diminish, leaving the Ministry of Works with ample resources. Scrutinize the numbers of artisans, laborers, and braves attached to the palace treasury, and audit the registers of the Embroidered-uniform Guard, the Teng Guard [?], and the Palace Army. Then expenditure on superfluous mouths will decline, and grain transported as tribute will be more than sufficient. Do not hastily initiate a measure merely on one person's word, nor hastily abolish one merely on one person's word. Then state policy will be settled, and the officials responsible for revenue will have some scope to exercise their abilities.
Alas! Every channel through which revenue can enter has already been opened, yet these channels are narrow and cannot match those through which resources flow out. As the saying goes, “Trickles that never cease will become rivers.” How much worse when the outflow resembles rivers bursting their banks! Thus no virtue is greater than frugality. Frugality is something an enlightened ruler can readily practice, but those around him do not much enjoy it. If the ruler is cautious in granting rewards, his attendants regard him as sparing in his favors; if he is reluctant to undertake building projects, they regard him as constrained in his use of resources; if he is thorough in investigation and scrutiny, they see that there is nowhere to conceal their abuses. Thus, from antiquity, when officials at court and in the provinces have spoken of schemes for financial gain, their feasibility has been readily discussed. In the morning…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
上而夕報可至著爲令甲有之言及國蠹
毋論其重輕也朝上而夕報罷甚且付廷
尉矣噫郎官晏諸才臣杜口可也
第五問
黄廷綬
同考試官教諭陳　批〔虜勢不必較惟我戰守相機宜是矣因與爲戰守且明賞罰之典寬文法之誅重將帥之權皆妙用也宜録之以〕
獻當宁
===
考試官教諭謝　批〔敘虜情瞭然如指掌至經畧處不爲大言而有條理蓋實究心於是者〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔談邊事痛快知兵之士也〕
中國之不能與虜敵也久矣而今爲甚其
說凡有八曰聚散之勢不敵也大約中國
勝兵與虜控弦之騎校之可各得三十餘
萬我散而爲九邊而虜長聚是以九而攻
我一也其不敵一也勇怯之實不敵也賊
便馬疾鬭耐饑渴上下馳逐若風視死若
punctuated:
上而夕報可，至著爲令甲有之。言及國蠹，毋論其重輕也，朝上而夕報罷，甚且付廷尉矣。噫！郎官晏諸，才臣杜口可也。

第五問
黄廷綬
同考試官教諭陳　批〔虜勢不必較，惟我戰守相機宜是矣。因與爲戰守，且明賞罰之典，寬文法之誅，重將帥之權，皆妙用也。宜録之以〕獻當宁。

考試官教諭謝　批〔敘虜情瞭然如指掌，至經畧處，不爲大言而有條理，蓋實究心於是者。〕
考試官教諭馬　批〔談邊事痛快，知兵之士也。〕

中國之不能與虜敵也久矣，而今爲甚。其說凡有八：曰聚散之勢不敵也。大約中國勝兵與虜控弦之騎，校之可各得三十餘萬。我散而爲九邊，而虜長聚，是以九而攻我一也，其不敵一也。勇怯之實不敵也。賊便馬疾鬭，耐饑渴，上下馳逐若風，視死若
translation_en:
…submitted in the morning and approved by evening; some proposals are even incorporated into the statutes. But when discussion touches on those who prey upon the state, regardless of the gravity of their offenses, a submission made in the morning is rejected by evening; in extreme cases its author is even handed over to the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement. Alas! The court gentleman Yan Zhu [?]—able ministers had best keep their mouths shut.

Fifth Policy Question
Huang Tingshou

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: 〔There is no need to compare the enemy’s strength with ours; what matters is that our fighting and defense suit the circumstances. Accordingly, engaging them in battle or defending against them, clarifying the rules for rewards and punishments, relaxing punishments imposed for procedural infractions, and strengthening the authority of commanders are all excellent practical measures. This deserves to be recorded for〕 presentation to His Majesty.

Comment by Examiner Xie, Instructor: 〔His account of the enemy’s circumstances is as clear as the palm of one’s hand. When he turns to strategic planning, he avoids grandiose claims and proceeds methodically. He has evidently given this matter serious thought.〕

Comment by Examiner Ma, Instructor: 〔His discussion of frontier affairs is incisive and gratifying. He is a man who understands warfare.〕

China has long been unable to match the northern enemy, and this is now worse than ever. There are eight explanations. First, we are unequal in the disposition of our forces, dispersed or concentrated. Roughly comparing China’s combat-ready troops with the enemy’s bow-bearing cavalry, each side numbers somewhat over three hundred thousand. Our forces are dispersed among the Nine Frontier Commands, whereas the enemy’s remain concentrated. Thus they bring nine against our one: this is the first inequality. We are unequal in actual courage and timidity. The enemy are adept on horseback, fight swiftly, endure hunger and thirst, and gallop up and down like the wind, regarding death as …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
赴而我於是數者無一焉其不敵二也虜
伏之形不敵也虜因糧於我我裹糧而應
之不待三日而自困其不敵三也騎步之
力不敵也我雖騎不能蹤行突鬬而爲騎
陣賊無所不衝而我無所不應其不敵四
也攻守之機不敵也賊既闌入邊抵宣大
薊晉之要衝而居之焉首東則東犯西則
西犯彼無所不攻而我無所不守其不敵
五也客主之變不敵也賊入而烽始舉烽
===
舉而兵始出賊顧爲主而我顧爲客彼得
從容設伏以誘我其不敵六也專緩之計
不敵也虜自春而至秋其上下日以入寇
爲計自辰而至夕其事非鬬即獵其所工
非騎即射而我之吏士則營營焉不憂鬬
而憂其妻子爲文武大帥者不憂外而憂
內又加以文法簿書之是牽逢迎便辟之
是熟而望其能贋懲大憝哉其不敵七也
上下之情不敵也虜自其主帥以至於鬬
punctuated: 赴，而我於是數者無一焉，其不敵二也。虜伏之形不敵也：虜因糧於我，我裹糧而應之，不待三日而自困，其不敵三也。騎步之力不敵也：我雖騎，不能蹤行突鬬而爲騎陣，賊無所不衝，而我無所不應，其不敵四也。攻守之機不敵也：賊既闌入邊，抵宣大薊晉之要衝而居之焉，首東則東犯，西則西犯，彼無所不攻，而我無所不守，其不敵五也。客主之變不敵也：賊入而烽始舉，烽舉而兵始出，賊顧爲主，而我顧爲客，彼得從容設伏以誘我，其不敵六也。專緩之計不敵也：虜自春而至秋，其上下日以入寇爲計；自辰而至夕，其事非鬬即獵，其所工非騎即射。而我之吏士則營營焉，不憂鬬而憂其妻子；爲文武大帥者，不憂外而憂內，又加以文法簿書之是牽，逢迎便辟之是熟，而望其能贋懲大憝哉？其不敵七也。上下之情不敵也：虜自其主帥以至於鬬
translation_en:
…something to rush toward [?], whereas we possess none of these qualities. This is the second respect in which we are no match for them.

We are unequal in the circumstances of the enemy’s lying in wait [?]: the enemy obtains provisions from us, while we carry provisions with us to respond to them. Before three days have passed, we have exhausted ourselves. This is the third respect in which we are no match for them.

We are unequal in the strength of cavalry and infantry. Even when mounted, our men cannot advance in pursuit and charge into combat in cavalry formation [?]. There is nowhere the enemy does not charge, and nowhere we do not have to respond. This is the fourth respect in which we are no match for them.

We are unequal in opportunities for attack and defense. Once the enemy has broken through the frontier, they reach and occupy the strategic points of Xuanfu, Datong, Jizhou, and Shanxi. If they turn east, they raid eastward; if west, they raid westward. There is nowhere they cannot attack, and nowhere we need not defend. This is the fifth respect in which we are no match for them.
