We are unequal in adapting to the roles of guest and host. Only after the enemy enters are the beacon fires raised; only after the beacons are raised do our troops march out. Thus the enemy instead becomes the host, while we become the guest. They can calmly lay ambushes to lure us in. This is the sixth respect in which we are no match for them.

We are unequal in the calculations of concentration and laxity [?]. From spring through autumn, the enemy’s superiors and subordinates alike plan daily to invade and plunder. From morning until evening, their activities are either fighting or hunting, and their skills are either riding or archery. Our officers and soldiers, however, busy themselves with their own affairs, worrying about their wives and children rather than combat. Those serving as senior civil and military commanders worry about internal affairs rather than external threats. Moreover, they are entangled in administrative rules and paperwork, and practiced in ingratiation and flattery. Can we expect them to punish the great malefactors [?]? This is the seventh respect in which we are no match for them.

We are unequal in the relations between superiors and subordinates. Among the enemy, from their commander down to the fighting…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
卒無貴賤一也其嗜欲易通而沈慼易達
也我士卒之於偏裨偏裨之於大帥武吏
之於文吏邊臣之於大臣若隔九閽焉而
何以責之效力也爲虜閒諜者本我中國
之民而以我情予虜爲我烽堠者本我中
國之兵而以我情予虜其不敵八也夫所
謂八不敵者審矣然而虜卒不能爲我害
者何也是匈奴突厥之虜而非女直蒙古
之虜也夫所謂女直蒙古之虜何也自其
===
立國之始而地半已中國矣中國之民安
虜而不相鄙也虜變中國之俗而不爲苦
也故以中國攻中國而虜得饒於戰以虜
供虜而虜得深入而久居也若夫匈奴突
厥則不然其嗜欲不合也其居處不便習
也其寇也利中國之玉帛貨賄而不必有
其地利中國之子女技作而不必有其民
匱則至贏則出月盛壯則攻戰月虧則退
兵深入則虞歸久居則虞疾中國之所以
punctuated:
卒，無貴賤，一也，其嗜欲易通，而沈慼易達也。我士卒之於偏裨，偏裨之於大帥，武吏之於文吏，邊臣之於大臣，若隔九閽焉，而何以責之效力也？爲虜閒諜者，本我中國之民，而以我情予虜；爲我烽堠者，本我中國之兵，而以我情予虜。其不敵八也。
夫所謂八不敵者審矣，然而虜卒不能爲我害者，何也？是匈奴、突厥之虜，而非女直、蒙古之虜也。夫所謂女直、蒙古之虜，何也？自其立國之始，而地半已中國矣。中國之民安虜而不相鄙也，虜變中國之俗而不爲苦也，故以中國攻中國，而虜得饒於戰；以虜供虜，而虜得深入而久居也。若夫匈奴、突厥則不然，其嗜欲不合也，其居處不便習也。其寇也，利中國之玉帛貨賄，而不必有其地；利中國之子女技作，而不必有其民。匱則至，贏則出；月盛壯則攻戰，月虧則退兵。深入則虞歸，久居則虞疾，中國之所以
translation_en:
…soldiers, high and low alike are as one: their desires are readily communicated, and their deepest sorrows readily made known. Yet between our soldiers and their subordinate commanders, between subordinate commanders and commanders-in-chief, between military and civil officials, and between frontier officials and high ministers, there seem to stand nine palace gates. How, then, can we demand that they exert themselves in service? Those who act as spies for the enemy are originally people of our own China, yet they give the enemy information about us. Those who man our beacon posts are originally soldiers of our own China, yet they too give the enemy information about us. This is the eighth respect in which we are no match for them.
These eight disadvantages are clear. Yet why is it that the enemy ultimately cannot bring about our ruin? Because these are enemies of the Xiongnu and Tujue kind, rather than of the Nüzhi (Jurchen) and Menggu (Mongol) kind. What do I mean by enemies of the Jurchen and Mongol kind? From the very founding of their states, half their territory already lay within China. The Chinese people were content under their rule, and the two did not despise one another. The invaders adopted Chinese customs without finding this burdensome. Thus they used China to attack China, gaining ample resources for warfare; they used their own conquered domains to supply their forces, enabling them to penetrate deeply and remain for a long time. The Xiongnu and Tujue, however, were different. Their tastes and desires did not accord with those of China, nor were they accustomed to its dwellings and ways of living. In their raids, they sought profit from China’s jade, silk, goods, and wealth, without necessarily seeking possession of its land; they sought profit from China’s sons and daughters and skilled workmanship, without necessarily seeking possession of its population. When short of supplies they came; when amply supplied they departed. When the moon waxed full, they attacked and fought; when it waned, they withdrew their troops. If they penetrated deeply, they worried about returning; if they remained long, they feared illness. This was why China…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
獲支梧而稍息肩也夫不求我之所以勝
漢唐者而幸虜之尚爲匈奴突厥愚以爲
中國之計左也夫薦紳守和親而介冑言
征伐自古則然今之薦紳之士不習虜者則
口虜亦人耳此其衆不過當漢一大郡戰
不勝則誅卻守不固則誅守臣吾法行而
前因無衡虜介冑之士習虜者曰不然虜
鬭士勇三倍我其馬力十倍我試卽邊兵
人校之其見虜而不股粟者十不一也其
===
能角虜而互見其技者百不一也夫士畏
敵而不畏將將甘死法而不死敵何以言
戰哉愚以爲皆非也愚非能抶穰苴臏起
之秘起衛霍於九京而與之筴也不過諸
邊大夫之所恒知者其略曰審形勢明賞
罰定國是重將權而已夫所謂審形勢者
不敢遠及秦諸邊也姑請言其近者宣大
之險與虜共矣其法當以戰而爲守山西
薊邊險猶在我也其法當以守而爲戰以
punctuated: 獲支梧而稍息肩也。夫不求我之所以勝漢唐者，而幸虜之尚爲匈奴突厥，愚以爲中國之計左也。夫薦紳守和親，而介冑言征伐，自古則然。今之薦紳之士不習虜者，則口虜亦人耳，此其衆不過當漢一大郡。戰不勝則誅卻，守不固則誅守臣，吾法行而前因無衡虜。介冑之士習虜者曰：「不然，虜鬭士勇三倍我，其馬力十倍我。試卽邊兵人校之，其見虜而不股粟者，十不一也；其能角虜而互見其技者，百不一也。夫士畏敵而不畏將，將甘死法而不死敵，何以言戰哉？」愚以爲皆非也。愚非能抶穰苴臏起之秘，起衛霍於九京而與之筴也，不過諸邊大夫之所恒知者。其略曰：審形勢，明賞罰，定國是，重將權而已。夫所謂審形勢者，不敢遠及秦諸邊也，姑請言其近者。宣大之險與虜共矣，其法當以戰而爲守；山西薊邊險猶在我也，其法當以守而爲戰。以
translation_en:
…has been able to hold out and find some relief from its burdens. Rather than seeking the means by which we might surpass the Han and Tang, we count ourselves fortunate that the northern foes are still like the Xiongnu and Tujue. In my humble opinion, this is a misguided strategy for China. Civil officials advocate peace through marriage alliances, while men in armor speak of punitive campaigns: this has been so since antiquity. Today, civil officials unfamiliar with the enemy say [?]: “The enemy are only human. Their numbers amount to no more than those of one large Han commandery. If a battle is not won, execute those who retreat [?]; if a position is not securely defended, execute the official defending it. Once our laws are enforced, the enemy will find no match before them [?].”

Military men familiar with the enemy say: “Not so. Their fighting men are three times as brave as ours, and their horses ten times as strong. Try comparing the frontier soldiers man by man: not one in ten can face the enemy without his thighs trembling; not one in a hundred can contend with them and display his skills in an exchange. When soldiers fear the enemy but do not fear their commanders, and commanders would willingly die under the law rather than die facing the enemy, how can we speak of battle?”

In my humble opinion, both views are wrong. I cannot wield [?] the secret arts of Rangju, Sun Bin, and Wu Qi, nor raise Wei Qing and Huo Qubing from their graves to deliberate with them. What I propose is merely what the officials of the various frontier regions have always known. In outline, it amounts to this: assess the strategic configuration of the terrain, make rewards and punishments clear, settle national policy, and strengthen commanders’ authority.

As for assessing the strategic configuration of the terrain, I dare not range as far as the various frontier regions of Qin; let me speak for now of those nearer at hand. The strategic terrain of Xuanfu and Datong is shared with the enemy, so the proper method there is to use fighting as a means of defense. Along the Shanxi and Ji frontiers, the strategic terrain remains in our hands, so the proper method there is to use defense as a means of fighting. To use…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
戰爲守者非必戰也我棄小堡而併於大
堡堡宿銳士栖餱糧擇帥以統之使不可
下而簡募精騎如所謂百保鮮卑者分屬
諸驍將以爲奇兵或擊其抄卒使不敢散
而輕我或襲其輜重使不敢易而近我然
後多間諜以離其黨廣招誘以弱其勢十
年之内虜庶幾且遠乎以守爲戰者非必
守也虜不入則堅墉浚濠宿兵以待之虜
入矣清野以疲其騎清野矣堅壁以防其
===
攻壁堅矣設疑而誤其路路疑矣嚴兵而
尾其歸此所謂守道也不然而責宣大以
守是坐困也責山西薊邊以戰是立敗也
所謂明賞罰者其說非徒謂峻罰也賞固
當先之夫古將兵而峻於罰者莫過楊素
將將而峻於罰者莫過漢武帝然而樂爲
素兵者樂微功之見知樂爲漢武帝將者
樂萬戶侯千金之易致也故酷罰者人之
所欲避也而賞能奪之戰危者人之所易
punctuated:
戰爲守者，非必戰也。我棄小堡而併於大堡，堡宿銳士，栖餱糧，擇帥以統之，使不可下，而簡募精騎，如所謂百保鮮卑者，分屬諸驍將，以爲奇兵。或擊其抄卒，使不敢散而輕我；或襲其輜重，使不敢易而近我。然後多間諜以離其黨，廣招誘以弱其勢。十年之内，虜庶幾且遠乎！以守爲戰者，非必守也。虜不入，則堅墉浚濠，宿兵以待之；虜入矣，清野以疲其騎；清野矣，堅壁以防其攻；壁堅矣，設疑而誤其路；路疑矣，嚴兵而尾其歸。此所謂守道也。不然而責宣大以守，是坐困也；責山西薊邊以戰，是立敗也。
所謂明賞罰者，其說非徒謂峻罰也，賞固當先之。夫古將兵而峻於罰者，莫過楊素；將將而峻於罰者，莫過漢武帝。然而樂爲素兵者，樂微功之見知；樂爲漢武帝將者，樂萬戶侯千金之易致也。故酷罰者，人之所欲避也，而賞能奪之；戰危者，人之所易
translation_en:
…using battle as defense does not necessarily mean fighting. We should abandon the small forts and consolidate their forces in the large ones. In each fort, station elite soldiers and store provisions; choose a commander to lead them and make the fort impregnable. Select and recruit picked cavalry, like the so-called Hundred-Guard Xianbei troops, and assign them among the valiant commanders as forces for surprise operations. Sometimes strike the enemy’s raiding parties, so that they dare not disperse and hold us in contempt; sometimes attack their baggage trains, so that they dare not approach us heedlessly. Then employ numerous spies to divide their adherents, and extend inducements widely to draw them over and weaken their strength. Within ten years, might the enemy not have withdrawn far away? Using defense as battle does not necessarily mean merely holding a position. If the enemy does not enter, strengthen the walls, deepen the moats, and station troops to await them. Once they enter, clear the countryside to wear out their cavalry. Once the countryside is cleared, strengthen the fortifications against their attacks. Once the fortifications are secure, employ deception to lead them astray. Once they are uncertain of their route, ready the troops and follow close behind their retreat. This is what is called the method of defense. Otherwise, demanding that Xuanfu and Datong defend themselves means sitting still until they are exhausted; demanding that Shanxi and the Ji frontier fight means immediate defeat.
As for making rewards and punishments clear, this does not simply mean imposing severe punishments: rewards should certainly come first. Among ancient commanders of troops, none was harsher in punishment than Yang Su; among rulers who commanded generals, none was harsher than Emperor Wu of Han. Yet those who gladly served as Yang Su’s soldiers did so because even small achievements were recognized; those who gladly served as Emperor Wu’s generals did so because a marquisate of ten thousand households and a thousand pieces of gold were readily attainable. Thus, cruel punishment is something people wish to avoid, but rewards can overcome that aversion; the dangers of battle are something people readily …

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
曉也而賞能愚之今
國家於失律之法嚴矣獨所謂賞者極於數
十金而所謂爵者不及世欲以此而售人
之死命何也愚以爲
人主精意於此如趙藝祖之別貯帛封樁庫購
虜首而又不愛通侯世爵之賞以待天下
之負材而自喜者蓋朝奏功而夕報
璽書毋使墨吏持文法譏訶之而後嚴繆巿之
令使天下有所甚欲者以易其生而有所
===
甚惡者以易其死其不悉讙力而致之於
敵也幾希所謂定國是者縣官下求材之
令人得舉所知銓部次第而用之矣其未
用也人人皆諸葛亮而其旣用也處處皆
李元平固所用之才未盡眞而所以待之
之道未盡是也不見形而有所爲則議者
得以其形而訾之稍破格而有所請則議
者得以其格而繩之愚以爲今用人自督
撫而下宜精簡其選旣用之後則精專其
punctuated:
曉也，而賞能愚之。今國家於失律之法嚴矣，獨所謂賞者極於數十金，而所謂爵者不及世，欲以此而售人之死命，何也？愚以爲，人主精意於此，如趙藝祖之別貯帛封樁庫購虜首，而又不愛通侯世爵之賞，以待天下之負材而自喜者。蓋朝奏功，而夕報璽書，毋使墨吏持文法譏訶之，而後嚴繆巿之令，使天下有所甚欲者以易其生，而有所甚惡者以易其死，其不悉讙力而致之於敵也幾希。
所謂定國是者，縣官下求材之令，人得舉所知，銓部次第而用之矣。其未用也，人人皆諸葛亮；而其旣用也，處處皆李元平。固所用之才未盡眞，而所以待之之道未盡是也。不見形而有所爲，則議者得以其形而訾之；稍破格而有所請，則議者得以其格而繩之。愚以爲，今用人，自督撫而下，宜精簡其選；旣用之後，則精專其
translation_en:
…is readily understood, yet rewards can make men disregard it. Today the state’s laws against breaches of military discipline are severe. Yet its so-called rewards amount at most to a few tens of taels of silver, and its so-called titles do not pass to heirs. How can it expect to purchase men’s lives with these? In my humble opinion, the ruler should devote earnest attention to this, as Zhao, the Founding Ancestor of the Song, separately stored silk in the Fengzhuang Treasury to purchase enemy heads. Nor should he begrudge rewards of marquisates and hereditary titles to attract men throughout the realm who possess ability and take pride in it. Let an achievement reported in the morning receive an imperial letter under seal that very evening. Do not allow corrupt officials to invoke legal formalities to criticize and obstruct it. Then rigorously enforce the orders of “Miu Market” [?]. Give men throughout the realm something they desire so greatly that they will exchange their lives for it, and something they detest so greatly that they will accept death instead. Few indeed would then fail to exert their full strength gladly [?] against the enemy.
As for what is meant by settling national policy: the court issues orders seeking talented men, people may recommend those they know, and the Ministry of Personnel appoints them in succession. Before appointment, every man is a Zhuge Liang; after appointment, everywhere there is a Li Yuanping. Certainly, the abilities of those appointed are not all genuine; but neither are the ways in which they are treated entirely right. If they undertake something before its results become manifest, critics can seize upon its outward appearance to disparage them. If they make a request that departs even slightly from established rules, critics can invoke those rules to constrain them. In my humble opinion, appointments today, from supreme commanders and grand coordinators downward, should be made through careful and discriminating selection. Once men have been appointed, their responsibilities should be clearly and exclusively entrusted to them…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
任而務將其成一切建白指摘〔凡議頗言〕
閫不令下可也所謂重將權者令督師之
委非不重也然陽示之重而陰迫之輕爲
之下者自一命而上即有與主咈息嚬笑
皆懼觸怒然猶平居言耳賊一入而督師
不能行之大將大將不能行之偏裨蓋有
令下而嘻出而稍相目曰此廷尉人耳非
而主也故愚所謂重者居平不爲之中制
賊至則聽其誅賞賊退務覈其情實而已
凡愚所以對執事者疏節闊目不能爲必
勝之策也異日倘捐前箸而借我尚當以
根本之說進
punctuated:
任，而務將其成。一切建白指摘〔凡議頗言〕，閫不令下可也。所謂重將權者，令督師之委非不重也，然陽示之重，而陰迫之輕。爲之下者，自一命而上，即有與主咈息嚬笑，皆懼觸怒，然猶平居言耳。賊一入，而督師不能行之大將，大將不能行之偏裨。蓋有令下而嘻，出而稍相目曰：「此廷尉人耳，非而主也。」故愚所謂重者，居平不爲之中制，賊至則聽其誅賞，賊退務覈其情實而已。
凡愚所以對執事者，疏節闊目，不能爲必勝之策也。異日倘捐前箸而借我，尚當以根本之說進。
translation_en:
…their responsibilities, and concentrate on bringing their work to fruition. As for all proposals and criticisms 〔all discussions and adverse remarks [?]〕, it would suffice to prevent them from being transmitted down to the military command [?]. As for what I call strengthening the commanding general’s authority, the charge entrusted to the commander overseeing the armies is certainly weighty [?]. Yet outwardly it is represented as weighty, while covert pressures diminish it. His subordinates, from the lowest appointed rank upward, fear provoking his anger in their dealings with their superior, even in breathing, frowning, or smiling [?]; but this describes only ordinary times. Once the enemy invades, the commander overseeing the armies cannot enforce his orders upon the senior generals, nor can the senior generals enforce theirs upon subordinate commanders. Indeed, some laugh when an order is issued and, on leaving, exchange glances and say: “This is merely a man of the Chamberlain for Law Enforcement [?], not your master.” Thus, by strengthening his authority, I mean that in ordinary times the court should not constrain him from within; when the enemy comes, he should be allowed to execute and reward; and when the enemy withdraws, every effort should be made to investigate the actual circumstances—that is all.
All that I, in my ignorance, have offered in reply to you is a loose outline of broad points; it cannot constitute a plan guaranteeing victory. If on some future day you should set aside the chopsticks before you and lend them to me to lay out my counsel, I would further submit an account of the fundamental principles.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
山西鄉試錄後序
隆慶之四年庚午試錄成而
〔良仕〕以職事序於後曰傳有
之庚位西方象秋時萬物庚
庚有實也午於日爲正中於
數五陰陽在天地間交午也
昔人謂堯舜禹之生寔在午
===
當天下文明之會故一時賢
聖出而交輔之天不愛道圖
書顯矣蓋五臣之職脩而萬
世之彛政禮樂秩如也今歲
在庚午晉以西庚分也物庚
庚有實矣更西而蒲坂平陽
安邑堯舜禹所都也稍西南
punctuated:
山西鄉試錄後序

隆慶之四年庚午，試錄成，而〔良仕〕以職事序於後曰：傳有之：「庚位西方，象秋時，萬物庚庚有實也。午於日爲正中，於數五，陰陽在天地間交午也。」昔人謂堯舜禹之生，寔在午，當天下文明之會，故一時賢聖出而交輔之。天不愛道，圖書顯矣。蓋五臣之職脩，而萬世之彛政禮樂秩如也。今歲在庚午，晉以西，庚分也，物庚庚有實矣。更西而蒲坂、平陽、安邑，堯舜禹所都也。稍西南
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shanxi Provincial Examination

In the fourth year of Longqing, the gengwu year (1570), the examination record was completed, and 〔Liangshi〕, in fulfillment of his official duties, appended this postface, saying: Tradition has it: “Geng occupies the west and represents the season of autumn, when the myriad things mature and bear fruit. Wu corresponds to the exact midpoint of the day and to the number five; it is where yin and yang intersect between Heaven and Earth.” People of old said that Yao, Shun, and Yu were born precisely in a wu period, at a convergence of cultural brilliance throughout the world. Thus worthy men and sages appeared together in that age and assisted them. Heaven did not withhold the Way: the River Chart and the Luo Writing were revealed. The five ministers duly performed their duties, and the enduring institutions, rites, and music for all ages stood in orderly array. This year is gengwu. Jin, being in the west, belongs to the domain of geng, and its myriad things have matured and borne fruit. Farther west are Puban, Pingyang, and Anyi, where Yao, Shun, and Yu established their capitals. A little farther southwest…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
而水滙之滎河溫洛也圖書
所由顯矣
天子乘午運沛然欲章明其治思
與天下之賢士大夫共之
詔郡邑各益其貢士之一齒太學
已釆國子祭酒言益兩都解
額各十五海內談經游藝之
===
士䇿不欲濯剔其肺腑自顯
見其長以答
主鼓舞至意又況山西爲堯舜
禹所故都獨當文明之會者
哉不佞謭且陋不足與於斯
文竊念以一校官應御史聘
而來獲縱觀山河表裏之盛
punctuated: 而水滙之，滎河溫洛也，圖書所由顯矣。天子乘午運，沛然欲章明其治，思與天下之賢士大夫共之。詔郡邑各益其貢士之一，齒太學；已釆國子祭酒言，益兩都解額各十五。海內談經游藝之士，䇿不欲濯剔其肺腑，自顯見其長，以答主鼓舞至意？又況山西爲堯舜禹所故都，獨當文明之會者哉！不佞謭且陋，不足與於斯文。竊念以一校官應御史聘而來，獲縱觀山河表裏之盛。
translation_en:
…and the waters converge there, at Xinghe and Wenluo [?], where the River Chart and the Luo Writing appeared. Riding the cyclical fortune of the wu year, the Son of Heaven ardently wishes to make his governance illustrious and considers sharing this undertaking with the worthy scholars and officials of the realm. He has decreed that each prefecture and county increase by one the number of its tribute students admitted to the Imperial University. He has already adopted the proposal of the Chancellor of the Directorate of Education to increase the Provincial Examination quotas of the two capitals by fifteen each. Among the scholars throughout the realm who discuss the classics and cultivate the arts, who would not wish [?] to cleanse their innermost hearts and display their strengths, responding to their sovereign’s earnest intention to encourage them? How much more must this be true of Shanxi, the site of the former capitals of Yao, Shun, and Yu, uniquely situated at this convergence of cultural brilliance!

I am shallow and uncultivated, unworthy to participate in this literary undertaking. Yet I reflect that, having come as a mere school official in response to a censor’s invitation, I have been able to survey the magnificent land, with mountains within and the river without…

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
與嚮所稱帝王之跡既不勝
其嘉樂稍間入棘復獲觀百
執事兢業飭比所以仰塞
上德意者至隆且備則又爕然而
興不戚寢懼無以稱也稍間
乃獲觀諸儒生之業咸彬彬
裁文質不悖於道其陳古諠
===
決策利害懇晰中窾則又快
然踴躍自勞慰不知其儤也
夫訓經而發其旨之謂義辨
志而當於理之謂論標情而
達於上之謂表決法而傳於
經之謂判陳見而宜於用之
謂策此五者不失一焉比於
punctuated:
與嚮所稱帝王之跡，既不勝其嘉樂。稍間入棘，復獲觀百執事兢業飭比，所以仰塞上德意者，至隆且備，則又爕然而興，不戚寢懼無以稱也。稍間，乃獲觀諸儒生之業，咸彬彬裁文質，不悖於道。其陳古諠，決策利害，懇晰中窾，則又快然踴躍，自勞慰，不知其儤也。

translation_en:
…and the traces of the emperors and kings mentioned earlier, I was already overcome with delight. A little later, I entered the examination compound and could also observe the many officials conscientiously attending to their duties, maintaining discipline and working together. Their efforts to fulfill His Majesty’s gracious intentions were most earnest and comprehensive. I was once again moved to harmonious enthusiasm [?], yet feared that I could not prove equal to the task [?]. A little later, I was able to examine the work of the Confucian students. All finely balanced literary refinement and substance without departing from the Way. In setting forth ancient teachings [?] and determining the benefits and harms of policy choices, they were earnest and lucid, striking at the essential points. Once again I rejoiced and leapt with delight, finding consolation for my labors and becoming oblivious to the strain of continuous duty.
To expound the classics and bring out their purport is called an exposition; to distinguish intentions and accord with principle is called a discourse; to express one’s sentiments and convey them to the sovereign is called a memorial; to decide according to law and transmit this through the classics [?] is called a legal judgment; to present one’s views in a manner suited to practical application is called a policy essay. title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
物正所謂庚庚有實者令舍
此而徵聲耦飾釆澤闘工曅
精於棘猴之末而謂之文卽
南戒之南有之吾無所取爾
也夫耳觀者不唯其實而泥
於山川之險塞則意其深思
而儉陋讀柳先生之問所稱
===
大鹵之金屋産之秉北山之
材猗氏之鹽則意其秀不鍾
於人而鍾於物觀薊門而北
士馬之雄盛則意其人多將
此皆非熟於晉掌故者霍宣
成狄梁公之洛日司馬文正
之補天裴晉公文潞公之爲
punctuated: 物，正所謂庚庚有實者。令舍此而徵聲耦，飾釆澤，闘工曅，精於棘猴之末，而謂之文，卽南戒之南有之，吾無所取爾也。夫耳觀者，不唯其實，而泥於山川之險塞，則意其深思而儉陋；讀柳先生之問，所稱大鹵之金、屋産之秉、北山之材、猗氏之鹽，則意其秀不鍾於人而鍾於物；觀薊門而北士馬之雄盛，則意其人多將。此皆非熟於晉掌故者。霍宣成、狄梁公之洛日，司馬文正之補天，裴晉公、文潞公之爲
translation_en:
…things: these are precisely what may be called lustrous and substantial. If [?] one abandons this to pursue paired sounds, embellish colorful surfaces, and compete in dazzling craftsmanship, lavishing ingenuity on minutiae like a monkey carved on a thorn-tip, and calls this literary writing, then even if such writing exists south of the southern boundary, I find nothing in it worth adopting.
Those who judge by hearsay fail to attend to the reality. Fixating on the rugged barriers of mountains and rivers, they suppose that the people here are deeply thoughtful but plain and uncultivated. Reading Master Liu’s “Questions,” with its references to the metal of Dalu, the “bundles of Wuchan” [?], the timber of Beishan, and the salt of Yishi, they suppose that the region’s finest energies gather in things rather than in people. Seeing the formidable strength of the troops and horses north of Jimen, they suppose that its people mostly become military commanders. None of these observers is familiar with the historical traditions of Jin.

title: 隆慶四年山西鄉試錄
text:
國柱石不亦虎炳相業哉太
史公之於史也柳先生之於
辭也河汾仲淹之於訓述也
固其造人人殊要之可以言
文矣雖然不佞竊有進於此
諸士子其益深唯堯舜禹之
傳而稷契諸大臣之所見聞
===
而知者乎其務精一乃心而
求太上所立布而功颺而言
庶幾焉
天子賛文明之治則豈唯晉重不
佞亦與有光焉
河南彰德府湯陰縣儒學教
諭謝〔良〕〔任〕謹序
punctuated:
國柱石，不亦虎炳相業哉！太史公之於史也，柳先生之於辭也，河汾仲淹之於訓述也，固其造人人殊，要之可以言文矣。雖然，不佞竊有進於此：諸士子其益深唯堯舜禹之傳，而稷契諸大臣之所見聞而知者乎？其務精一乃心，而求太上所立，布而功，颺而言，庶幾焉！天子賛文明之治，則豈唯晉重，不佞亦與有光焉。
河南彰德府湯陰縣儒學教諭謝〔良〕〔任〕謹序。
translation_en:
…pillars of the state—were these not ministerial achievements as resplendent as a tiger’s markings? The Grand Historian’s work in history, Master Liu’s work in literary expression, and Zhongyan of the He–Fen region’s work in instruction and exposition differed, to be sure, in their attainments from person to person [?]; yet all may be spoken of as manifestations of cultural accomplishment. Nevertheless, I venture to propose something beyond this: should you candidates not ponder still more deeply the transmission from Yao, Shun, and Yu, and what the great ministers Ji, Xie, and others understood through seeing and hearing? Strive to make your hearts refined and single-minded, and seek what the highest exemplars established; spread abroad your achievements and raise your voices. Then perhaps you may help the Son of Heaven advance a government of civilized flourishing [?]. Would this bring distinction only to Jin? I too would share in its reflected glory.
Respectfully prefaced by Xie Liangren 謝良任, Instructor of the Confucian School of Tangyin County, Zhangde Prefecture, Henan.
